articleTitle: An Efficient Petri Net Dynamics-Based Controllability of FMS Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The novel algorithm presented highly efficient Petri Nets (PNs) dynamics-based controllability flexible manufacturing systems (FMSs) that use PNs with optimal control transitions (CTs). The effectiveness of the CT detection process guarantees that dead markings satisfy implicit resource requirements, prompting CT to reconfigure the FMS. The PN is an appropriate model that benefits the approach from the specification, verification, and implementation in FMS. Deadlock detection and analysis often use the most effective Reachability Graph (RG). For this reason, this paper proposes a novel recovery policy based on CT to recover all of the system's states. Making systems as maximally permissive as possible is extremely difficult, even if their policies can fix the deadlock problem in FMSs. The proposed technology is demonstrated with examples, particularly for classical S3PR Petri nets. Experimental data confirm that the algorithm established with PNs, particularly as specified by CTs, can provide optimal solutions for the dynamic model of various types of FMS.

articleTitle: An Optimal Transition Efficiency Maximally Permissive Liveness of FMSs Modeled With S4PR Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: A novel approach is presented to design maximally permissive liveness implementation successfully in the highly efficient Petri Nets (PNs) controller for flexible manufacturing systems. The algorithm stabilizes design control transitions (CTs), which are solutions considered to make PNs able to quickly and automatically prevent all deadlocks with guaranteed live PN. In general, we focus our approach on class PN, namely a system of sequential systems with shared resources (S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>PR) that can model intricate FMSs where carrying out a task might call for several different kinds of resources as well as several units of a particular resource. The ability of PN to fully executable a Reachability Graph (RG) in terms of producing efficient procedures for the preservation of all FMS resource activity is under the influence of CTs. In particular, we aim to guarantee that promoting liveness in PN verification will achieve the maximally permissive supervisor RG in an optimal PN manner. Three examples show that PNs with modeled FMS are significantly more efficient and require simulation and control FMS.

articleTitle: Hybrid Fake News Detection Model: Bagging and Logistic Regression Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In Today’s world or from Past Scenario’s Fake News has a Huge Impact on Everyone’s Lives including Politics, Sports, Education, External Foreign Affairs, Defense, etc. This project aims to develop a model for identifying and detecting fake news. In this model, we implement an ensemble method that leverages the TF IDF vectorization technique to extract meaningful textual features and employ a Bagging Classifier with Logistic Regression as the base estimator to enhance classification accuracy. To build this classifier, we utilized the scikit learn library. Our work was implemented using Jupyter Notebook, an online platform. For feature extraction, we employed a well-known vectorizer called Term Frequency Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF). We split our data into training sets (75%) and test sets (25%). The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 99.15% on the test dataset, with a precision of 99.45%, a recall of 99%, and an F1-score of 99.17%. It outperforms standalone Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting classifiers.

articleTitle: AI Integrated Recommender System for Improving e-commerce Experience
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With a broad range of applications for users, recommender systems (RSs), which are made to provide individualized content, have become a crucial technological answer. Despite the fact that numerous RSs have been created and successfully used in various domains, traditional AI-driven RSs continue to encounter difficulties such as data sparsity, cold start problems, and diversity maintenance. By combining artificial intelligence (AI) and human intelligence (HI), augmented intelligence (AuI) makes up for their shortcomings while maximizing their individual strengths. It has been demonstrated that combining artificial intelligence (AI) and human intelligence (HI) improves each technology's capabilities and produces better results than utilizing each technology alone. Recommender systems, which provide predictions for a variety of goods to help consumers with personalized suggestions, have grown in popularity and usefulness. These systems guarantee that they provide users with useful and efficient help by concentrating on particular item categories and utilizing strategies intended to produce tailored recommendations. Particularly during the COVID-19 lockdown, online material streaming has become the most popular kind of entertainment in recent years. Prominent streaming services use a variety of product recommendation techniques to draw customers in and make content recommendations that suit their tastes, which increases user retention. Several recommendation systems are used by well-known streaming services like Netflix, Amazon Prime, and Hulu to improve user experience. However, serious problems including the first-rater dilemma, data sparsity, and computing complexity frequently cause these systems to struggle with accuracy and consistency. In information science, security issues have emerged as a crucial subject of user discourse. E-commerce is becoming increasingly popular as a fundamental part of the Information Science framework. Ironically, though, people are growing more cautious as security and privacy risks increase. Notably, the banking sector has entered a new era as a result of e-commerce, which has changed its services and operations.

articleTitle: Advanced Screening in Oil Recovery Processes using Attention Mechanisms Combined with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Detecting oil spill is essential for monitoring the environment and disaster management thus, helps to minimize ecological damage. Traditional methods, such as satellite imagery analysis and radar sensing, often struggle with low spatial resolution, weather interference, and not suitable for distinguishing oil from similar substances. These issues lead to inaccurate detection and delayed response time. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes an integrated topology combining attention mechanisms with Deep Convolutional Neural networks (DCNN) for Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) screening. The raw data is preprocessed by Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), scaling and normalization approaches. The preprocessed data is visualized graphically to identify the patterns or features underlying in the complex dataset. A Deep Learning (DL) based classification model is integrated with attention mechanism that effectively detects and classifies the EOR chemicals by analyzing its features. The proposed model is implemented in the Python software and it achieves the accuracy of 98% allowing more precise screening for ROR.

articleTitle: Path Loss Models Analysis for Tetra hertz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This study conducts an in-depth analysis of path loss models tailored for terahertz (THz) frequency applications, focusing on the Free Space, Okumura, and Hata-231 models. THz frequencies, characterized by their short wavelengths and broad bandwidth, are vital for advancing next-generation wireless communication systems. However, they are particularly susceptible to path loss challenges. The research evaluates modulation techniques including BPSK, QPSK, and 16-QAM to investigate how they affect important parameters like channel capacity, bit error rate (BER), and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), across various conditions. Key findings illustrate the influence of factors like distance, frequency, and antenna configurations on these metrics, emphasizing the trade-offs involved in optimizing THz communication networks. Furthermore, the study delves into atmospheric effects like absorption and scattering, offering valuable insights for designing resilient THz communication infrastructures.

articleTitle: Optimized Power Quality Monitoring in Electrical Systems Using Adaptive Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The reliable and efficient delivery of electrical power is crucial in modern societies, where a wide range of industries, infrastructure, and everyday life depend on a stable and high-quality power supply. However, the increasing complexity and integration of electrical systems, coupled with the growing use of power electronics and non-linear loads, have led to the emergence of various power quality disturbances that have significant impacts on the performance and lifespan of electrical equipment. To overcome these issues this proposes a leveraging adaptive RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) for enhanced detection of power quality disturbances in electrical systems. The methodology begins with comprehensive data collection from various power system sources to capture a wide range of disturbance patterns. Preprocessing techniques, including data cleaning and remove null values, are applied to enhance data quality and ensure accurate feature extraction. Data analysis and exploration then provide insight into underlying trends and characteristics within the dataset, facilitating the selection of relevant features. These features are then split into training and test datasets to build a robust predictive model. An adaptive RNN model is utilized to detect and classify disturbances, leveraging its ability to handle sequential data efficiently. The model’s performance is assessed through python, followed by accuracy of 91% and F1 Score of 0.89 evaluation to validate its reliability. This approach ensures an effective and adaptive solution for real-time PQDS monitoring, thereby enhancing the resilience and reliability of power systems in dynamic operating environments.

articleTitle: SARSA-Based Voltage Regulation of PV-Buck Converter System Under Multi-Nature Load Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: DC microgrids are experiencing rapid evolution due to increasing renewable energy integration and diverse load requirements, necessitating advanced control strategies for stable operation. This paper presents a novel voltage regulation approach utilizing policy gradient reinforcement learning with SARSA algorithm for a PV-fed buck converter system. The proposed methodology addresses the complex dynamics of multiple load types through a hierarchical control framework that combines actor-critic networks for continuous control actions. The control strategy employs a comprehensive seven-parameter state space encompassing voltage error, current measurement, solar irradiance, duty cycle history, voltage dynamics, error integration, and average voltage deviation. The experimental validation employs a buck converter maintaining 48V DC output from a 100V PV source, tested under challenging scenarios including 100W constant power load, 50W pulsed power load, and variable linear load conditions. The results demonstrate significant advantages over traditional PI control: 83% reduction in steady-state error, 75% improvement in voltage stability, and 73% faster load transition response. The controller successfully maintains voltage variations within +-1V across diverse load combinations, effectively addressing the destabilizing effects of constant power loads and sudden pulsed load changes. The integration of policy-based learning with on-policy SARSA implementation enables real-time adaptation without prior system modeling requirements. This approach showcases exceptional performance in both steady-state maintenance and transient response, particularly in scenarios involving mixed load characteristics. The framework provides a robust solution for modern DC microgrid applications requiring stable voltage regulation under complex load dynamics.

articleTitle: Recommender Systems for Sector-Specific Stock Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Recommender systems are essential tools that assist users in making informed decisions by providing suggestions based on their previous actions and preferences. Traditional methods like content based and collaborative filtering work well for smaller datasets but often fail to extract information from large datasets due to their limited ability to capture complex patterns. This paper introduces a novel approach for stock recommendation that leverages a large language model, Llama 3.1, fine-tuned on financial news data. Financial news headlines and summaries were collected using the FinnHub API which served as the primary dataset. The system integrates stock price forecasting, sentiment analysis, and performance indicators to generate an effective analysis for decision making. The forecasting algorithm generates the stock price predictions which were integrated with sentiment analysis and stock performance indicators to create an informative prompt-response dataset for fine-tuning. The proposed system ranks stocks based on positive developments, potential concerns, and forecasted closing prices, providing Buy or Sell recommendations. Experimental results demonstrated moderate performance for predicting Buy recommendations, while Sell predictions exhibited lower accuracy comparatively. Analysis based on sectors revealed that the consumer cyclical and healthcare sectors yielded the best performance for Buy and Sell recommendations, respectively.

articleTitle: Intelligent Defenses: Advancing Cybersecurity through Machine Learning-Driven Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The exponential rise in cyberthreats has rendered malware detection a crucial component of cybersecurity. Traditional signature-based detection technologies are insufficient for combating emerging threat vectors, as increasingly complex malware targets sensitive systems. Machine learning techniques have emerged as a viable alternative for the precise detection and classification of malware through data-driven insights. This study presents a comprehensive malware detection system that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with sophisticated machine learning (ML) methodologies, including ensemble techniques like Random Forest and Gradient Boosted Decision Trees. To rectify class imbalance and enhance model performance, the framework utilizes extensive preprocessing methods, including SMOTE. The Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy of 97.4%, followed by Gradient Boosted Decision Trees at 96.7%; the CNN demonstrated competitive performance at 95.0%. Dynamic API call sequences were identified as essential elements for precise classification. The proposed technique significantly reduces false negatives, hence ensuring improved protection against malicious software and enhancing recall. This research provides a scalable framework for future malware detection systems and demonstrates how machine learning may enhance cybersecurity protocols.

articleTitle: An Ensemble-Based Framework for Enhanced Missing Data Imputation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Missing data is a pervasive issue in many real-world datasets, often leading to biased estimates, reduced statistical power, and invalid conclusions if not properly addressed. Traditional imputation methods, such as mean, median, and K-nearest neighbors (KNN), each have their advantages but often fail to provide consistently accurate estimates across different datasets and missing data patterns. Advanced methods, including IterativeImputer and matrix factorization-based SoftImpute, offer improvements but still face limitations. In this paper, we propose a novel ensemble-based imputation method that synergistically combines the strengths of KNN, IterativeImputer, mean, median, and SoftImpute. The ensemble method leverages the performance of each individual technique to provide the most accurate imputation for each missing value. We conducted extensive evaluations on a dataset with artificially introduced 2%, 5%, 10% and 20% missing data. Our results, analysed using root mean square error (RMSE), demonstrate that the proposed ensemble method consistently outperforms each individual imputation method across various levels of missing data. This research highlights the effectiveness of an ensemble approach in enhancing data quality and reliability, offering a robust solution for practitioners dealing with incomplete datasets.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Deep Learning Models for Sentiment Analysis on Social Media Data Using Hybrid BiLSTM-CNN Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In the modern era, social media platforms serve as key venues where individuals engage in conversations, share ideas, and express opinions. Sentiment analysis is a subfield of Natural Language Processing that seeks to examine public emotions and opinions, offering valuable insights helping businesses, governments and organisations to connect with public sentiments. This work investigates Deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTMs), Single and Multilayer Bidirectional LSTMs (BiLSTMs), and Hybrid Neural Networks. Using the Sentiment140 dataset, preprocessing techniques were utilised to clean noisy data, and GloVe embedding were applied for improved word representation. The hybrid BiLSTM-CNN model successfully combined CNN’s capacity to extract local semantic patterns with BiLSTM’s strength in capturing contextual features, outperforming all other models with an accuracy of 76.54%.

articleTitle: Automated Pomegranate Leaf Disease Identification: An Image Processing Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Agriculture is a predominant occupation in India, and to date, automated plant disease detection has been applied primarily to crops such as paddy, wheat, and various vegetables (e.g., tomato, cucumber, and potato). In this work, a novel approach is proposed for the automated detection and labeling of pomegranate leaf diseases by employing Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification and K-Means Clustering for image segmentation. The study focuses on four specific plant diseases—Bacterial Blight, Alternaria Alternata, Cercospora Leaf Spot, and Anthracnose—as well as the detection of healthy leaves when no affected areas are present. To enhance the visibility of the leaf images, contrast enhancement is performed as a preliminary step. Subsequently, K-Means Clustering is applied to segment the input image in the Lab color space. A Multiclass SVM is then utilized to classify the segmented regions based on identified affected portions of the leaf. Finally, the Region of Interest (ROI) is determined to calculate and display the total affected area, facilitating precise disease-type detection. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 0.96, a precision of 0.95455, a recall of 0.9333, an F1 score of 0.978, and a kappa statistic of 0.947, thereby demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed system for automated pomegranate leaf disease detection.

articleTitle: Investigation on Different Array Configurations of Microstrip Antenna at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This article presents a 5G mm-wave rectangular microstrip patch antenna that operates at 28 GHz and examines the impact of gain variation as the number of antenna elements increases. The antenna has a 6×6×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> footprint and operates in the 28 GHz frequency band (26.78-29.7 GHz) with an impedance bandwidth of 3 GHz (⩽ -10 dB). The patch is 4.6×1.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in length and width. Throughout the experiment, a typical FR-4 material with a substrate thickness of 1.6 mm and a dielectric constant of 4.4 is taken into consideration. The multiple array antenna elements are used to examine the gain increase technique. Experiments with a 2×2, 4×4, and 8×8 antenna array have shown that the gain of the antenna is significantly increased by increasing the number of radiators. The single antenna element has a gain of 7.58 dB. The antenna's gain rises to 13, 18, and 25 dB in various array configurations as the number of array elements increases.

articleTitle: ANSYS-Based Finite Element Approach to Enhance PM-BLDC Motor Efficiency For EV Support
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper presents an exhaustive study on the performance enhancement of a Permanent Magnet Brushless DC (PM-BLDC) motor toward electric vehicle applications using both mathematical modelling and finite element method (FEM) analysis. Such an investigation of critical design parameters includes stator and rotor configuration, torque-speed characteristics, and magnetic flux distributions using a combination of analytical methods along with FEM simulations. All modelling is done in MATLAB, while FEM analysis is run in ANSOFT MAXWELL within the ANSYS environment to achieve high accuracy and precision. The proposed design methodology is validated by comparing results from analytical and FEM approaches. A 550-watt PM-BLDC motor with a rated speed of 1500 rpm is designed, and its efficiency, torque, and cogging torque are analysed. The findings demonstrate the motor's potential for optimised performance in EV systems. The detailed analysis points out that the techniques used in this work on the ANSYS-based FEM improve the efficiency of PM-BLDC motors. The development of reliable and sustainable EV technologies can be enhanced through the techniques adopted in this work.

articleTitle: A Review on Design Optimization of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors for Modern Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) extensively used in various sectors such as Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEV), industries and Renewable Energy Source (RES) applications because of their optimal flux-weakening, high torque density and low weight. This paper analyzes the optimization design and analysis of PMSM. The Interior-PMSM (IPMSM) is internally employed the rotor with PM this makes the proposed work more appealing than the traditional converters to fulfill the characteristics of different types of electric motors. The costs and the motor size gets reduced by implying PM. Based on the comparative analysis including Y-shaped, V-shaped and spoke type, integrating V-shaped magnet for PMSM attains highest inductances, low peak cogging torque and has the lowest magnet weight compared to conventional design configurations. The effective design of the motor includes a comprehensive perspective on various potential machine designs, leading to the selection of an appropriate design. The strong correlation between the simulation results and the experimental findings for the globally optimized Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) design with V-shaped magnet achieves high efficiency of the optimization method. The PMSM achieves higher performance at relatively cost and make it as an optimal solution for driving the machine.

articleTitle: A Fine-Tuned Deep Transfer Learning-Based Framework for Efficient MRI Brain Tumor Images Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The expansion of brain tumor cells increases intracranial pressure within the skull, posing a serious threat to the delicate processes of life. Medication is the only solution to maximize lifetime. If not treated early on, it can be fatal. Thus, brain tumor categorization is a critical issue in the medical profession. Deep Transfer learning approaches (DTL) have demonstrated significant potential for brain tumor categorization. Utilizing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images of the brain skull. Transformer-based deep learning models have shown promising results for image categorization. This paper uses skull striping and mean filter to remove extra layers, denoise brain tumor cancer cell images, and classify using four pre-trained CNN architecture models: Alex Net, DenseNet-201, ResNet-152, and EfficientNet-B3. The approach employed in this study achieved the highest accuracy, with a value of 99.72%, using EfficientNet-B3. The ResNet-152 model also achieved a good accuracy rate of 99.23%. Other models have tumor classification accuracy values of DenseNet-201 98.62%, and Alex Net 98.22%, respectively. The findings indicate that EfficientNet-B3 has proven to be the most effective model for detecting brain tumor cancer cells. This level of accuracy facilitates early cancer detection, enabling identification before any physical symptoms appear.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis on Refined BiLSTM-RNN Models for Accurate Forecasting of Bottom Hole Pressure in Managed Pressure Drilling Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Managed Pressure Drilling (MPD) is a crucial technique in the oil and gas industry, ensuring optimal pressure conditions to reduce risks like bore instability and blowouts. Accurate Bottom Hole Pressure (BHP) forecasting is essential for real-time decision-making, but traditional methods often fail to capture the complex dynamics of drilling environments. This paper introduces a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Network (BiLSTM-RNN) model for BHP forecasting in MPD. The process includes data exploration, cleaning, pattern identification, feature engineering, and dimensionality reduction to enhance computational efficiency. The BiLSTM-RNN model addresses the vanishing gradient problem and passes in time-series analysis. Simulations in Python achieved reliable error metrics, including MSE of 31942.15, MAE of 136.71, MAPE of 13.02, RMSE of 178.72, and an R2-score of 0.6, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving drilling performance and safety.

Author Keywords: Bidirectional long short-term memory - Recurrent neural network

articleTitle: Dynamic Composite S-Boxes for High-Speed IoT Encryption with Enhanced Security
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: For resource-constrained systems and IoT applications, the proposed DS2B is an efficient encryption scheme. Further, the issues of the DS2B are that it has a very simple form and offers strong encryption. Therefore, to support strong nonlinearity, the results of some of the performance analyses of the DS2B presented have been able to support strong nonlinear analysis. For achieving throughput enhancement, dynamic composite S boxes and associated pipelining methods replace LUT-based S boxes. The flip-flop-based masking technique, applied for the highest level of transformation of the encryption key and for enhancing resistance against any scan-based attacks, is utilized in the S box module in this work. Without compromising the quality of the proposed core, this research presents alternatives that are faster as well as more secure. The performance of the proposed method is analyzed, and simulation results have clearly depicted its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Parkinson’s Disease Prediction Using Spectrograms and Deep Belief Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This research presents a way to forecast Parkinson's disease in the early stages by means of spectrogram investigation and deep belief networks (DBNs). The aforesaid way concentrates on the use of spectrograms in order to get the best results and the extraction of innovative features and patterns from the signal of the speech or motor, which is indicative of Parkinson's disease. By using DBNs, which is a resilient deep learning mechanism, the system has the good feature of learning deep representations of the data, which makes the detection and classification accurate. The coupling of spectrograms with DBNs gives the model perspective to notice even the less severe differences in the input signals which are often missed out by traditional methods. The outlined aggregate demonstrates a prologue to a system that would be an accurate and automated solution to the problem, which in the end could be a help to healthcare professionals in a timely procurement of intervention and treatment. The proposed model makes clear the the ability of advanced machine learning techniques to solve hard neurological disorders and enhance patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Aerial and Satellite Image Analysis: a CNN-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Applications like disaster management, urban planning, and environmental monitoring rely on satellite image categorization. This project develops a machine learning pipeline using MobileNetV2, a CNN architecture, to classify high-resolution satellite images. It employs two convolutional layers (3x3 kernels) with ReLU activation, 2x2 max-pooling, a fully connected layer, and a SoftMax output for multi-class classification. Images are resized to 200x200 pixels (RGB) to balance detail and efficiency. MobileNetV2 was chosen for its low latency and high performance, using depth-wise separable convolutions and inverted residuals. The model, optimized with Adam and categorical crossentropy, achieved 98% validation accuracy and F1-scores above 0.96 across all classes, converging in 8 epochs. The architecture balances simplicity and performance for robust feature learning and generalization. This approach highlights CNNs' ability to classify satellite images effectively. Future work could explore transformer-based models or integrate temporal satellite data to enhance analysis. This work offers a scalable, automated solution for satellite image classification.

articleTitle: Advanced Projectile Propulsion System Using Harnessing Kinetic Launch Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This project delves into the pioneering development of a kinetic launch system designed specifically for the deployment of projectiles. Inspired by Spin Launch Technology, the system leverages centripetal force to achieve high-speed launches, offering a cost-effective and energy-efficient alternative to traditional combustion-based methods. By utilizing centripetal force, the system minimizes fuel consumption and reduces operational costs, making it an environmentally friendly solution. The study chronicles the engineering challenges and innovative solutions encountered during the creation process, such as overcoming the immense stress and heat generated during launches and ensuring the structural integrity of the projectiles. Advanced materials and design techniques were employed to address these issues, resulting in a robust and reliable system. Furthermore, the research highlights the potential applications of this technology in various sectors, including military and aerospace industries. For the military, it could revolutionize the deployment of munitions and reconnaissance devices, providing rapid and precise delivery. In the aerospace sector, it could facilitate the launch of satellites and other space-bound payloads, reducing dependency on conventional rocket propulsion.

articleTitle: Discovering Influential Nodes in Hypergraphs With MHRW Sampling and Isolating Centrality
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Determining the influential nodes is a fundamental problem in analyzing the dynamics of a complex system. The complex systems are represented as hypergraphs, conventional centrality metrics, such as degree, closeness, betweenness and harmonic centralities have been extended from graph-based models to hypergraphs, but these adaptions fail to capture the unique structural characteristics and higher order relationships inherent in hypergraphs. To overcome these limitations, we proposed Isolating centrality (ISC), quantifies node influence by incorporating both local connectivity patterns and degree of structural isolation. To manage the computational complexity of analyzing large-scale hypergraphs, we employed the Metropolis-Hastings Random Walk (MHRW) sampling technique, traditionally used in graphs and extended to hypergraphs, by preserving the basic properties of hypergraphs. For this sampled hypergraph we computed ISC and compared it with traditional metrics by evaluation metrics such as SIR model, Kendall Tau correlation analysis.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability Analysis in Transmission and Distribution Network using Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The reliable operation of modern power systems relies upon voltage stability analysis, especially when load demands and the integration of renewable energy sources increase. Conventional methods struggle with real-time and large-scale analysis. In this study, Modal Analysis and Random Forest machine learning model are combined to propose a novel method to evaluate voltage stability and to detect the most vulnerable branch in the network with contingency analysis and load variation. The feasibility of the proposed work is evaluated in IEEE 14 bus transmission system and IEEE 33 bus radial distribution networks, respectively. The results demonstrate the promising potential of machine learning for voltage stability prediction

articleTitle: GlobalLearn: An Efficient Multilingual Textual Summary for Education Videos
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Educational videos have become a preferred medium for learning, offering advantages such as self-paced study, the ability to revisit concepts, and a distraction-free environment. However, the effective- ness of such videos can be amplified through concise, multilingual textual summaries. This paper introduces GlobalLearn, an AI powered educational video to text summarization application that integrates speech recognition, optical character recognition, and NLP-driven large language models(LLMs) to extract and summarize key concepts from educational videos. By integrating audio and visual transcripts, time-stamped summaries, and multilingual capabilities, GlobalLearn ensures accessibility for diverse global audiences. This user-centric approach not only supports efficient learning and revision, but also bridges linguistic barriers, fostering an inclusive educational ecosystem. The paper explores GlobalLearn’s design and technical architecture, and core functionalities to outline its potential impact on modern education.

articleTitle: Computational Model of Episodic Memory: Encoding, Recalling, Forgetting
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper introduces a computational model of episodic memory that learns episodes in response to continuous sensory input. The proposed model utilizes a Hebbian based associative learning network to dynamically encode events by associating sensory inputs from different fields as activities within an event and applies a mapping technique to store episodes. The proposed mechanism makes use of ART that can continuously learn new activities with and without forgetting past ones, making them suitable for real-time incremental and lifelong learning. The ART makes event activities generalized as it continuously adds new information on match with the existing activities, and forgets past ones. In proposed model event is divided into a set of simultaneously occurred activities which represents a binding of current sensory values with its corresponding category variables. The model further incorporates both episode and event forgetting mechanism and combined with a mechanism of episode updating. It also incorporates a consolidation mechanism that prevents false information (events) from being added to the episode and ensures that no events are forgotten after a certain number of recalls over time. An empirical investigation was done in order to validate the suggested episodic memory model. The recall accuracy of the model was assessed utilizing incomplete and erroneous cues. The results of the investigation demonstrate that even with imperfect and noisy cues, the suggested model is highly connected with encoding and recalling events and episodes.

articleTitle: Lightweight CNN for Everyday Human Sound Classification on Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This study presents a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that recognizes everyday sounds on IoT edge devices. Audio signals encompassing daily activities are captured via a microphone and transformed into time-frequency images using Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT). The proposed CNN is optimized for low computational requirements and performs better than established pre-trained models such as DenseNet, EfficientNet, InceptionNet, MobileNet, NASNet, ResNet, VGGNet, and Xception. The model achieves an overall validation accuracy of 84 % in a ten-fold cross-validation framework, with a compact model size of only 854KB and an inference time of 7.3 milliseconds (ms) on a Raspberry Pi. In comparison, EfficientNetV2B1, the second-best performer, achieves comparable accuracy but with a significantly larger size of 27.1 MB and an inference time of 119.99 ms. The model’s inference time was evaluated on various devices, including Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA A100, Tesla V100, and Intel Xeon Platinum, demonstrating its efficiency across different platforms. The dataset includes everyday human sounds, such as crying, applause, breathing, coughing, footsteps, laughter, brushing teeth, snoring, and drinking water. The efficiency and accuracy of the proposed CNN make it ideal for real-time sound recognition in smart home automation, health monitoring, and ambient assisted living, where low latency and resource efficiency are critical.

articleTitle: From Misinformation to Truth: Fake News Detection with Transformer-Based Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Nowadays, technological advancements have significantly transformed information dissemination and consumption strategies. People acquire news through online portals such as social media and news websites. However, this change is also accompanied by the rapid spread of fake news based on false and misleading information. The main reason is that the coverage of digital platforms and social media is wide, and news can spread quickly without any authenticity verification. This problem poses a serious challenge to social trust, the ability to make wise decisions, and democratic stability. Therefore, in this study, we developed an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) model to detect fake news using Transformer (BERT, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa ) models and evaluated their performance based on indicators such as accuracy, recall, and F1 score. The results show that RoBERTa performs best due to the use of a large dataset and better contextual understanding and achieved an accuracy of 93.84%, a precision of 91.80%, a recall of 95.28%, and an F1 score of 90.82%.

articleTitle: Identification Method of Building Engineering Structural System Based on Fuzzy Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: There are complex problems such as nonlinearity, time-varying and environmental interference in the identification of building structures. Based on this, this paper introduces a system identification method based on fuzzy neural networks. This method uses the powerful nonlinear mapping and learning capabilities of fuzzy neural networks to accurately and quickly identify the dynamic characteristics of building structures. First, the paper uses three-dimensional modeling technology to construct a digital twin model of the building structure as the basis for system identification. Secondly, IoT devices are deployed at key locations of the building structure to collect structural response data. Then, the input data is converted into a fuzzy set through fuzzification processing, and the fuzzy rules are trained and optimized using the self-learning ability of the neural network. Then the model is used to identify the dynamic characteristics of the building structure. In the test of 20 sets of different building structure data, the average accuracy of this method reaches 99.17%, with the highest accuracy reaching a perfect 100% and the lowest reaching 98.2%. The identification time and identification accuracy are also better than the identification method based on radial basis function network. This paper enhances the understanding of structural dynamic behavior and provides new perspectives and tools for structural safety assessment and disaster prevention in the field of construction engineering.

articleTitle: Robust Exudate Segmentation in Retinal Fundus Images using the combination of Efficient-Net and U-Net Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is an eye disease. Lesions like exudates play a major role while grading DR. Hence, it’s important for accurate segmentation of exudate, as it plays a significant role in detecting and segmenting lesions. The exudates are smaller in shape and size, which are often irregular, and the contrast is also not high. Therefore, it is challenging to identify the exudate’s actual location to get exudates in fundus images. Here in The paper, we present a novel deep neural network architecture that focuses a combination of EfficientNet and U-net architecture to accurately segmenting the exudate present in the fundus image. The proposed framework combines a U-shaped structure with residual connections to capture the subtle features of exudates. Here, in this paper, we proposed model has been utilized using Karas and Tensor-Flow tools, and it provides accurate results in identifying exudates, even small in size. This model has been trained and evaluated on the Indian Diabetic Retinopathy Image Dataset (IDRID). The experimental results show a novel precision (pre) value of 96.79%, Area Under Curve(AUC) value of 90.57%, a dice coefficient value of 96.87%, and an IOU value of 95.63%, This method demonstrates a significant improvement, outperforming the other states-of-art approaches in terms of accuracy and performance or efficiency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Graphene-Silicon Based Two-Port THz Patch Antenna using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The enhancement of MIMO antenna performance assumes a pivotal role in addressing the escalating demands of high-capacity wireless communication systems. These techniques, in tandem, contribute to improved data rates, expanded coverage, and a more dependable wireless connectivity. This paper proposes a hybrid twin port radiator with polarization and pattern diversity features in the THz frequency domain. The design is suitable for THz-based cellular machines due to its three main contributions: (i) a rounded wave is obtained by stimulating the silicon ceramic via fan blade formed slot; (ii) the |S11| of the designed aerial is effectively predicted by the Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost technique; (iii) the radiator is tunable due to the coating of graphene over silicon dielectric; the optimized result confirms that the planned aerial operates effectively between 2.46-3.16 THz with less than 3-dB axial ratio from 2.62-2.9 THz.

articleTitle: Emerging Field of NoC-Based Convolution Architecture with Systolic Arrays
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Neural networks are widely used in image detection and identification applications because of their efficacy in handling complex problems. However, they require substantial memory bandwidth and CPU operations, limiting the performance of conventional CPUs. To address this challenge, researchers have developed an FPGA hardware accelerator for Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs). To enhance acceleration performance in CNNs, researchers have identified three key techniques: parallelization, memory optimization, and specialized data flow. A new network on-Chip paradigm was created by the researchers to reduce the off-chip memory Optimization according to researchers, a Network-on-Chip (NoC) architecture and Systolic Arrays (SA) have been created to enhance runtime, computational efficiency, and throughput while reducing off-chip memory traffic. In this paper recent trends in the NoC-Based CNN architecture have been represented.

articleTitle: Plant Disease Detection using Image Processing and Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Agriculture is a key contributor to the GDP of our country, India. Plants play a very important role in the ecosystem and plant diseases can negatively impact the agricultural industry by causing huge losses to the food supply. Plant leaves are prone to a variety of diseases, including blights, leaf spots, and other infections. Therefore, identifying diseases efficiently is crucial to pave the way for sustainable agriculture. In the field of agriculture, traditional and manual methods for detecting diseases in plants have sometimes been found to be inefficient and error prone. We therefore present a novel solution to these issues by introducing a method to automate plant disease detection in the Tomato plant leaf by using advanced Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) frameworks, image processing libraries and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The pipeline of our work involves preprocessing plant image datasets, generating synthetic images using GANs, segmenting region of interests via a U-Net model, and classifying diseases with a CNN-based classifier. A deployed model ensures accurate disease identification from user input.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection at the Edge Computing: A Deep Learning Approach Using the UNSW-NB15 Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Edge computing has transformed technology by enabling seamless connections between IoT devices, but it also introduces significant security challenges. EC is crucial for providing minimal latency processing and reducing the load on centralized servers, ensuring timely and scalable intrusion detection for IoT environments. The findings underscore the potential of combining edge computing, IoT, and deep learning to address evolving security challenges in distributed systems. To mitigate these risks, efficient models for detecting malicious activities are crucial. This study investigates the application of edge computing, Internet of Things (IoT), and deep learning to improve the performance of Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). By leveraging the UNSW-NB15 dataset, the research assesses the capability of deep learning models to identify and mitigate cyber threats effectively. The results demonstrate better performance, showing their suitability for real-time security applications. These findings highlight the potential of intelligent intrusion detection systems powered by robust datasets and deep learning for addressing evolving security threats in edge computing environments.

articleTitle: Integrative Hybrid Machine Learning Methodologies for Decoding and Analysing Complex Encoded Data on Oil Pipeline Incident Patterns and Risks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Oil pipelines are vital components of global energy infrastructure, but it is susceptible to accidents that leads to severe environmental and economic consequences. Accidents are often preceded by complex, high-dimensional sensor data, which is challenging to interpret and analyze directly. This paper presents a novel hybrid Machine Learning (ML) approach, called the Hybrid Boost Forest Net, for analyzing encoded data on oil pipeline accidents. Boosting is a popular ensemble learning method that improves predictive accuracy by sequentially correcting the errors of weak models. ForestNet, on the other hand, leverages a deep neural network architecture specifically designed to handle complex, high-dimensional data through multiple layers of feature extraction. In this hybrid approach, Boosting first refines the data by focusing on difficult- to-predict accident instances, while Forest Net further processes the refined data, identifying intricate patterns and dependencies between pipeline conditions, environmental factors, and operational parameters. The method is tested using real-world accident data, demonstrating superior performance in accident prediction compared to traditional machine learning models. Results indicate that the Hybrid Boost ForestNet approach not only enhances predictive accuracy but also improves interpretability, offering significant potential for early detection, risk assessment, and preventive measures in pipeline safety management. The evaluation phase employs metrics like mean squared error (MSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) to assess the model’s predictive performance. This project is implemented using Python, achieving a MSE of 0.71 and an accuracy of 96%.

articleTitle: Early Eye Disease Detection Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Early detection of eye diseases such as diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and cataracts is crucial in preventing severe vision impairment and blindness. This study explores the application of machine learning (ML) techniques, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), for the automated diagnosis of eye diseases. A deep learning model was trained on a labeled dataset of retinal images, utilizing CNNs for feature extraction and classification. The Tkinter-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) facilitates easy user interaction, enabling real-time diagnosis from uploaded eye images. Experimental results demonstrate a high accuracy rate of 91%, outperforming traditional diagnostic techniques. Additionally, explainable AI (XAI) methodologies were incorporated to enhance model interpretability, improving trust and usability in clinical settings. In the proposed methodology the findings highlight the potential of ML in ophthalmology, paving the way for cost-effective and scalable screening solutions.

articleTitle: Network and Security Solution using Jaya Algorithm-based graph search for Drone Transportation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This study reports the suitability of several algorithms to identify the best course in a network of lines that is utilized to guide an Unmanned Arial Vehicle (UAV) aircraft in a safety configuration. It utilizes a waypoint graph using Jaya algorithm for this purpose, which is based on the GPS coordinates of flight route movement locations in three dimensions. It performs a comparative analysis of the drone path prediction using a dynamic adjacency matrix that represents the shortest path in the graph. In the context of the area observation mode, evaluate the benefits and drawbacks of the two routing methods.

articleTitle: Hybrid Framework for Chronic Kidney Disease Prediction: Integrating Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System and LIME
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) affects millions of people worldwide, making early detection critical for effective management and treatment. This paper presents a novel approach for CKD prediction using a hybrid model that combines the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) with Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME). The ANFIS framework integrates fuzzy logic for managing uncertainty, while LIME enhances model interpretability by explaining individual predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that this hybrid model achieves competitive accuracy and provides actionable insights, making it a valuable tool for healthcare professionals.

articleTitle: Design of Circular and Inverted Y-Shape Slot Loaded Dual Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The main aim of this paper is to design a dual-band antenna for wireless communication applications. This proposed antenna is prepared by using rectangular notches, circular, and inverted Y-shaped slots. Initially, a pair of rectangular notches is created on bottom corners of the patch; after that, an inverted Y-shaped slot is created on the top, and finally, two circular slots are created in the patch. The proposed antenna is resonating from 3.19 to 3.40 GHz for lower and while 4.97 to 5.53 GHz for upper bands. The bandwidths of 210 MHz (6.37%) in lower band (LB) 560 MHz (6.98%) are obtained by the proposed antenna in upper band (UB) frequencies. The proposed antenna resonates at 3.30 GHz with a return loss (RL) of –14.54 dB in the lower band and resonates at 5.24 GHz with a return loss of –41.77 dB. The proposed antenna provides a gain of 4.21 and 4.80 dB, a VSWR of 1.46 and 1.01, directivity of 4.37 and 4.80 dB, and also an efficiency of 90.62% and 93.99% in the lower and upper bands. The proposed antenna is very efficient and convenient for the various applications of wireless communication.

articleTitle: A Bayesian Optimization Framework for Adaptive Node Deployment in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) require efficient node deployment strategies to optimize network longevity, energy consumption, and coverage. This paper introduces a novel approach for strategic node deployment in WSNs using Bayesian Optimization (BO). A BO-based framework that iteratively modifies node positions to maximize network performance metrics, such as energy efficiency and coverage ratio, while minimizing execution time is proposed. Through extensive simulations across diverse deployment scenarios, the proposed method is evaluated and demonstrates superior performance compared to both traditional and machine learning (ML)-based techniques. The results indicate significant improvements in coverage and energy efficiency, alongside competitive execution times. These findings highlight the potential of BO to enhance WSN deployment strategies, offering a scalable and adaptive solution for real-world applications. Future research will focus on integrating BO with other optimization techniques and extending the approach to dynamic environments and varied network configurations.

articleTitle: Person Detection using Proposed YOLOv8 algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Surveillance systems are vital for detecting and preventing crime, especially in urban environments where real-time monitoring is crucial. This research proposes an advanced surveillance system that combines proposed YOLOv8 object detection with DeepSORT tracking for tracking a person in crowded place, enhanced with a DenseNet backbone, achieves 97.1% detection accuracy and an mAP of 0.971 at an IoU of 0.5, outperforming YOLOv3 and YOLOv5. The model makes use of Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP) and Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) for multi-scale detection and an anchor-free approach for improved accuracy. Integrated with DeepSORT, the system tracks individuals reliably across frames, even in dynamic environments. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly improves detection and tracking efficiency, making it ideal for automated surveillance and crime prevention in urban areas.

articleTitle: An FMS Reconfigurable Model With S4PR Petri Nets by Controllable Transitions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The reconfigurable model of the flexible manufacturing systems (FMSs) with Petri Net by controllable transitions (CTs) is presented in this work. The Petri Net (PN) can provide effective procedures to solve deadlock handling in the FMS. Accurately eliminating deadlocked states in FMS and dynamic processes demonstrates the effectiveness of CTS. A novelty algorithm is presented to obtain the maximum permissive behaviors with fewer supervisors, which are obtained fully live. S4PRs, a system of sequential systems with shared resources, are used to implement the PNs that are effective and practical for describing the FMS interaction processes. The motivation analyzes and simulates FMS models using the PN simulator to solve the deadlock. The influence of a reachability graph (RG) is essential for detecting the states of deadlocked (DL). This paper focuses on the influence of CTs in PN that are controlling all resource utilization. In particular, the dynamic model of different kinds of FMS can have optimal solutions given by CTs.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Worst-Case Power-Delay Performance for a 1-Bit Full Adder
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The growing demand for high-performance computing requires the development of compact, high-speed, and energy-efficient processor architectures. As a critical component within Arithmetic Logic Units(ALUs) and Floating-Point Units (FPUs), the full adder significantly impacts overall system performance and power efficiency. This study investigates and evaluates various full-adder implementations that utilize 90-nm CMOS technology within the Virtuoso Cadence EDA tool. A comprehensive testing methodology was used, which encompassed all 56 possible input combinations and nine distinct input patterns, to determine the worst-case delay and maximum dynamic power dissipation. Furthermore, the study analyzed the influence of temperature variations and capacitive loading on delay and power consumption, providing valuable insights into the full adder’s performance across diverse operating conditions. The 28T Full-Adder demonstrated superior performance, while the 28T Multiplex-based Full Adder exhibited the lowest performance among the four architectures evaluated.

articleTitle: Square Patch Antenna for Breast Tumor Detection at 2.45 GHz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This work involves the novel use of a square patch antenna uniquely tuned to work at the resonance frequency of 2.45 GHz as a vital tool in breast tumor detection. The objective of the research is to utilize this property of the given antenna configuration to facilitate the challenging task of identifying and characterizing breast tissue cancers. Holding the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) measurements as the reference methodology, the study tries to find out some signs of tumors from small variations in the SAR values placed at specific locations. The aim of the work is to determine multi-parametric SAR patterns associated with the pathophysiologic processes in the breast using theoretical modeling and empirical validation. Such opinion is backed by empirical work that shows that there are significant changes in SAR profile especially at 1g and 10g samples and that outline a way of achieving high level of tumor identification. Interpreting the SAR dynamics and the tumor pathophysiology, the work presents rich data source for the biomedical engineering and oncological diagnostic fields. Such talk not only represents a shift in the making in the early-detection of breast cancers but also underscores the need for enhancing the development of differential treatment strategies which leads to enhancements in the quality of operations and outcomes in the treatment of early-stage breast cancers. Taking all the facts into consideration, it can be stated that the study is a real breakthrough in the framework of medical science, as well as, in the treatment and diagnostics of breast cancer. This is the best example that illustrates the utility of advanced technologies and the latest clinical developments side by side.

articleTitle: Analysis of Automatic Detection Algorithm for Network UI Design Violations Based on Unity3D
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The network UI design based on the Unity3D engine faces design violations such as unreasonable interface layout, non-compliant interactive operations, and potential interface element errors. This paper proposes a UI violation detection algorithm based on the Unity3D engine. The algorithm first traverses the UI tree structure of the Unity3D scene, starting from the root node and going deeper layer by layer to obtain all UI objects and their component information one by one. Next, specific and detailed violation detection rules are set according to the UI design specifications. At the same time, in order to detect interactive operations more accurately, a ray detection algorithm module is introduced to simulate user operations and detect various interaction modes of UI objects, such as ray interaction, trigger interaction, and field of view. Through the ray detection algorithm, it detects whether the button is clicked correctly and whether the drag operation is smooth. In the violation determination stage, the information of each UI object is compared one by one with the preset violation detection rules. A comparison found that the algorithm is superior to traditional manual detection methods in terms of detection speed and accuracy. The average detection time is shortened to 1.68 seconds and the accuracy is as high as 99.1%. In addition, the detection efficiency and accuracy of the algorithm are further improved by integrating feedback learning mechanism, modular design and optimizing algorithm performance. This study not only provides a new automated method for network UI design violation detection, but also verifies its effectiveness in practical applications through experimental data.

articleTitle: Advancement of Loan Approval System for Diverse Applicants with Machine Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In the current financial environment, Utilization of applicant data for pre-assessment can significantly enhance the effectiveness of loan approval processes. Traditional loan approval processes sometimes rely on financial specialists which can lead to mistakes, biases, and higher operational costs, eventually compromising the quality of service (QoS) for clients. Technology can speed up, minimize risk, and improve decision-making. This is vital for economically unprivileged people who often have trouble securing loans owing to insufficient financial literacy and a lack of understanding of eligibility criteria. This research study presents a computer-based loan approval system that use machine learning (ML) algorithms to accurately forecast loan eligibility using key financial parameters. It provides applicants with insights for informed decisions while ensuring inclusivity across diverse demographics and socioeconomic backgrounds. A thorough comparison of multiple ML algorithms has been performed using publicly available loan approval dataset available at Kaggle platform. The results demonstrate that the XGBoost model significantly outperforms other machine learning models in terms of predictive accuracy, offering a robust solution for enhancing transparency and inclusivity in loan approval processes. This automated, data-driven approach enables financial institutions to make more efficient and unbiased lending decisions, ultimately improving the overall fairness and reliability of their operations.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic based Soil Nutrient Categorization System for Decision Making in Soil Nutrient Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Soil health determines plant health, quantity and quality of the yield. By assessing soil nutrient status, farmers can address nutrient imbalance and promote long-term soil health. The soil nutrient status of the particular soil can be categorized as Low, Medium, or High. Conventional methods for evaluating soil nutrient usually give exact numbers for nutrient levels, but these numbers might not reflect the natural uncertainty or variability in soil properties and measurements. Fuzzy logic, on the other hand, uses linguistic variables and fuzzy sets to represent imprecise information in a way that’s easier to understand. Using fuzzy if-then rules, soil nutrient values can be translated into a more intuitive soil nutrient status within a a set range. The present study aims to develop a comprehensive framework that utilizes fuzzy logic-based categorization methods to assess soil nutrient status. Linguistic variables are defined to categorize soil nutrient levels as Low, Medium, or High. Membership functions are established to quantify the degree of belongingness to each category. Fuzzy rules are formulated based on expert knowledge, encompassing 12 parameters to assess soil nutrient status. Simplifying the system into four distinct categories mitigates complexity, focusing on macronutrients, physical attributes, secondary and micronutrients. A final fuzzy inference system with 36 rules was developed to categorize soil nutrient status that facilitates informed decision making for agricultural practices using Python's skuzzy tool. This paper outlines the advancement of soil fertility assessment and underscores the applicability of fuzzy logic-based systems in agricultural decision-making processes.

articleTitle: Efficient Traffic Density Calculation for Diverse Road Traffic using Yolov8 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Accurate traffic density estimation is vital for effective traffic management. Traditional methods like inductive loop detectors and radar have high costs and scalability issues. This report introduces a method using the YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm to calculate traffic density. YOLOv3, fine-tuned with a custom dataset, enhances vehicle detection accuracy. The approach involves collecting video feeds from traffic surveillance cameras, sampling frames at regular intervals, and processing them with YOLOv3 to detect and count the number of vehicles. Traffic density is calculated based on vehicles per unit length of the road. Testing across various lighting conditions and traffic densities showed a detection rate consistently above 95%, validating the method's robustness. YOLO's real-time processing ensures efficient traffic density computation, supporting timely traffic control decisions.EfficientDet algorithm is also detects the vehicles but not accurate as YOLO algorithm as it does not detect the fast moving vehicles which leads to the inefficient use of algorithm.

articleTitle: Smart irrigation for soil moisture prediction using hybrid AI and fog computing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Irrigation control is essential for optimizing water usage in smart agricultural systems, especially where there is water scarcity. The fast development of IoT and fog computing brings up new opportunities for developing new and advanced systems that are both efficient and flexible. Further integration of fog computing with machine learning will bring more developments to smart agriculture systems. This paper has framed an irrigation supervision algorithm to predict irrigation needs in the smart agriculture system. The methodology uses a hybrid algorithm that incorporates Gradient Boosting (GB), Logistic Regression (LR) and Random Forest (RF). The system accurately forecasts the irrigation requirement by processing ecological information such as humidity, temperature, and time-based factors. 97.78% of accuracy illustrates the reliability of the resultant model, and initial processing of the data illustrates that information is concise and accurate. Recall, precision and F1- score are computed as metrics for the performance. The system is integrated into fog computing and machine learning to manage real-time data processing to achieve faster and more accurate predictions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Intelligent Greenhouse Environmental Management Using Fuzzy Logic Control Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In modern intelligent greenhouse environmental management, the complexity and dynamics of environmental factors make temperature control more difficult. Traditional control methods show problems of insensitive response and insufficient precision when facing a greenhouse environment with multiple variables and uncertainties. For this reason, this paper studies an optimization scheme based on fuzzy logic control algorithm. First, this paper establishes a mathematical model of the relevant greenhouse environment, which comprehensively considers multiple variables such as temperature, humidity, and light. Then this paper uses a fuzzy logic controller to monitor and adjust these environmental parameters in real-time. The final experimental results show that fuzzy logic control has significant advantages in improving temperature control accuracy, response speed and system stability. Among them, in the temperature control accuracy experiment, the system can keep the temperature in the greenhouse within ±1°C of the set target temperature. In the response speed experiment, the system can quickly recover when the external temperature changes suddenly. In the stability experiment, the system can maintain the stability of the internal environment of the greenhouse when facing changes in external temperature, humidity and light. In the above data conclusions, the fuzzy logic control system demonstrates its superior performance and can effectively improve the efficiency and accuracy of intelligent greenhouse management.

articleTitle: Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Airborne Object Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Airborne object detection and classification play an important role in applications like military surveillance, border security, and public safety. The ability to accurately distinguish between airplanes, helicopters, drones, and birds is essential for monitoring and responding to potential aerial threats in real-time. This study leverages the AOD 4 dataset, which contains a comprehensive collection of 22,516 images spanning diverse environmental conditions. After organizing the dataset into four distinct classes, a custom lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was developed to classify airborne objects. The proposed lightweight CNN achieves a remarkable accuracy of 97.12% and is able to outperform state-of-the-art pre-trained models in terms of accuracy and model size. On top of it, the model is also targeted at the various processors to unleash its potential to run in a real-time environment. The proposed model infers in 2.9 milliseconds on intel core i7 processor, which is a fourfold improvement compared to the MobileNetv3Small model. The findings from this study contribute to advancing the field of airborne object classification and pave the way for more robust real-world implementations.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a 4 GHz Antenna with Enhanced Bandwidth through Slot Configuration Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This report presents the design and performance analysis of a 4 GHz antenna with varied substrate materials likeFR-4 epoxy (4.4), Arlon 25N (tm) (3.38), Roger RO4350(tm)(3.66), and Nelco N4000-13 SI (tm)(3.4). The electrical properties of each substrate material are analyzed, and its effect on the antenna's performance is evaluated. Our research explores a range of dielectric materials with varying permittivity values to assess their effects on key antenna parameters such as bandwidth, gain and VSWR.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient 8T SRAM Cell for Enhancing Read/Write Assist Performances with Stability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The paper proposes a proposed 8T SRAM cell design with a read and write path for read and write operations, which improves read and write stability when compared to the 6T SRAM cells. To solve leakage power concerns, two PMOS transistors were included in the read and write circuitry. This implementation substantially decreases leakage current caused by the induced swing restoration inverter (SRI). The proposed 8T SRAM cells show a significant decrease in leakage current, with reductions of 37.66% and 40.11% compared to 6T SRAM cells. In terms of read latency, the proposed 8T cell surpasses the 6T SRAM cells by 39.80% and 89.13%, respectively. Furthermore, the study reveals a higher speed in write operations, with a 46.97% improvement over the 6T SRAM and a 57.5% gain in performance above the proposed 8T SRAM. The RSNM and WSNM of the suggested 8T SRAM cell were 100 mV and 649 mV, respectively, which shows a considerable improvement compared to the 6T SRAM cell. The performance of the 6T SRAM and suggested 8T SRAM cells is illustrated through simulation studies in the Cadence Virtuoso environment based on the 130 nm technology node.

articleTitle: Multimodal Affective Communication Analysis: Integrating Text Sentiment with Speech Emotion using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The final aim is to integrate sentiment analysis and speech emotion recognition through transfer learning. These traditional systems analyse text and speech separately - thereby missing a lot of emotional expressions that cannot be captured in either text or speech alone. Hence, the presented work integrates both modalities to improve emotion detection accuracy. Advanced natural language processing models complete the task of text sentiment analysis while features from acoustics and deep learning techniques help complete the task of speech emotion recognition. Its power with transfer learning – leveraging. These methods will primarily improve the final recognition performance of speech emotion recognition where available labelled data can't measure up with their original corpus. The study indicates that such late fusion techniques compared with unimodal systems work way better- more robust and accurate class recognition of emotions is achievable.

articleTitle: Advancing Automatic Number Plate Recognition: Insights, Innovations, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This study explores the advancements and future prospects of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) technology. By integrating state-of-the-art algorithms such as YOLO for vehicle detection, Custom YOLO for precise number plate localization, DeepSort for vehicle tracking, and Tesseract OCR for character recognition, the research elucidates optimal ANPR system design and implementation strategies. Findings reveal significant contributions to law enforcement, traffic management, and surveillance domains, enhancing security, traffic flow, and resource utilization. The study underscores the importance of algorithm optimization, data augmentation, and adaptive learning for advancing ANPR technology. Looking forward, opportunities lie in hardware acceleration, multimodal fusion, and ethical considerations to further elevate ANPR efficacy and address societal concerns. Collaboration across academia, industry, and government sectors will drive continued innovation, enabling safer and smarter communities in the digital age.

articleTitle: Sustainable Substrate Design for High-Performance Wi-Fi Antennas in Green Electronics
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Microstrip patch antennas are important parts of modern wireless communication systems because of their compact size, high efficiency, and versatility.
