In this paper, the effect of the properties of the substrate material on the performance of coaxial-feed rectangular microstrip patch antennas operating within the Wi-Fi band (2.4–2.485 GHz) is investigated. A comparative analysis was thus carried out on substrates such as FR-4 and RT Duroid 5870 using CST Studio Suite, evaluating gain, directivity, bandwidth, and return loss. This shows that low dielectric substrates, such as those of Rogers 5870, offer better performance since they provide optimal impedance matching, increased gain, and least return loss, thereby recommended for high-frequency applications. This study underlines the importance of substrate optimization in designing energy-efficient and green antennas for next-generation technologies such as 5G, IoT, and wireless sensor networks in the context of green electronics and sustainable communication systems.

articleTitle: Sentimental Analysis of E-Commerce Product Reviews for Product Specific Insights
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The abundance of digital data available in today’s environment can improve quality of life and offer helpful insights. In the e-commerce space, customer evaluations and comments about a product may truly be utilized to gain valuable information for the seller, which can then be applied to the product’s enhancement. This study seeks to collect comments on the product’s surrounding features as well as the polarity of the sentiments expressed in product reviews. By doing this, the vendor will be able to comprehend the consumer market, consider ideas, and adjust their product properly. The model implementation consists of three parts, aspect term extraction, opinion term extraction, and sentiment score calculation. An unsupervised rule-based model has been implemented to extract aspect and opinion terms, whereas a BERT model to obtain the sentiment score.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Channel Estimation Using Geo-spatial Data With Modified DMRS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Accurate channel estimation is very important in wireless communication systems and particularly with the increasing demand for enhanced connectivity in diversified environment (multiple). Traditional techniques that often rely on complex mathematical models, which struggles to balance for dynamic and noisy conditions, especially in multicarrier signal transmission/propagation. This paper will explore the application of a fully connected deep neural network (DNN) for better channel estimation across various scenarios, include urban areas like Tokyo and Bengaluru, as well as rural and semi-urban regions like Bastar and Patiala. MATLAB 2024b as the primary simulation tool, the proposed AI-based approach eliminates the need of complex and twisted channel modeling and adapt to real-world like conditions. Once the model is trained on specific scenario and environmental parameters, the DNN model will then demonstrates superior performance and accuracy compared to the traditional methods, even in challenging different propagation environments. By leveraging data-driven and insights, the AI model can achieve lower mean squared error (MSE) notably, which showcase its hidden potential to address the limitations of traditional techniques. This study will highlight efficiency and comparison of AI-driven channel estimation with traditional method in ensuring better communication across different environment scenarios. Our findings will later be useful in easily integrating it into 5G and beyond, due to its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on Computational Art Design Visual System Based on Weak Artificial Intelligence Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The increasing development of weak artificial intelligence technology has had a profound impact on the field of design. It not only provides new sources of inspiration for artistic creation, but also makes the constraints of visual communication design more complex. At the same time, media convergence has promoted a strong demand for cross media conversion and diversified output, especially in the process of brand visual innovation, where more and more multimedia elements, dynamic effects, and interactive needs are emerging. Traditional visual design methods are insufficient in this complex design environment, and there is an urgent need to innovate design patterns through new technologies and strategies. Since the concept of "computational design" was proposed, algorithms and programming techniques have gradually become the core tools of modern visual design. Through extensive practice, computational design has not only brought rich changes to brand visual forms, but also developed into a systematic design pattern that can respond to the diversity and dynamism of today's design needs. This study explores the structure and development of computational visual design systems, with a focus on analyzing their potential applications and practical strategies in new retail pet brands. Through in-depth market research, the application opportunities of computational design in brand vision have been revealed, and algorithm based brand vision construction strategies, brand image communication strategies, and community driven visual communication strategies have been proposed. Finally, by combining the actual design case of the "Xiaopei Pet" brand, the effectiveness of these strategies was verified, providing new ideas for innovation in the field of brand visual design and valuable experience for the future development of computational visual design.

articleTitle: Advanced Embedded Software and Systems using MBD for Electrical Grid Stability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper describes the advance embedded system and software platform for inspection of grid infrastructure in the electric utilities sector for resilient power supply. A systematic model-based development (MBD) design approach used for plant model development for visual inspection of electric grid and embedded coder used for the controller code generation. The solution for critical applications such as detecting hotspot using embedded infrastructure with cloud/ server-based image processing to achieve the grid stability explained in this paper.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Real-Time Spectral Peak Estimator for Radar Altimeter Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This research work presents Real-Time Spectral Peak Estimator for radar altimeter signal analysis on an FPGA- based platform, focusing on accurate beat frequency estimation for precise above-ground level (AGL) altitude measurements. The proposed design is based on the first-order derivative difference estimator combined with zero crossover point detection to identify spectral maxima efficiently. This estimator is implemented using a fixed-point concurrent FPGA architecture to achieve high computational efficiency, low latency, and optimal hardware utilization, enabling real-time processing of radar return signals. This system has been verified and validated during various lab and field tests for the accurate beat frequency estimation under the dynamic signal conditions. The solution meets the stringent performance requirements of radar altimeter applications, making it suitable for aerospace, autonomous landing, and navigation systems where real-time accuracy is critical.

articleTitle: Enhanced Sand Cat Swarm Optimization to Achieving Maximum Coverage for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: When it comes to ensuring the effective operation of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), it is essential to achieve total coverage of the region that is being targeted. However, the random initial deployment of sensor nodes often leads to inefficient positioning, resulting in coverage gaps. To mitigate this issue, an improved algorithm based on the Optimization of the Virtual Force-Directed Enhanced Sand Cat Swarm (SCSO) is introduced to optimize sensor node placement, thereby reducing coverage voids and enhancing overall network coverage. This approach enhances the natural hunting behavior of sand cats and integrates a nonlinear convergence mechanism to improve their sensitivity. Moreover, the algorithm incorporates a virtual resultant force as a perturbation factor during node position updates, accelerating convergence and enhancing optimization efficiency. Simulation results, based on the deployment of 30 sensor nodes within a 60 m × 80 m area, demonstrate that the SCSO algorithm that was proposed is capable of achieving a coverage rate (CR) of approximately 99.61%, reflecting a 29.3% increase over the baseline. Additionally, the algorithm maintains superior coverage performance across different sensor node densities and monitoring region sizes.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Transmission Line Faults in Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The reliability of power transmission systems is vital for delivering uninterrupted electricity. Faults such as Single Line-to-Ground (SLG), Line-to-Line (LL), Double Line-to-Ground (LLG), Three-Phase (LLL), and Three-Phase-to-Ground (LLLG) pose significant risks, causing disruptions and potential damage to infrastructure. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of these faults using MATLAB/Simulink to simulate various fault conditions and assess their impact on voltage and current waveforms. The analysis evaluates fault severity and system response, providing critical insights into fault dynamics. The results emphasize the necessity of robust protection schemes to minimize fault impacts, reduce downtime, and ensure system reliability. This research advances the understanding of fault behavior and contributes to the development of more effective fault detection and protection strategies, which are essential for maintaining the stability and integrity of modern power transmission networks.

articleTitle: Lightweight Chest X-Ray Classification for Pneumonia and Tuberculosis Using MobileNet with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Chest X-rays are a low-radiation, cost-effective alternative for the diagnosis of respiratory diseases and are particularly valuable as a first-line screening tool. Our solution uses deep learning to classify chest radiographs into three categories: pneumonia, tuberculosis, and healthy (without disease). The Mobile Net model has a lightweight architecture perfectly suited for smartphones which in turn is useful as our aim here is to make this tool accessible, easy to use and helpful for health care workers in remote areas. In order to improve trust and reliability, we have incorporated explainable AI (XAI), which provides detailed insights of how the model arrived at a particular conclusion/decision. While our model does maintain a balance between speed and accuracy, we have also tested it against other resource-intensive models such as ResNet and DenseNet. The results show that MobileNet achieves comparable accuracy while significantly reducing computational demands. This was designed as an early diagnostic aid and provides a feasible, affordable alternative to CT scans, especially for regions with minimal access to advanced medical infrastructure. Its aim is to combine innovation and accessibility in one place to bring about timely and effective healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Pipelined and Low-Power MAC Unit with Sparsity-Aware Encoding for Neural Network Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Multiply- Accumulate Units (MACs) are basic blocks in accelerators for neural networks, which need both high throughput and low power consumption to optimize matrix and vector computations. The present work proposes a new pipelined MAC architecture targeting neural network operations, focusing on issues concerning power efficiency and performance in computation. The proposed design exploits sparsity-aware methods to remove unnecessary operations with zero or redundant inputs, which reduces energy consumption significantly. An optimized pipeline architecture ensures decreased latency and increased throughput that makes the design suitable for real-time applications. Experiment results reveal that the proposed MAC unit performs very well in terms of power efficiency and processing speed compared to state-of-the-art architectures. This shows its suitability for energy-efficient neural network accelerators.

articleTitle: Research on Semantic Analysis Algorithm of Network Public Opinion Based on LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, social media platforms have become the main places for the public to discuss hot events, express opinions and emotions. Real time monitoring and effective analysis of online public opinion play a crucial role in grasping social dynamics, preventing and resolving social conflicts. This study aims to improve the accuracy of predicting changes in online public opinion by constructing and optimizing a semantic analysis algorithm based on LSTM, in order to more effectively manage and guide public emotions and maintain social stability. This article introduces the structures and functions of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), LSTM, and BiLSTM. Collect data through social media platforms and train and evaluate it using a BiLSTM model. The findings indicate that the BiLSTM model surpasses RNN and conventional LSTM models regarding predictive precision, particularly in managing long - range dependencies and grasping textual contextual details. The article also discusses the impact of Dropout technology and activation function selection on model performance. The BiLSTM model provides an effective method for predicting network public opinion trends, which helps to identify emotional outliers in a timely manner and prevent public opinion events from developing into major social events.

articleTitle: Design & Optimization of Advanced wearable body worn two port MIMO Antennas with Reduced Mutual Coupling through Genetic Algorithm used in Consumer IOT and Health Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In this proposed work, a two-port wearable MIMO Antennas is designed by using a jeans substrate whose dimension is 70×70×1.0 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> placed on a 0.035 mm thick ground plane of same dimensions and, a rectangular patch antenna of dimension 11×15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is situated on jeans substrate. A single patch dimension is optimized through Genetic Algorithm. Now after optimization, a 2-port MIMO Antennasis designed and to avoid the mutual coupling between two antennas, a resonator of dimensions 38×4 is added with a gap of 38 mm, now the complete system is simulated using CST software and through parametric analysis, the desired value of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> is found to be -38.81 dB at 6 GHz resonance frequency used in the application of 5G wireless communication, Consumer IoT, medical application, Wi-Max

articleTitle: Leveraging Seasonal Trends and Symptomatic Data for Precise Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Our analysis examines the amalgamation of seasonal and symptomatic data to boost the forecasting of diseases, emphasizing the need for proactive healthcare measures. The rising need for accurate, data-driven preventive healthcare solutions, especially in regions where seasonal variations significantly impact disease patterns, serves as the foundation for this study. We developed a comprehensive prediction framework using a range of machine learning models, including logistic regression, decision trees, Naive Bayes, K-nearest neighbors, support vector machines (SVM), and random forests. Our results show that logistic regression and SVM achieved high accuracy both with and without the use of SMOTE, demonstrating their effectiveness in handling imbalanced datasets. This technique links symptoms, seasonal variations, and disease patterns for precise categorization and actionable insights, enabling effective illness detection and preventive coordination. The findings of this study help foster the use of machine learning methods to improve preventive healthcare and illustrate the need to include contextual seasonal data in healthcare forecasts. Additionally, the research highlights how symptoms and seasonal variables work together dynamically, demonstrating the potential of adaptive models to assist with healthcare decision-making in real-time.

Author Keywords: Dynamic Disease Modeling. Support Vector Machine(SVM)

articleTitle: Internet of Things Based Agriculture Crop Cutting Mechanism Using Green Energy and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The physical tool called a lawn cutter uses renewable energy sources rather than electricity to cut grass. Since it is utilized in lawn movers that can be left in direct sunshine, the renewable energy is referred to as solar. The body is constructed first from a hollow square bar, and a caster wheel is positioned beneath the square bar's body. A solar panel is then positioned on top of an incline fiber plate that has been mounted on a body. The energy is transferred via solar panels and transformed into electrical energy, which is subsequently transformed back into mechanical energy. The electric motor, which is attached to the shaft, receives this electrical energy. This representation explores the evolution of IoT deployment in addressing various agricultural issues by looking at enabling technology, services, and agricultural applications built on state-of-the-art machine learning models. Potential obstacles and constraints in the IoT based agricultural system.

articleTitle: Fault Location Technology of Information System Across Isolation Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Fault location across isolated devices remains one of the most challenging tasks for modern information systems. Traditional linear regression fault location technology results in highly inaccurate and unproductive diagnoses due to the complex nature of the network environments and multiple layers of isolation. This paper aims at studying the fault location technology of information systems across isolated devices, specifying the improvement expected for diagnosis in both accuracy and speed. System logs and network traffic data are collected by data acquisition tools, which are then processed by feature extraction technology to individualize the key fault features. The convolutional neural networks (CNN) are then applied to identify and locate the patterns of fault. The experimental results indicate a maximum accuracy of 93% for this method in locating faults, with diagnosis time being reduced by 34% on average compared to the linear regression method. The CNN-based fault location technology appears to be capable of significantly improving the capability of fault diagnosis for information systems across isolated devices and providing a new solution for the fault management of complex network environments.

articleTitle: Deep-Prenatal: A Deep Learning Approach for Detection and Analysis of Nuchal Translucency for Enhanced Prenatal Screening
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Nuchal Translucency (NT) observed in ultrasound scans is widely utilized to identify genetic abnormalities in foetuses. However, NT measurements may be challenging to perform as a mainstay of prenatal screening. These challenges include operator dependency, which primarily relies on the technician’s expertise, and variations in imaging settings that can introduce data anomalies. Thus, the precision of NT measurements is not always definitive, raising questions about their dependability in clinical practice. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) framework is proposed to address these constraints. This architecture comprises of Conv2D, Max Pooling, Dense, and Flatten layers and advanced components. Together, these elements enable the CNN to effectively identify and analyse NT measurements, thereby automating the process and reducing reliance on human involvement. The proposed CNN architecture performs well across critical criteria such as accuracy, precision, recall, and Intersection over Union (IoU). Furthermore, the framework has demonstrated stability when applied to diverse datasets, owing to its robustness and flexibility across various clinical databases. This proposed efficient and reliable preliminary screening method, based on the enhanced CNN architecture, addresses the inherent limitations of NT measurements. It establishes a new benchmark for accuracy in the field and introduces a transformative approach that enhances clinical outcomes.

articleTitle: Collaborative Filtering Approach for Improved Recommender System by VADER and TextBlob
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper presents a grocery recommendation system using collaborative filtering to enhance user shopping experience and increase sales. The proposed method leverages both user-based and item-based collaborative filtering techniques to analyze purchase history and identify patterns among users with similar shopping behaviors. By comparing a user's preferences with those of similar users, the system generates personalized product recommendations. This approach aims to address the challenge of providing relevant and diverse suggestions in grocery retail, where user preferences are dynamic and varied. Experimental findings reveal that the proposed system achieves high accuracy in predicting user preferences, presenting a practical and effective solution for recommendation systems in the grocery domain.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Multiband Circularly Polarized Antenna for Indoor/Outdoor Tracking and Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This article presents a low-profile, small size, multi-functional circularly polarized antenna design for tracking and sensing systems. The antenna resonates in the ultra-high frequency (UHF) (915 MHz), GPS L2 (1.227 GHz), RFID 1.8 GHz, 2.45 GHz, and 3.3 GHz bands. The use of the GPS L2 band makes sensing more secure, precise, and accurate than the GPS L1 band, and RFID bands are used for indoor sensing, whereas GPS L2 is used for outdoor sensing. The proposed antenna is a cross-dipole arrangement, with three dipoles printed on each side of the polyimide substrate, which is extremely flexible and heat-resistant. The primary dipole, consisting of longer metallic patches with semi-arrow-shaped terminations, is designed to cover the UHF and GPS L2 frequency bands. The subsequent dipole consists of inverted mirrored L-shaped radiators that operate in the 1.8 GHz frequency band. The third dipole consists of an L-shaped radiator that operates in the 2.45 GHz and 3.3 GHz frequency bands.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks for Noise Reduction in Electrocardiogram Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals are essential for detecting and diagnosing heart diseases. Nevertheless, in the presence of noise and artefacts, ECG signals usually corrupt, hindering diagnostic and analysis. Conventional ECG denoising methods, like filtering techniques, are not efficient in mitigating complex noise patterns. This research examines the potential of applying Denoising based on GANs to ECG signals. ECG signals can be considered as time series signals. Deep ‘Recurrent Neural Networks’ were widely used for advanced regression and forecasting tasks, but that was before 2005 when Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) were first described. We propose a GAN-based architecture for denoising ECG signals, and through experiments, we demonstrate its efficacy in removing both white noise and motion artefacts from ECG data. Our results indicate that GANs can outperform conventional denoising methods, leading to clearer and more reliable ECG signals for further clinical analysis.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models for Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Protecting networks from mischievous attacks in the scenario of cybersecurity require Intrusion Detection System (IDS). Leveraging machine learning algorithms to develop IDS has gathered substantial consideration due to its capacity to adapt and study from vast datasets. In this research paper, an extensive analysis of intrusion detection has been conducted utilizing various machine learning models trained on the CICIDS2018 dataset. Fifteen distinct models have been explored, ranging from traditional methods to sophisticated deep learning architectures. Subsequently, Random Forest has been identified as the optimal classifier based on its superior performance metrics of F1 score 99.79%, precision 99.79%, and recall 99.81%. Moreover, a framework has been proposed for real-time intrusion detection using the Random Forest classifier, employing CICFlowMeter for data collection, which aligns with the dataset used for model training.

articleTitle: Role of Edge Computing in IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Computing stands at a crossroads between speed and scale. The cloud promises vast computing power and storage, yet shuffling data to and from those distant servers takes time - often too much. Edge computing looks to resolve that dilemma by shifting processing closer to the devices generating all that data. Rather than relying solely on gargantuan centralized cloud servers, edge computing utilizes nearby devices and micro data centers to enable real-time, location-aware services and this distributed approach brings quicker responses and leaner loads by leveraging local gadgets to handle localized computing chores. However fully activating edge computing's potential requires surmounting a few obstacles first. Efficiently coordinating myriad devices for data storage and number-crunching poses logistical challenges. Integrating these decentralized nodes into the centralized cloud framework demands care and forethought. And securing expansive networks of hardware and software is no simple feat. Still, the promised gains in speed and adaptability compel this revolution in computing.

articleTitle: Classification of Ovarian Tumor using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Cancer of the ovaries is one of the most challenging malignancies to diagnose accurately due to its varied tumor types and complex morphology. This study leverages advanced deep learning techniques, integrating CNN’s, GeoProteoNet & VGG models that enhanced with transfer learning to improve detection precision. Tumor is classified based on the shape of the tumors and the area of the origin of the tumor and some other parameters. There are majorly three types of tumors. They are Germ cell tumor, Stromal tumor and epithelial tumors. With the deep learning model we can classify and test the type of tumor and accurate tumor segmentation. The hybrid approaches address challenges like limited datasets and variability in tumor morphology by incorporating augmented data and multi-model genomic-proteomic analysis. The method achieves over 90% accuracy(99.7%), promising significant advances in the ovarian cancer diagnostics and reduced diagnostic delays.

articleTitle: CKKS Homomorphic Encryption Scheme for Financial Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Homomorphic Encryption(HE) makes it possible for highly regulated sectors to collaborate securely and share data. To achieve different objectives of financial services and preventing malicious activities financial institutions use various confidential data. Across a range of application areas detecting anomalies concerns the risk since unprotected data could contain important, crucial, and useful information and the use of machine learning models is essential for performing these operations. Models for machine learning are particularly vulnerable to different types of attacks at different phases of implementation due effective application in different domains based on sensitive data. The machine learning model can be protected using HE and HE is a cryptography technique that promises to provide privacy to data for sharing along with performing complex computations on confidential data. In this paper anomaly detection is performed using Multilayer perceptron, Random Forest, KNN and SVR. The performance of models is compared with the models working on encrypted data and pain text data as well.

articleTitle: Analysis of Demodulation Algorithm For Data Transmission In Low Orbit
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of signal attenuation and low transmission efficiency in low-orbit satellite data transmission, this paper analyzes and implements an effective modulation and demodulation algorithm. First, in view of the frequent interruption of links in low-orbit environments, a scheme based on QPSK (Quadrature Phase Shift Keying) modulation is designed, combined with Forward Error Correction (FEC) to improve anti-interference capability. Then, the ACM (Adaptive Coding and Modulation) adaptive equalization technology is introduced to deal with the nonlinear effect of channel attenuation, and the transmission efficiency is maximized by adjusting the spectrum resource allocation. Finally, this paper conducts experimental verification on an actual low-orbit satellite communication link. The experimental results show that under the condition of 20dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the bit error rate (BER) of the scheme using QPSK modulation combined with FEC coding is reduced. After combining ACM technology, under the SNR condition of 20dB, the system transmission rate is increased to 0.85bps/H, and under high spectrum resource configuration, ACM technology shows more significant performance improvement. From the above data conclusions, the modulation and demodulation algorithm proposed in this paper can effectively deal with channel fading and interference in low-orbit satellite communication systems, improve data transmission efficiency, and has strong anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: Abusive Content Detection with LangChain Integration Using Fine-Tuned RoBERTa
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The proliferation of abusive content on social media platforms necessitates the development of automated detection systems. This research focuses on integrating a fine-tuned RoBERTa model with LangChain to classify text into hateful, offensive, or neither categories. The study leverages a pretrained RoBERTa model for high-accuracy classification and employs LangChain to generate meaningful explanations for predictions. Results demonstrate an overall accuracy of 91%, highlighting the model's efficacy in detecting abusive content while providing transparent reasoning for classifications.

articleTitle: Enhancing 6G Communication Ecosystems with Blockchain Technology: A Comprehensive Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The landscape of the communication system is undergoing a rapid evolution, emphasizing the need for intelligence, efficiency, and adaptability to enable cloud computing, Internet-of-Everything, and cyber-physical systems. With the rapidly growing complexities and interconnectivities of the systems, assurance of security and privacy is of paramount importance. The inherent nature of blockchain technology is its immutability, decentralization, anonymity, and transparency. It has the potential to establish trust between distributed networks through secure access management, robust authentication, improved integrity, confidentiality, and optimized resource allocation. Implementation of blockchain technology in 6G communication systems is likely to introduce dramatic innovations, enabling digital economy growth and enhancing societal functioning and connectivity. This article delves into the history of the evolution of mobile communications from 1G to 6G, the significance of blockchain technology in 6G, and the latest advances in terahertz antennas that can make an immense contribution to the field of 6G technology.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Multipath TCP Congestion Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In modern high-speed networks, providing reliable and high-quality Internet services is essential. However, maintaining consistent network performance in dynamic environments with varying scenarios presents significant challenges. To address these, Multipath TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) offers a viable solution by aggregating multiple network paths, resulting in improved bandwidth utilization, higher throughput, and reduced delay. This approach overcomes the limitations of traditional single-path TCP by enhancing responsiveness, friendliness, and reducing window oscillation. Moreover, MPTCP incorporates congestion control mechanisms that couple several subflows, ensuring efficient traffic distribution across multiple paths, thereby improving overall network performance and fairness. In this paper, we analyze the performance of LIA (Linked Increases Algorithm), OLIA (Opportunistic Linked Increases Algorithm), and BALIA (Balanced Linked Adaptation) congestion control algorithms using the ns-3 network simulator. The results show that BALIA achieves 21% higher throughput compared to LIA.

articleTitle: Research on Network Traffic Transmission Characteristics of Substations Based on FRFT System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the characteristics of cosine-Gaussian beams in a fractional Fourier transform system and conducts research through theoretical derivation and simulation. In the research on the ideal fractional Fourier transform system, the parameter settings of a standard focal length of 2.0 meters, a wavelength of 1.06 micrometers, and a beam waist radius of 1.0 millimeter are adopted. For the fractional Fourier transform system with spherical aberration, the spherical aberration coefficient c takes the values of ±0.001, ±0.002, and ±0.003, and the modulation parameter is 3. The purpose of studying its transmission characteristics is to provide theoretical references for the research on network traffic transmission characteristics of substations. The paper introduces the theoretical basis and research methods of fractional Fourier transform, elaborates on the concept, image and properties of cosine-Gaussian beams, deeply analyzes their transmission characteristics in different fractional Fourier transform systems, draws relevant conclusions and looks forward to the future research directions.

articleTitle: Crop Recommender and Yield Prediction System using Ensemble Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Machine learning techniques to develop a system for crop recommendation and yield prediction, aimed at supporting data-driven agricultural decision-making. Exploratory data analysis (EDA) is conducted to identify patterns within the data, and correlation maps are used to visualize relationships between features. The dataset is split into training and testing sets, with preprocessing involving feature scaling through Standard Scaler and categorical encoding via OneHotEncoder. Decision Tree Regressor (DTR), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), and Gradient Boosting Regressor are incorporated as base models in the architecture whereas XGB and Random Forest (RF) Regressor are used as meta-models in a Stacking Regressor pipeline. Stacking is chosen over other ensemble methods like bagging and boosting because of its ability to combine multiple models for meta learning framework. The performance of the model is evaluated using the following metrics Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) scores. The model developed provides an effective and practical tool for improving agriculture decision making through cutting edge machine learning methodologies.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Single Phase PWM Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Inverters are key components in modern power systems, converting DC to AC power efficiently. The use of Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) techniques in inverters is crucial for improving performance by enhancing power factor, reducing harmonic distortion, and increasing overall efficiency. This analysis focuses on Sinusoidal PWM (SPWM) techniques, specifically comparing unipolar and bipolar configurations through MATLAB-Simulink modeling. The analysis highlights the significance of reducing total harmonic distortion (THD), which is essential for achieving better power quality and operational efficiency in applications ranging from household appliances to industrial systems. By evaluating the performance of SPWM inverters with and without filters, this work provides insights into the optimal design and implementation of inverters for various load conditions. The findings underscore the importance of advanced PWM strategies in modern power electronics, paving the way for more reliable and efficient energy conversion solutions.

articleTitle: Exploration of Computer Linguistics Model Algorithms Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: How to build an effective language model in NLP field to capture the statistical laws of language, improve the performance of machine translation, and enable machines to understand and generate texts with complex semantic structures is still a problem that cannot be ignored. Firstly, word segmentation, cleaning, etc., and word embedding using Word2Vec pre-training model are carried out. Then the Transformer model is constructed, and the whole sequence is processed simultaneously through the self-attention mechanism. In this paper, the learning rate, the size of hidden layer and the number of layers are adjusted by grid search, and the dropout technology is used to prevent over-fitting. Transformer model performs well in machine translation tasks, with accuracy exceeding 95%, and the METEOR value is generally higher than that of LSTM model, which is stable at a high level. In 20 different text generation tasks, the BERT score of the model is between 0.83 and 0.99, which shows that the model can understand and generate complex semantic structures. These results prove the effectiveness of Transformer model in dealing with natural language tasks, and provide new directions and ideas for future research and application.

articleTitle: Marine Mammals Sound Classification Using a Lightweight CNN for Edge Computing Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)

authors.preferredName: Vellalacheruvu Venkata Siva Sai Anil Kumar

abstract: This paper presents a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for marine mammals sound classification. Seven classes are considered in this work, namely humpback whale, killer whale, pilot whale, sperm whale, spinner dolphin, striped dolphin, and white whale. The sound signals are transformed from the .wav file to time-frequency images through Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT). The proposed CNN consumes time-frequency images as input and consumes only a 0.8 MB size model benchmarked against several well-known pre-trained models, including DenseNet, Efficient-Net, InceptionNet, MobileNet, NASNet, ResNet, VGGNet, and Xception. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed lightweight CNN significantly outperformed pre-trained models, able to achieve a validation accuracy of 80.9% in a ten-fold cross-validation framework. The best performance among the pre-trained models is Mo-bileNetV3Small, which achieved only 78.91% validation accuracy in a ten-fold cross-validation framework with a considerably larger model size of 4 MB. Furthermore, the proposed model was successfully deployed on the Raspberry Pi IOT module and able to run with 30.134 milliseconds per inference. The lightweight CNN’s high accuracy and low latency make it an ideal candidate for applications in real-time audio event detection in underwater with resource-constrained devices.

articleTitle: Application of VR Virtual Reality Technology in Intelligent Space Environment Design
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Environmental design is undergoing a transformation from traditional design methods to digital technology driven, and the trend is unstoppable. Virtual Reality (VR) technology, with its immersive experience and high interactivity, provides designers and users with a new way of design and experience. This article adopts a systematic approach to clarify the goals and user expectations of the smart space through requirement analysis, and uses professional software to construct a detailed virtual model. In terms of technical implementation, this article describes the selection and configuration of VR hardware and software, 3D modeling, and virtual environment construction. By comparing with traditional design methods, this article finds that VR technology significantly improves user satisfaction, optimizes spatial layout, and shortens design cycles. The average satisfaction rate of users using VR technology reached 91.12, while the satisfaction rate of users using traditional design methods was only 68.84. In addition, VR technology has shown significant advantages in design accuracy and design cycle, with an overall design accuracy of over 80.2% and a significantly shortened design cycle.

articleTitle: Lora-Enabled System for Smart Farming Management and Oversight, Utilizing Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to create a LoRa-based smart farming management and surveillance system. Utilizing Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) in rural settings, with the aim of replacing the existing technology in agricultural monitoring systems. A dedicated private network server is established and connected to a gateway, which gathers information or signals from the nodes at the end and sends this data to the cloud without the need for routers. This data can then be utilized for various applications by the end users. The system overcomes issues related to communication failures and energy-efficient data transmission. This advanced farming platform enhances the effectiveness of farming methods. The proposed methodology is the application of resources including as water, fertilizers, and pesticides should be optimized in order to achieve maximum efficiency while simultaneously minimizing waste. Farming productivity and sustainability are both significantly improved because of its contribution, notably in terms of the efficient management of resources. And intelligent cities used to improve agriculture—comparing the planned weather station and the numerous developed patents. The technique here is like a cutting-edge, reasonably priced choice for local weather monitoring.

articleTitle: Hybrid AI Models for Predicting Inshore and Offshore Oil and Gas Exploration Fields
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The oil and gas industry faces significant challenges and opportunities in the era of digital transformation, with rising energy demand driving the need for improved production efficiency, cost reduction, and environmental impact minimization. This study presents a hybrid AI learning model aimed at enhancing predictions for inshore and offshore oil and gas exploration fields to address these challenges. The process begins with raw data collection, followed by data cleaning, transformation, and visualization to gain insights into its complexity. Feature engineering extracts meaningful attributes, preparing the data for model input. A hybrid CNN-BILSTM model is employed to improve classification accuracy, and the system implemented using Python, established significant improvements. The model's accuracy and precision is 90% and 92%. Highlighting its effectiveness in handling complex data and enhancing classification results. The system demonstrates robust performance in refining accuracy iteratively for better predictive results.

articleTitle: Optimization-Driven Vendor Selection with Tabu Search and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Vendor selection in supply chain management is a complex but extremely important process that requires the evaluation of multiple factors such as cost, quality, delivery time, and responsiveness. This study presents a new hybrid methodology that makes the vendor selection process more efficient by combining tabu search optimization and neural network analysis. The proposed model operates in two stages. In the first stage, tabu search algorithms systematically analyze the solution space and identify optimal vendor combinations based on predefined criteria. In the second stage, these selected combinations are evaluated through a neural network. This trained network has the ability to recognize patterns in performance indicators such as cost efficiency, delivery time, and operational wastage. Tests conducted on simulated data clearly demonstrated the superior performance of this hybrid model compared to traditional single-method approaches. The model significantly improved key parameters such as Mean Absolute Error and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score. Moreover, it also proved to be adaptable to changing conditions. This framework not only addresses challenges such as scalability and integration of qualitative-quantitative factors in vendor selection, but also highlights the effectiveness of combining optimization algorithms and machine learning techniques for complex supply chain decisions. This model not only serves as a practical decision-support tool for procurement managers but also lays a strong foundation for the development of hybrid AI techniques in the field of operational optimization.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Kidney Disease Prediction using Combined LSTM and MLP Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Kidney disease (KD) is a prevalent global health issue, and early prediction is critical for improving patient outcomes. In this study, we propose a federated learning approach that combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) models for kidney disease prediction. The LSTM component captures temporal dependencies in the data, while the MLP enhances the model’s ability to classify based on learned features. The federated learning framework ensures data privacy by keeping patient information decentralized across multiple hospitals. Experimental results show promising accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, demonstrating the potential of combining LSTM and MLP for healthcare applications.

articleTitle: The Security Verification and Analysis of Information Nodes in Cyberspace by Deep Spiking Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In the research on the security verification technology of information nodes in cyberspace, the balance accuracy and operational stability are very important for the security of the entire Internet enterprise. In this paper, an improved method based on deep spiking algorithm is proposed to improve the effect of cyberspace information verification. In the process of research, the current security verification technology is analyzed and designed, and then the deep spiking algorithm is implemented. Then, simulation experiments and final applications are carried out to verify its effectiveness. Experimental data shows that the improved system reduces the risk spillover level by 50% and improves the accuracy of safety verification by 30%. The comprehensive conclusions can show that the proposed method can significantly improve the security verification performance of information nodes in cyberspace, and provide a strong technical guarantee for the further safe and stable operation of Internet enterprises.

articleTitle: LIGHT-YOLOv11: An Efficient Small Object Detection Model for UAV Images
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Object recognition in UAV images is very challenging due to the frequent appearance of numerous small and truncated entities. Object detection is an essential component of computer vision for accurate object localization and identification in complex and dynamic aerial scenarios. We introduce LIGHT-YOLOv11, a modified object detection model that integrates architectural enhancements to address the specific challenges of aerial imagery. To improve feature extraction and emphasize essential regions, the network’s initial block has been restructured into a Focus Block. Additionally, a Transformer block has been integrated into the backbone, replacing two blocks in the final architecture, to opti-mize spatial and contextual understanding. With these adjustments, detection accuracy and processing efficiency are remarkably balanced, especially for small and closely spaced objects. In-depth analyses of the VisDrone2019-DET dataset show that LIGHT-YOLOv11 outperforms other popular techniques, producing impressive outcomes across a range of situations.

articleTitle: Application of Multi-Target Visual Tracking Method Combined with HRNet in Complex Dynamic Scenes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In crowded streets or markets, the tracking task becomes extremely challenging due to mutual occlusion, similar appearance, and rapid motion changes between targets. The paper first processes the input video frame, then uses the same human frame detector as in Simple Baseline, propagates the detected frame to adjacent frames by propagating the predicted key points according to the optical flow calculated by FlowNet 2.0, and performs non-maximum suppression. Then, pose estimation is performed within the detected human frame, and key point detection is performed using HRNet. Correspondences between keypoints in adjacent frames are computed using a greedy matching algorithm based on the similarity between the keypoints within a frame and the keypoints propagated from adjacent frames according to optical flow. Finally, the feature extraction capability of HRNet and the optimized re-identification branch are combined to achieve multi-target tracking in complex dynamic scenes. The research results show that the average tracking success rate of the multi-target visual tracking method combined with HRNet reaches 97.555%, and the number of loss times in multiple test scenarios is 0. Compared with the traditional method based on mean shift, the average IDF1 value and the highest MOTP value of this method reach 0.9115 and close to the full score respectively. Therefore, this paper provides an effective solution to the problem of multi-target tracking in practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced Identification of Fraud in Credit Card Transactions Applying Machine Learning Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Credit card theft resulting in multi-millions of dollars in damages is making it a major global financial and security concern yearly. This analysis focuses on dealing with this critical issue by establishing a model developed on machine learning that can identify fraudulent transactions effectively. Developed model leverages earlier credit card transactions to identify patterns indicative of fraud. By employing several kinds of Machine learning algorithms, comprising K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Trees, and XGB Classifier, the project evaluates the performance of each approach in accurately differentiating among transactions that are fraudulent and those that are not. These models work well for preventing credit card scams as they can manage unbalanced data, identify irregularities, and adjust to intricate fraud patterns. Random Forest and XGBoost provide excellent accuracy and resilience. Enabling early identification of fraudulent activities, and ensuring that customers’ money is safeguarded and unauthorized charges are prevented, is the principal focus. This will benefit customers by ensuring their funds are restored and their accounts remain secure. The effectiveness of the models is examined by integrating measures involving precision, recall, accuracy, F1-score, and confusion matrix after they have been trained and tested on a dataset. This paper emphasizes a way in which machine learning may be used to detect fraud also emphasizing how important the advanced algorithms are in mitigating financial losses and enhancing the security of digital transactions.

articleTitle: Mobile Edge Computing for Efficient Vehicle Management in Smart City
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC) promises to be a useful technology to enable applications in a smart city. However, the task offloading becomes challenging as the MEC infrastructure has limited resources. To solve the challenges of MEC, we have proposed a system architecture with an optimization algorithm to minimize the task delay in MEC. A Genetic Algorithm based task allocation algorithm finds the optimal set of edge servers for task deployment and processing. The proposed system efficiently optimizes the task delay in MEC as analyzed from the experiments performed by taking virtual machines as MEC servers. We show the usefulness of the proposed system by taking an application scenario for efficient vehicle management in a smart city.

articleTitle: An Effectual Forecasting of Oil Production Performance Using Advanced Adaptive Recurrent Neural Network Classifier
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Oil is the primary source of energy worldwide, accounting for a large percentage of global energy consumption, with significant impacts on economic, industrial, geopolitical, and social dimensions. It enables the movement of transport, driving globalization and economic integration because oil is a backbone of international trade. However, various reasons, including political, technical, natural, economic, and strategic ones, lead to the reduction of oil production. Hence, this paper proposed a comprehensive analysis and prediction of oil production using an advanced adaptive Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). Initially, diverse datasets are collected to ensure a robust foundation for analysis. Following this, preprocessing techniques, including data cleaning and filtering, are employed to enhance data quality and relevance. The exploration phase focuses on evaluating the data, identifying trends, and uncovering underlying patterns. Feature selection is critical to optimize the predictive model's performance. The Adaptive RNN is then utilized to model the relationships within the dataset, leading to the generation of predicted values. Overall, this work is implemented by python language. Finally, predicted the error value, such as the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 72.9% and the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 26.1%, are attained. This structured approach facilitates effective data analysis and contributes to the advancement of predictive analytics in various domains.

articleTitle: Face Emotion Recognition Using Deep Neural Network (DNN)
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Facial expression recognition is an intelligent human-computer interaction technology that gives a great sense of communication of the expression of our emotions, understanding, and intent between ourselves. Many researchers have attempted to categorize facial expressions, and it has been proven that there are seven universal basic emotions: happiness, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, disgust, and neutrality. Real-time emotion detection is achievable using a webcam. The paper discusses an architecture based on CNN for emotion detection. This model was trained on the FER-2013 dataset after performing some pre-processing steps such as scaling images and color mode correction. A multi-layer CNN model is designed for the classification of emotions as happy, sad, angry, fearful, or surprised, as well as disgusted and neutral. In addition to this, it focuses on real-time analysis to present solutions based on emotions detected, such as automatically playing videos to address sad or angry or fearful emotions. Our developed algorithm attained an highest accuracy of 97.8%. The developed algorithms are very robust, effective and helps in automated seizure detection.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Cardiac Arrhythmia using DeepCNNFeatures via Transfer Learning and Optimized -KNN
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Deep Learning(DL) has emerged as a significant area of research across various fields, particularly in healthcare. The identification of irregularities in Electrocardiogram (ECG) readings is crucial for effective patient monitoring. Research indicates that a DL model when trained on available datasets, can identify arrhythmias with high accuracies. The ECG procedure is straightforward and non-invasive, serving as a vital tool for predicting and diagnosing Cardiac Arrhythmia. This paper introduces an innovative DL model that employs transfer learning to extract features using deep networks and enables the automatic classification of ECG beats into sixteen distinct categories using the Optimized K-Nearest Neighbour Classifier (KNN). The proposed research approach initiates with collecting ECG Dataset from MIT-BIH Database. Then noise is removed using DWT Filtering. Segmentation of beats is done to extract ECG beats and labelled as per the annotation file. Further deep features are extracted using Deep Learning Models-AlexNet and ResNet18 and Classification is done using optimized KNN Classifier. Feature maps learned by a model when trained on input ECG beats can be used as general descriptors of ECG signal. Proposed system records an accuracy of 97.98% using AlexNet Feature Set and 98.18% using ResNet18 Feature Set. Our proposed transfer learning based inference model is effective, promising when compared with existing Techniques

articleTitle: Enhancing Metabolomics Pathway Prediction with Sequential Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Metabolomics is a powerful tool for the understanding of biological systems by analysis of metabolites and their related pathways. Prediction of metabolic pathways is still one of the most challenging tasks because of the complexity of molecular structures and graph-structured metabolomics data. This article presents a robust framework using Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to address the challenges. The methodology proposed includes first preprocessing through metabolite identification by mass spectrometry, and then it utilizes feature extraction through the RDKit library. The objective of the research is aim to metabolic pathway prediction using machine learning algorithm. Complex patterns and relationships are captured from the SMILES representation through the molecular graphs constructed and passed on for the GCN model to learn structured data. ReLU activation functions have been employed within a three-layer sequential GCN architecture that enables it to deliver highly accurate results while ensuring that they are understandable as well. The proposed sequential GCN Model was evaluated on the KEGG dataset with an accuracy of 98.00%, precision of 92.10%, and recall of 93.02%. The performance of these metrics is well beyond traditional approaches such as KNN, ensemble logistic regression, and other GCN based approaches. Thus, this work brings GCN based approaches closer to revolutionizing metabolic pathway prediction and the advancement of the metabolomics field.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimization Algorithm of Deep Learning and Compliant Control in Online Trajectory Planning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With the rapid development of robotics and automation, online trajectory planning faces problems such as poor adaptability to dynamic environments and low computational efficiency. This study aims to propose a collaborative optimization algorithm that combines deep learning and compliant control to improve the efficiency and accuracy of online trajectory planning. First, CNN is used for feature extraction and a prediction model is established. Then a compliant control strategy is designed to deal with dynamic obstacles to ensure the flexibility and stability of the robot in trajectory planning. The trained CNN model is then used to generate real-time trajectory predictions. The robot motion is adjusted through a fuzzy logic controller to optimize the relative position of the trajectory and obstacles. The average obstacle avoidance success rate of the algorithm in dynamic environments reaches 97%. The collaborative optimization algorithm of deep learning and compliant control effectively improves the real-time and accuracy of online trajectory planning, providing a new solution for the application of intelligent robots in complex environments.

articleTitle: Smart Vision: AI-Driven Driver Fatigue Monitoring for Drivers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Over the past decade, continuous advancements in the field of computing technologies and artificial intelligence that had led to notable improvements in systems monitoring for drivers. Various study experiments have gathered actual data on driver drowsiness and algorithms that employs about the diverse artificial intelligence and feature combinations to significantly enhance real-time performance. This paper offers a current overview of driver drowsiness detection systems that have been developed in the past decade. In this research, we address the important issue of driver drowsiness detection and to improve road safety. The proposed system utilizes deep learning, image based learning, machine learning, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) that accurately identifies the signs of driver fatigue. Using a comprehensive data set, the model is trained to recognize drowsiness. The developed solution contributes to advancing driver safety technology by providing a robust and real-time method for detecting and preventing drowsy driving accidents.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Testing of XOR-Free Polar Encoder
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Polar codes play a pivotal role for the successor of the 5G due to their capacity-achieving approach and robust error correction performance by adapting diverse channel conditions. Polar codes use channel polarization to address critical requirements like reliability and throughput of the 5G standard. In this paper, the register transfer level (RTL) code of the polar encoder is first configured in the form of a Xilinx Vivado intellectual property (IP) block and then proposed a system-level diagram for testing that IP block using Xilinx Vivado IP Integrator. This system-level diagram sends data wirelessly between Mobile Terminal (MT) and FPGA using the Bluetooth module through the UART protocol. The system-level system is synthesized and implemented with the Zynq-7000 FPGA family using the Xilinx Vivado 2019.2 tool. Further, the functionality of the proposed RTL code for the polar encoder is validated by using a hardware-software (HW-SW) co-simulation environment created between MATLAB and Xilinx Vitis Modal Composer.

articleTitle: Enhancing Socio-Economic Development Through Digital Literacy: a Strategic Imperative for Rural Communities
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Modern society requires digital literacy because it operates under IT leadership. Various locations across rural territory continue to experience technology shortages alongside insufficient training regarding proper IT utilization. The communities encounter multiple obstacles because they have inadequate internet connectivity and insufficient infrastructure alongside poor cybersecurity capabilities. A mobile-based digital platform targeting rural needs was proposed to solve this problem. Digital literacy training helps people gain abilities that enhance their access to education and healthcare services and government programs. The research examines digital literacy fundamentals alongside practical applications and educational and social effects that digital literacy creates for employment alongside society at large. The research evaluates methods which can improve digital literacy knowledge delivery to different population segments.

articleTitle: PosturalNet, an Advanced Architecture to Detect Shoplifting at Megastores
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) requires a full understanding of postural dynamics to create sophisticated surveillance systems that specifically detect shoplifting activities. PosturalNet represents a new architectural framework that uses human postural analytics to detect shoplifting incidents in large retail spaces. The proposed method uses a 2D body joint detection algorithm named OpenPose to extract postural information. Subsequently, these postures are pre-processed, and then features such as joint velocities, normalized body joints, magnitudes and angles are extracted. A combination of feature encoding techniques together with dimension reduction strategies maintains vital information while improving system computational efficiency. Testing PosturalNet on synthetic shoplifting data yielded an accurate detection rate of 96.87%. The method demonstrates robust performance in real-time applications which handle occluded environments when applied to practical store surveillance footage.

articleTitle: Smart Retail Solutions through Edge Computing and IoT Automation: Implementing Dynamic Pricing and Real-Time Customer Engagement
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The rapid advancement in retail technology has necessitated the development of systems that can adapt to dynamic customer behaviours and optimize pricing strategies in real time. This paper presents a smart retail system that integrates edge computing and IoT automation to address these challenges effectively. The system utilises YOLOv8 for real-time crowd counting, with camera sensors deployed around product shelves to monitor customer interactions. IoT devices, including smart shelves and QR codes, facilitate real-time data communication and enhance customer engagement. Edge computing processes this data locally to enable immediate adjustments in pricing and inventory management, minimizing latency and improving responsiveness. The integration of these technologies aims to optimize operational efficiency, enhance the shopping experience, and provide personalized promotions based on real-time crowd density and sales data.

articleTitle: Multi-Label Satellite Image Classification using Lightweight Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: To address the shortcomings of traditional deep learning applications for multi-label satellite image classification, this work shifts focus toward lightweight Vision Transformers (ViTs) that involve fewer parameters and can be deployed in resource-constrained devices. ViT offers a promising alternative to Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) due to its unique architecture which is designed to capture long-range dependencies more effectively. While CNN relies on convolutional layers to extract features, ViT divides images into patches and processes them as token sequences, similar to the manner text is handled in language processing, which is comparatively way better than CNN. This approach enables ViT to capture broader and more detailed features across the entire image, essential for dealing with multi-label satellite images that involve varying categories, sizes, and spatial arrangements. In our study, we employ six lightweight ViT models, namely, ViT-Small, ViT-Tiny, ViT-Base, Swin-Tiny, DeiT-Tiny, and DeiT-Base, to effectively capture different sets of labels associated with Amazon rainforest satellite imagery, leveraging extensive prior training to better recognize complex patterns and relationships within the data. The ViT-Tiny model achieves the best F-beta score (beta=2) of 0.9252, surpassing the performance of the baseline ViT model and other lightweight ViT architectures.

articleTitle: AI Driven Risk Management Model for the Entire Lifecycle of Power Transmission and Transformation Projects
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: As the complexity of power transmission and transformation projects continues to increase, the risks they face are becoming more diverse and unpredictable. Traditional risk management methods can no longer meet the accuracy and efficiency requirements of modern power transmission and transformation projects. To address this problem, this paper introduces artificial intelligence technology and adopts a full life cycle risk management model based on AI (Artificial Intelligence), aiming to improve the accuracy and timeliness of risk prediction, assessment and management through intelligent means, thereby reducing engineering risks and improving safety. Firstly, this paper uses big data technology and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) algorithm to identify the risks in each life cycle stage of power transmission and transformation projects and builds a risk assessment model. Then, based on the clustering algorithm and reinforcement learning technology, an adaptive risk warning and control strategy is proposed, which can dynamically adjust the response measures according to the real-time monitoring data. Finally, combined with actual engineering cases, the effectiveness and feasibility of the model are verified. In each group of experiments, there are differences between the minimum and maximum response times, but the fluctuations are relatively stable. For example, when there are 5 samples, the response time fluctuated between 0.30 and 0.40 seconds. The AI-driven power transmission and transformation project risk management model proposed in this paper not only innovatively supplements traditional risk management methods in theory, but also verifies its advantages in practice.

Author Keywords: risk management model for the entire life cycle

articleTitle: Improving Target Detection Accuracy with OEERP in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The energy consumption of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is constrained by battery power. This paper presents a method aimed at reducing energy usage during network routing. An opportunistic energy-efficient routing protocol, often known as an OEERP, is a concept that comprises introduced to enhance the network’s performance, improve target location detection accuracy, Increase the network’s energy efficiency while simultaneously extending its existence. The approach that has been presented puts idle nodes into a sleep state, hence reducing the amount of energy that is consumed. When the network’s residual energy (RE) is taken into consideration, sleep states are dynamically regulated and flow rate (FR), optimizing energy conservation. Nodes in sleep mode are periodically activated through triggering mechanisms. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the OEERP, showing enhanced target detection accuracy, energy efficiency, and overall network performance, and comparisons with existing protocols are provided through plotted results.

articleTitle: Artificial Ecosystem-Based Optimization for Solving the Multi-Objective Economic Emission Load Dispatch Problem with Wind-Solar-Thermal Integration and Uncertainty Handling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Thermal generating units have incorporated renewable energy sources, such solar and wind, to lower pollutant gas emissions and overall fuel costs. As a result, the incorporation of renewable sources such as wind energy makes the multi-objective EELD issue more complicated and non-linear. An Artificial Ecosystem-Based Optimization (AEO) method has been presented to address this issue by optimizing the wind-solar-thermal model's cost and emissions while accounting for uncertainty in the outputs of solar and wind power. Key components of the AEO algorithm, which draw inspiration from ecosystem dynamics, enable search agents to more quickly converge to global optima and successfully escape local optima. Two systems—one with 40 heat producing units and the other with 13—have been used to test the suggested method.

articleTitle: A PSO Tuned CNN Approach for Accurate Fault Detection in PV Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems are growing in popularity and are widely utilized in power systems to capture renewable energy. However, these systems remain susceptible to numerous defects caused by environmental variables, device lifespan, and failures in operation. The proposed system presents an effective methodology for fault diagnostics in PV-connected grid systems by combining Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The system utilizes data to monitor crucial factors like voltage, current, and other indicators of performance. This data is processed through acquisition and preprocessing stages, including normalization and structured transmission, to ensure effective analysis for further use in decision-making processes. The hybrid model employs PSO to optimize CNN hyperparameters, enhancing the network's ability to accurately detect and classify faults. In this work, Python software implemented to diagnose faults in PV systems, with the effectiveness of the proposed approach evaluated using a "Solar Panel Fault Detection Dataset". The results are evaluated to ensure accurate and making an accuracy of 93.36%, precision of 94%, recall of 95%, and an F1 score of 95% for maintaining the stability and efficiency of PV-connected grid systems.

articleTitle: Design of H-Shape Open Slot Loaded Dual Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for Internet of Things (IoT) and Fixed Satellite Service (FSS) Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper presents a dual band square shape microstrip patch antenna of overall size 40×40 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> consisting an open H-shape slot inside the patch. IE3D software is used to design and simulation of presented antenna using microstrip line feed. The dual band antenna resonates at 2.53 GHz and 3.96 GHz having return losses of −25.90 dB and −36.89 dB. Impedance bandwidth of 380 MHz (15.08%) and 480 MHz (12.12%) is obtained in lower and upper bands from frequency range 3.14 to 3.48 GHz and 4.77 to 5.37 GHz respectively. The presented antenna exhibits peak gain of 3.77 dB and 4.87 dB while antenna efficiency of 88.76% and 85.96% at operating frequencies 2.53 GHz and 3.96 GHz. Moreover, the VSWR value of antenna is 1.107 at 2.53 GHz and 1.029 at 3.96 GHz.
