The presented antenna of dual band characteristics is suitable for IoT in S-band and FSS (Fixed Satellite Service) in C-band applications.

articleTitle: Actor-Critic RL Approach to Stabilize Voltage in DC Microgrids for Linear, CPL, and PPL Load Profiles
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Voltage regulation is essential for stable and efficient operation in DC microgrids, especially under varying load conditions, including pulsed power loads (PPL) and constant power loads (CPL). Nonlinear and dynamic load profiles cause significant voltage fluctuations, challenging the performance of conventional control techniques. This paper introduces an Actor-Critic reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach combined with a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller to enhance voltage regulation in DC microgrids. The proposed method dynamically adjusts the duty cycle of DC-DC converters, minimizing voltage variations and ensuring smooth transitions. Simulation results, validated through MATLAB Simulink, demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over traditional PI controllers. For PPL conditions, the approach achieves a 60% reduction in voltage dip, 50% faster recovery time, and improved damping. Under CPL scenarios, voltage variation is reduced by 57%, steady-state error decreases by 57%, and power quality is enhanced with stable performance. During additional PPL events, the voltage spike is reduced by 55%, settling time improves by 52%, and overall system stability is significantly enhanced. These findings highlight the robustness and adaptability of the proposed hybrid Actor-Critic RL framework in addressing the challenges posed by nonlinear and dynamic load variations in DC microgrids, offering a practical solution for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Image-based DeepFake Detection Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The increasing sophistication of deepfake technology poses significant risks to privacy, security, and public trust in digital media. As a result, deepfake detection has become a critical research area, with artificial intelligence -driven approaches playing a central role. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of convolutional neural network -based deepfake detection methods, highlighting key challenges such as dataset limitations, social media compression effects, real-time detection constraints, and the rapid evolution of manipulation techniques. While existing detection models demonstrate promising accuracy, challenges remain in terms of generalizability, computational efficiency, and robustness against complex manipulations, including audio and full-body deepfakes. This study explores strategies to enhance detection performance through data augmentation and optimized architectural design. Furthermore, it discusses potential future directions, such as leveraging multimodal analysis, federated learning, and explainable AI, to improve the reliability and adaptability of deepfake detection systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Text-to-Video Retrieval Using Clip Based Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Text-to-video retrieval is an essential task in multimedia information retrieval, enabling users to search and retrieve videos based on natural language descriptions. In this paper, we explore a deep learning approach leveraging the CLIP model for feature extraction and retrieval on the MSR-VTT dataset. We sample video frames and extract joint visual and textual embeddings using attention-based fusion and L2 normalization. Our basic model achieves Recall@1 of 13.96%, Recall@5 of 28.63%, Recall@10 of 36.40%, and Recall@50 of 57.12%, with a Median Rank (MdR) of 30 and a Mean Rank (MnR) of 406.75. We further discuss limitations and propose improvements such as multi-modal fusion, fine-tuning of the CLIP model, and advanced attention mechanisms. Our findings are compared against state-of-the-art methods, highlighting both progress and remaining challenges.

articleTitle: Hybrid Machine Learning Approach using Wingbeat Frequencies for Mosquito Species Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Many of life-threatening diseases such as malaria, dengue and Zika virus are vectors through mosquitoes. Three or four effective mosquito species must be identified to monitor and control their spread. In this study, we propose a hybrid model for classifying the mosquitoes based on their wingbeat frequencies using advanced deep learning techniques for monitoring and controlling their spread. This study proposes a hybrid approach for mosquito species classification based on their wingbeat frequencies, leveraging advanced deep learning techniques. We employ the Xception, a state of art deep learning architecture for feature extraction with classification using XGBoost, a strong ensemble learning algorithm. An accuracy of 95.41% is achieved on a comprehensive dataset of mosquito wingbeat recordings when the proposed model is evaluated. This hybrid approach achieves the feature extraction power of Xception and the predictive abilities of XGBoost and outperforms traditional models and single algorithm approaches. Such models are shown to be feasible in the deployment for real world vector monitoring and disease prevention initiatives with the high accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Low Power Energy Efficient 14T Hybrid Full Adder for Multiplier Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Since long, there is a rapid rise in energy-efficient appliances like electronics gadgets and microchip devices like health monitor wearable’s etc. The increased use of mentioned devices is built up via engineers to perform enhancement of the different type of circuits. Circuit with high efficiency, low power consumption and good speed having less chip-area have been explored. Full adder is a primary component that is used in arithmetic circuits, which shows a key role in present digital signal processing system. Some of arithmetic circuits are integrators, comparators, multipliers etc. Important thing of this device is, it’s a main part of the recent communication systems and complex path of many network circuits. Therefore, optimizing its performance in early stages enhances the system's overall performance with high efficiency and greater accuracy. Reducing transistor count can often lead to a decrease in processing speed or computational power. The Cadence Virtuoso tool in the study simulates this adder circuit at 0.8v–1.2v VDD using 90 nano meter CMOS technology, with a comparatively short delay and the average consumption of power for a 0.9 V supply was remarkably low. The current method proved to be more efficient than existing hybrid designs.

articleTitle: Detection of False Data Injection Attacks in Power Grids Based on Spatiotemporal Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With the development of new power systems, fast and accurate detection of False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA) is crucial for the secure operation of power grids. Existing FDIA detection models based on spatiotemporal correlations have poor feature extraction capabilities and suffer from feature shift, facing the issue of disrupted inherent spatiotemporal correlations in measurement data. To address this, we propose a detection model based on adaptive fusion of spatiotemporal features. First, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) is used to extract static spatial features from the power grid topology, while Graph Attention Networks (GAT) captures the dynamic spatial features. Next, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is employed to analyze the temporal variations and extract temporal features. Finally, the extracted spatiotemporal information is projected into feature space for alignment, and feature fusion is performed using a bilinear attention mechanism. The fused features are then used for FDIA detection. Experimental results show that, compared to existing detection models, the proposed model performs better in terms of detection accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Characterization and Statistical Analysis of Beer Produced by Bacterial Strains Isolated from Traditional Fermented Foods of Northeast India
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Beer fermentation is a multifaceted biochemical process influenced by microbial activity, with yeasts and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) playing pivotal roles in determining its sensory attributes. This study aims to isolate and characterize LAB strains from traditional fermented foods of Northeast India and evaluate their potential in enhancing the sensory properties of beer. A total of 41 LAB strains were isolated and subjected to biochemical characterization, including proteolytic, lipolytic, and carbohydrate fermentation assays. Non-pathogenic strains (B/4, Chuwan/YEPD/1, HTK/5, Khorisa/NA/3, NAP/2, NGA/5, NGA/6, Soibum/NA/3, TL/2, TL/4, TL/5 and TL/6) exhibiting favorable metabolic activities were selected for beer fermentation using a rice-based substrate. Sensory evaluation was conducted by a trained panel to assess attributes such as aroma, flavor, mouthfeel, and overall acceptability. Statistical analyses, including the Friedman and Nemenyi tests, revealed significant variations in the sensory profiles of beer samples produced by different LAB strains. Notably, the strains (B/4, Chuwan/YEPD/1, HTK/5, Khorisa/NA/3, NAP/2, NGA/5, NGA/6 and TL/2) imparted distinctive aroma and flavor, indicating its potential application in specialty beer production. These findings underscore the role of LAB in modulating beer characteristics and offer valuable insights for the development of innovative, naturally fermented beverages. These findings highlight the potential application of LAB strains in specialty beer production, emphasizing their role in enhancing sensory appeal. While the study confirms LAB’s viability in small-scale brewing, further research involving large-scale trials and advanced metabolomic analyses is recommended to assess their full industrial potential. This study provides valuable insights into the use of indigenous LAB strains for developing innovative, naturally fermented beverages.

articleTitle: Plant Disease Detection with Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Overseeing plant leaf diseases is vital for sustaining crop health, preventing extensive agricultural losses, safeguarding farmers livelihoods and ensuring a stable food supply. The health of the plant leaf is severely harmed by diseases such as early and late blight. Detecting leaf diseases is a time-consuming operation, and many farmers lack understanding about it, resulting in crop failure. Thus, early disease detection is crucial since it affects the quality and quantity of the potatoes. A type of artificial intelligence called deep learning has many uses in several domains and enables accurate and efficient data processing and decision-making. In this study, Leaf illnesses like early blight and late blight are detected and predicted using DL architectures like MobileNetV2, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0. A comprehensive dataset is employed, containing images of healthy and infected leaves, which aids in model training and evaluation. The results show that MobileNetV2 achieves the highest accuracy of 91% in identifying leaf diseases.

articleTitle: Accelerated MR image reconstruction using non convex regularized non-subsampled Contourlet transform and total variation based prior
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In the domain of compressive sensing MRI (CSMRI), MRI image is reconstructed using partially acquired k-space data, in order to shorten the acquisition time of MRI. Various priors and their combinations have been examined for compressive sensing MRI application. In this paper, we propose a CS-MRI method comprised of the combination of non convex regularized non-subsampled contourlet transform (NSCT) based sparsity and hybrid total variation as a prior. The NSCT captures multi-directional and multi-scale image features effectively, while hybrid total variation preserves edges better while suppressing artifacts. The non conex regularization provides better measure of sparseness and preserve structural details better compared to convex regularization. Alternating direction method of multipliers is used to solve the proposed method. The experimental results of the proposed method are analyzed for different under-sampling patterns.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence Algorithms in Personalized Design of Visual Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Based on the problems of insufficient design innovation and low design efficiency in personalized visual communication design, this study uses the style transfer algorithm to apply a specific artistic style to the design and automatically generates visual elements with personalized characteristics. At the same time, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) are used to create new patterns and color combinations and enhance the diversity of design, while ChatGPT is used to parse user needs and transform text descriptions into design concepts. In the process of implementing these methods, this paper collects and analyzes user data to build user portraits to understand their preferences and needs. This paper also uses a style transfer algorithm to combine user-favorite elements with design templates to generate preliminary design sketches. Then GAN intervenes to generate new design elements and uses these elements to enrich and refine the design content. During the design process, the artificial intelligence model is continuously optimized based on user feedback to ensure that the final output design not only meets the user's personalized needs but is also highly innovative and attractive. Ultimately, these individually adjusted designs are output in an appropriate format for application in actual products or services. Based on comparative experiments, this paper found that personalized design is superior to traditional design methods in multiple key indicators: the average innovation score of personalized design is as high as 9.06, higher than the 6.89 of traditional design; the time required for personalized design is mainly concentrated between 20 and 30 minutes, while the time required for traditional design ranges from 30 to nearly 50 minutes and fluctuates greatly; the adoption rate of personalized design reaches a minimum of 90.2% and a maximum of 99.9%, while the adoption rate of traditional design is lower, with a minimum of only 75.2% and a maximum of only 88.7%. Through comparative analysis, this paper confirms the advantages of personalized design over traditional design in multiple dimensions, and demonstrates the application potential and value of artificial intelligence technology in the field of design.

articleTitle: Advanced Fake News Detection: Multi-Lingual Analysis and Image Forgery Detection Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The advent of the internet has brought about both positive changes and some critical issues. One critical issue is the spread of fake news, which leads to misinterpretation of events, threats to social integrity, and just gives rise to chaos. To tackle this problem, an efficient system is required which can detect fake news effectively. The proposed system introduces a multi-functional fake news detection system. The system makes the use of Gradient Boosting Classifier and Decision Tree Classifier algorithms to predict the authenticity of textual news articles with high accuracy. Furthermore, it integrates a novel feature to analyze the authenticity of images accompanying news articles, using Error Level Analysis (ELA) combined with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to detect signs of image forgery. To enhance versatility and to reduce linguistic challenges, the system can analyze and classifying news articles in both English and Hindi, addressing the diversity of a country like India. The implementation involves preprocessing, feature extraction, and model training, ensuring reliability and robustness. This work contributes to the development of a comprehensive tool that can effectively classify text and images for authenticity, making it a valuable resource in combating the spread of fake news.

articleTitle: Analyzing Network Traffic Features for IoT Malware Detection through Forensic Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This emerges as an issue given that the rapid proliferation of IoT (Internet of Things) devices came alongside several security issues in which IoT malware became an issue of interest in this regard. Due to the fact that IoT devices are of different kinds then their network interaction is also not uniform hence this work proposes a new approach for detecting IoT malware using forensic methods that analyze network traffic features. The focus of the study will be on the network traffic patterns (data flow, packet characteristics and communication protocols) in order to identify anomalous behaviors which are likely to contain malicious activity. Forensic analysis techniques are applied on network logs to build up a picture of what attack scenarios might look like and where suspicious traffic is coming from. Statistical and machine learning methods are applied at an advanced level to classify traffic as normal or abnormal in order to improve detection accuracy. This approach provides a non-intrusive and scalable solution for real-time detection of IoT malware without exposing vulnerable IoT ecosystems to emerging threats.

articleTitle: AI – Driven Marine Debris Detection for Ocean Conservation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Marine debris is a growing environmental crisis that impacts marine ecosystem's biodiversity and human livelihoods. Oceans are flooded with waste like plastics, due to improper disposal, illegal dumping, and limited waste management infrastructure. Traditional methods of detecting and managing marine debris, such as manual surveys or trawler-based cleanups, are labour-intensive, costly, and inefficient for large-scale application. With growing urgency, there is a need for scalable, automated solutions that can monitor vast oceanic areas and provide insights for debris mitigation. To overcome these challenges, we have introduced an advanced system utilizing the YOLOv8 deep learning model which is trained to detect debris under challenging underwater conditions, including low visibility and varying light levels. By leveraging cutting-edge object detection techniques, the system identifies and classifies various debris types from underwater images with high accuracy. The project begins with data collection, representing an extensive dataset of diverse debris categories. Evaluation metrics like precision, recall, and F1 score demonstrate the model's efficiency in identifying debris while minimizing false positives. This model can decrease the intensive labour process and increase the efficiency for large scale applications. This research advances marine debris management through deep learning, promoting sustainable ocean practices and contributing to global environmental health. Future work involves extending the system's capabilities to detect microplastics and integrating it with real-time response systems for effective cleanup operations.

articleTitle: A Hybrid CNN-SVM Approach for Skin Lesion Classification Using The ISIC 2019 Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Identifying skin lesions accurately is necessary for immediate diagnosis of skin cancer, particularly melanoma, which can significantly reduce mortality rates. However, automating the categorization of skin lesions poses challenges due to subtle variations in their appearance on the skin. This article presents a hybrid approach that combines Support Vector Machines (SVM) for categorization with Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) for feature extraction. Random Forest (RF) and Decision Tree (DT) methods are also included for comparative analysis. Using ISIC 2019 dataset encompassing dermoscopic images, the evaluation results show that the CNN-SVM hybrid paradigm surpasses other classifiers for accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Experimental findings indicate performance improvements of 3.6% and 6.9% for CNN-SVM model compared to the CNN-RF and CNN-DT models, respectively. These results emphasize the ability of hybrid methods to enhance classification efficiency for medical image analysis tasks.

articleTitle: CA-Unet: Cascaded Attention Transformer for Underwater Image Deblurring and Color Restoration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The absorption and scattering of light in water result in low-quality photographs being captured underwater. This degradation hampers analysis in fields such as marine biology. To address this, we propose a novel deep-learning model that utilizes a Cascaded Attention Transformer for underwater image enhancement (CA-Unet). The central component of CA-Unet, the Residual Cascaded Attention Block (RCAB), employs various attention techniques to capture both local and global dependencies while extracting deep and superficial features. This approach effectively recovers lost details in underwater scenes, enhances contrast, reduces color cast, and restores image quality. Compared to other methods, our model demonstrates superior performance on both synthetic and real-world underwater photos, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Exploring Advanced Optimized Machine Learning Frameworks for Enhanced Analysis and Predictive Modeling of Drilling Well Production Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The oil and gas industry is increasingly depending on advanced data analytics to maximize production and reduce costs. Perhaps the greatest difficult issue in this industry is precisely estimating the performance of drilling wells to improve decision-making processes. This paper provides ML techniques for predicting drilling well production using ensemble learning. To develop an accurate prediction system, the framework includes Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), data preprocessing, visualization, optimization, and model selection. In this work, combining RF with XGBoost aims to improve predictive performance through utilizing the capabilities of both algorithms. Firefly Optimization is utilized to tune hyperparameters in the hybrid model-building process. This hybrid model is specifically intended for error prediction in firefly optimization scenarios. The approach is developed in Python software and exhibits the real-world application of advanced ML techniques in industrial conditions. The proposed hybrid RF-XGBoost model exceeds in terms of error predicting for drilling well production, with an RMSE of 0.01, MAE of 0.01, and MSE of 0.10. The results indicate the approach is effectively accurate in predicting errors in complex data settings, providing insights that have a significant effect on operational decisions in the field of well data management.

articleTitle: Automatic Optimization of Trading Strategies Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: At present, investment transactions in domestic financial markets are gradually shifting from subjective transactions relying on traditional technical analysis to programmatic quantitative strategy transactions. Although a large number of quantitative strategies have been studied in the stock market, there is still insufficient research on quantitative trading strategies in the futures market, and there is still room for improvement in the investment return and risk control of existing strategies in intraday high-frequency trading. In order to improve the profitability and risk management of the high-frequency quantitative strategy of futures, this paper designs a futures trading environment, uses the 1-minute granularity of high-frequency K-line as the environmental state, and constructs the position state and the action space and algorithm of trading operations suitable for futures trading. Lstm-dueling DQN, a deep reinforcement learning model based on LSTM, is adopted to better deal with the state space of sequence input and significantly accelerate the learning speed of the model. Through the experimental comparison of three benchmark models DQN, Double DQN and Dueling DQN (FF-Dueling DQN) based on fully connected neural network, the results show that the cumulative return rate of the proposed strategy in the trading of four black series commodity futures can reach 43%, and the annual return rate can reach 153%. The maximum retracement was controlled within 10.7%. The experimental results show that this strategy can achieve excess returns beyond the performance benchmark in both volatile and trend markets.

articleTitle: sEMG Signal Acquisition: of Hand Movements for Feature Extraction and Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper explores the classification of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals for hand movement recognition using time and frequency domain features used for feature extraction. Three hand movements were recorded from four healthy subjects for signal analysis achieving an SNR range of 14.81dB to 23.14dB. Two machine learning classifiers, medium neural network (MNN) and cubic support vector machine (CSVM), were evaluated to determine their effectiveness performance. MNN achieved the highest accuracy of 93.8%, demonstrating robust feature separation, while CSVM provided a simpler but slightly less precise result at 92.5%. The findings underscore the potential of MNN in classification of hand movements and aids on the development of advanced prosthetic control systems.

articleTitle: Computer Animation Interaction Design Driven by Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Computer animation interaction design in traditional research has a single user experience and cannot adapt to personalized needs due to problems such as disconnection between animation and user interaction, insufficient intelligent recognition ability, and poor real-time response. This article uses a design method driven by a neural network algorithm to achieve a deep integration of animation and interaction, and improve the naturalness, fluency and real-time performance of animation. In the study, GAN (Generative Adversarial Network) is used to generate natural and smooth animation movements, and CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) is used to analyze users’ facial expressions and voices. LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) is used to process users’ time series data; RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) is responsible for real-time analysis of users’ dynamic input and generating instant animation feedback; TCN (Temporal Convolutional Network) optimizes the system’s real-time feedback mechanism and improves the response accuracy and speed to continuous input. Compared with the FSM (Finite State Machine) and BT (Behavior Tree) methods, the maximum response time of this method is 0.174s; the DTW (Dynamic Time Warping) distance value is between 0.136 and 0.402; the maximum Euclidean distance is 0.416. Experimental results show that through the combination of these algorithms, the system can generate personalized animation feedback according to the user’s real-time input, emotional state and behavioral characteristics, significantly improving the naturalness, fluency, real-time and personalized response capabilities of the animation, and providing a more intelligent, natural and immersive interactive experience.

articleTitle: Sensor Data Fusion and Motion Status Monitoring in Smart Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In view of the limitations of traditional motion monitoring methods in data accuracy and real-time performance, this study introduces multi-sensor data fusion technology to improve the accuracy and reliability of motion state monitoring. By fusing the data of accelerometer, gyroscope and heart rate sensor in real time, the user's motion state can be analyzed more comprehensively, providing more accurate health analysis and feedback. First, this paper designs a sensor data fusion framework based on Kalman filtering, which fuses the data of accelerometer, gyroscope and heart rate sensor. Through the Kalman filtering algorithm, this paper can reduce the impact of sensor error on motion state detection while ensuring computational efficiency. Secondly, the support vector machine (SVM) is used to classify and analyze the fused data, and the user's motion type (such as gait, running, cycling, etc.) is extracted based on time series features. Finally, in order to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm, this paper collects sensor data of different users in different motion states and evaluates the performance of the system in multiple scenarios. In a static environment, the recognition accuracy of walking and running is generally high, with the walking recognition rate of user 1 being 96.54% and the running recognition rate being 94.17%. The walking recognition rate of user 2 reaches 98.31%, and the running recognition rate reaches 95.04%. This study proposes a new motion state monitoring method through multi-sensor data fusion technology, which significantly improves the accuracy and real-time performance of motion monitoring. This method provides strong technical support for the application of smart wearable devices in health management and sports tracking.

articleTitle: Hybrid Power Conversion System Using PWM Rectification and Advanced Bidirectional DC-DC Control for Efficient Load Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The increasing demand for efficient energy conversion and management in various applications has spurred significant advancements in power electronics. To address these needs, the proposed system employs the Advanced Hybrid Power Conversion System (AHPCS), which integrates Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) rectification and bidirectional DC-DC control. Hence, this paper proposes a power conversion topology that utilizing PWM control for efficient energy transfer, providing an efficient and consistent power conversion solutions. The system architecture consists of multiple stages, such as single-phase PWM rectifier, high-frequency inverter, LC tank, a transformer and synchronous rectifier which work together for utilizing isolated power and deliver a stable DC output to the load. Additionally, a bidirectional DC-DC converter is linked to a battery, enabling energy storage and retrieval for enhanced flexibility in power management. The simulation results performed with MATLAB Simulink indicate the system's capability of handling high power density applications and maintaining efficient energy storage integration and isolation.

articleTitle: Indoor Sound Classification Using Lightweight CNN with Real-Time IoT Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for indoor sound classification, specifically designed to identify ten distinct classes: knock on the door, mouse click, keyboard typing, wooden door squeaks, opening the can, washing machine, vacuum cleaner, alarm clock, clock ticking, and broken glass from [1]. The sound signals were captured using a microphone and transformed from the time domain to time-frequency images through Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT). The proposed CNN, with a compact model size of 2.1 MB, was benchmarked against several well-known pre-trained models, including DenseNet, EfficientNet, InceptionNet, MobileNet, NASNet, ResNet, VGGNet, and Xception. Experimental results demonstrate that our lightweight CNN significantly outperformed these models, achieving a validation accuracy of 80% in a ten-fold cross-validation framework. The best performance among the pre-trained models was observed with ResNet101V2, which achieved only 62% validation accuracy in a ten-fold cross-validation framework with a considerably larger model size of 163 MB. Furthermore, the proposed model was successfully deployed in real-time on various IoT and processor modules, including the Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA A100, Tesla V100, and Intel Xeon Platinum, where it demonstrated superior efficiency, running at just 35 milliseconds per inference on the Raspberry Pi edge device. The lightweight CNN’s high accuracy and low latency make it an ideal candidate for applications in smart home systems, security monitoring, and real-time audio event detection on resource-constrained devices.

articleTitle: An Exploration of GAN Applications in Stock Prediction through Bibliometric Analysis and Co-occurrence Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Predicting the stock market has become a global problem in recent years, requiring massive scientific study. In this study, bibliometric investigation was performed to comprehend a essential outlook and help academics recognize the features of stock market prediction. In light of the aforementioned research, this article concludes with some discussions regarding the upcoming challenges of stock market prediction. With a focus on its many approaches, this article provides a detailed introduction to bibliometric methodology. Additionally, it offers a set of trustworthy, detailed directions for carrying out bibliometric analysis with assurance. Additionally, this study looks into the appropriate application of bibliometric analysis as a substitute for systematic literature reviews. Concretely, it provides a thorough overview of the field of stock market prediction using GAN in terms of the number of regular publications produced, the primary focus of stock market prediction researchers, the most influential nations (authors, institutions, and sources), and intriguing research avenues in this area. The evolution of stock market prediction using GAN is objectively understood in this study, which also serves as a useful reference for academics and researchers in the fields of technology, management, and economics.

articleTitle: Depression Detection on Social Media Posts Using BERT and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Depression is a growing mental health challenge, affecting countless individuals worldwide. As people increasingly express their mental states on social media platforms like Twitter and Reddit, there is an opportunity to leverage this data to identify signs of depression. This study investigates the potential of social media text for detecting depression using machine learning techniques. We used Kaggle-sourced Twitter and Reddit datasets, each containing labeled samples of depressive and non-depressive content. After extensive preprocessing such as text cleaning, tokenization, and BERT embedding generation we trained Support Vector Machine (SVM) models with various kernel functions. Our results show Twitter data significantly enhances model performance, achieving 94.4% accuracy with the polynomial kernel while 87.5% on twitter dataset with Radial basis function (RBF). These findings underscore the potential for accurate depression detection, suggesting its value for early intervention and use of social media data for depression detection.

articleTitle: Intelligent Anti-Theft System with Automated Spray Control using ESP32 WROOM
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This project demonstrates a low-cost anti-theft solution built around the ESP32-WROOM microcontroller, with integrated chemical spray for security. The system is designed to detect unauthorized entry and respond with spraying disinfectant chemicals such as pepper spray, thus ensuring security as well as being effective against attackers. The ESP32-WROOM microcontroller is known for its Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities, which plays a key role in providing real-time monitoring and control. Users can also access the system via mobile or web applications. In case of any abnormal situation, the user will be notified immediately. This hospitality provides a living environment for its users. Therefore, they can move with peace of mind and even safeguard their valuable things from anywhere. This system also has a modular design that saves energy for easy installation and is suitable for residential, small business and commercial environments.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Advance Body Worn Antenna with Optimized Return loss and Bandwidth using Python in the application of Wi-Fi 6E and IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In this paper, a proposed advanced body worn antenna of half circular ring of thickness 6 mm is placed on a jeans substrate of dimension 80×80×1.0 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with a defected ground plane of dimension 32×80×0.035 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Now after simulating using CST software, the return loss, resonant frequency, bandwidth and gain are optimized with feed position and ground length using Python and then we get optimized return loss of 38 dB and 6.01 GHz resonance frequency with a bandwidth of 2 GHz band from 6.09 to 8.09 GHz and gain of 11 dBi used in the application of Wi-Fi 6E and IoT.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy Transition and Population Dynamics: Data-Driven Approach to Mitigating Greenhouse Gas Emissions in BRICS Nations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Natural resource overuse has had detrimental effects on the ecosystem, especially in the form of rising Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions. This problem is made worse by excessive extraction of energy resources and fast population increase. Using a data-driven methodology, this paper examines the dynamic link between GHG emissions, population growth, and primary energy use in the BRICS countries. E-Views 9 software's Unit Root Tests, regression analysis, and Johansen-Fisher Panel Cointegration techniques are used to examine secondary data. The empirical results highlight the urgent need for a shift to sustainable energy systems by establishing a strong long-run equilibrium relationship among these variables. In order to slow down environmental deterioration, the report promotes the use of renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, biomass, hydropower, geothermal, tidal, wave, & biofuels. The findings give policymakers practical advice by highlighting the need to incorporate sustainable energy measures in order to attain carbon neutrality while maintaining economic growth and resource efficiency, especially in highly populous nations like China and India.

articleTitle: Design of Energy-Saving Optimization Algorithm for Power Electronic Devices in Railway Electrification System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the scale of railway electrification systems, the proportion of power electronic devices in energy consumption has increased significantly, and effective energy-saving optimization strategies are urgently needed to improve the overall efficiency of the system. To address this problem, this paper designs an energy-saving optimization scheme based on a hybrid optimization algorithm. First, an energy consumption model of power electronic devices in railway electrification systems is established to accurately describe the energy conversion and loss mechanism of each component. Then, a hybrid optimization algorithm is developed by combining genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) to fully utilize the advantages of both in global search and local search. Finally, by introducing a multi-objective optimization method, the energy-saving effect and system stability are balanced to ensure that the various requirements of the optimization process are met. In the experimental conclusion, the optimized configuration saves a total of about 6594.1 kWh of electricity in a 24-hour operation cycle, with an average energy saving of about 270 kWh per hour. In addition, the optimized configuration performs well in terms of system reliability. However, the stability of the optimized configuration in terms of load fluctuation and voltage fluctuation is slightly reduced. In the above conclusions, the proposed hybrid optimization algorithm performs outstandingly in terms of energy saving and reliability, providing effective technical support for the optimization of railway electrification systems. However, further optimization is still needed in terms of system stability.

articleTitle: MinerGenesis: Integrated Well-being and Environmental Surveillance for Mining Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The mining industry operates in dynamic and high-stakes environments, requiring robust systems to monitor worker health and ensure operational safety. It plays a crucial role in the global economy, supplying essential raw materials for construction, manufacturing, and energy production. The mining industry faces critical problems in ensuring worker health and safety due to hazardous environments, exposure to toxic gases, and a lack of real-time monitoring systems. Miners are often exposed to life-threatening conditions without real-time mechanisms to detect or mitigate risks. A health monitoring system has been designed that leverages wearable IoT devices and blockchain technology. The system employs sensors to continuously monitor vital signs such as heart rate and body temperature, along with environmental parameters like toxic gas concentrations. Real-time data transmission via LoRaWAN ensures immediate detection and alerting of abnormal conditions, enabling timely interventions. Blockchain technology secures the collected data, providing tamper-proof records and fostering trust among stakeholders. The wearable devices are optimized for durability, comfort, and minimal disruption to miners' activities. the system includes emergency alert features for accidents, ensuring prompt response and enhanced safety measures. By integrating advanced technologies, the solution aims to improve safety standards and promote proactive health management within the mining industry.

articleTitle: Detection of Brain Tumors from MRI scans using Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The diagnosis of brain tumors dominates the medical sector and great accuracy along with efficiency in their methods to detect the tumor is required. The ability to diagnose brain cancers from MRI data has been greatly aided by recent developments in computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems. Recent years have seen improvements in approaches used, for instance with CNN or tumor images being automated. In this work was proposed a model that is based on deep learning using Inception-V3 for the classification and localization of brain tumors. Our model was validated on a publicly available dataset and it was shown that the proposed model is accurate and robust in distinguishing among different kinds of brain tumors. The paper also addresses issues such as data imbalance and model interpretability and the feasibility of integrating the system to be used clinically for real time applications.

articleTitle: Optimization Control of HVAC System and Building Energy Management Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper discusses the optimal control and building energy management of building heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) systems based on deep Q networks (DQNs). Traditional control strategies often have difficulty adapting to the dynamic changes of the environment and the personalized needs of users. This paper studies a DQN algorithm based on reinforcement learning to learn the optimal control strategy through interaction with the environment to achieve the best balance between energy saving and comfort. First, the HVAC system is modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP), including three elements: state, action, and reward. Then, a DQN model is designed and implemented to improve the efficiency and stability of learning through experience replay and target network. Experience replay reduces the correlation between samples by randomly sampling past experience, while the target network reduces the oscillation during training by stabilizing the estimation of Q values. Finally, the application effect of DQN in HVAC system control is verified by verification. The specific data of the experimental results show that DQN performs well in energy efficiency. In terms of response speed, the response time of DQN to indoor and outdoor temperature fluctuations is 64.4 seconds, which is significantly faster than other traditional methods. In the adaptability score, DQN's highest adaptability score can reach 91.1 points. The DQN algorithm has significant advantages in HVAC system optimization control and building energy consumption management, and can achieve lower energy consumption and higher control accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of Blockchain Technology Based on Ring Signature in Intelligent Referral System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In response to the data leakage risks and inefficient referral process in the intelligent referral system, this paper proposes a solution that combines ring signatures and smart contracts. The solution protects patient privacy through ring signature technology, while leveraging the immutability and transparency of blockchain to improve the efficiency and security of the referral process. This paper first applies ring signature technology to ensure the anonymity of patient data, and then builds a blockchain-based platform for storing and sharing medical data. This paper uses the distributed ledger technology of blockchain to ensure that data cannot be tampered with once it is uploaded to the chain, and then integrates smart contracts to automate the referral process, reduce human intervention, and improve the efficiency of referrals. The experiment found that the average leakage rate of the experimental group was 0.084%, which was much lower than the 0.23% of the control group, showing the advantages of ring signature technology in preventing data leakage. In addition, the referral time of the experimental group was generally lower than that of the control group. In terms of the number of unauthorized accesses and patient satisfaction, the experimental group showed better performance than the control group. The maximum number of unauthorized accesses was 2 times, while the maximum number in the control group was 22 times. The patient satisfaction rate in the experimental group was as low as 88% and as high as 99%, while that in the control group was between 58% and 78%. Based on the above data, this paper finds that the intelligent referral system based on ring signature is superior to the traditional referral system in terms of data protection and referral efficiency, has higher security and reliability, and can provide patients with safer and more efficient referral services.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Quad-band Slotted Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: A compact quad-band slotted patch antenna with an octagonal design, measuring 27.5 mm × 22 mm × 1.6 mm, is implemented and analysed for its efficiency across multiple resonating characteristics. This antenna is optimized for four operating modes, supporting tetra wireless standards. Proposed design achieved S-band WLAN (2.4 GHz – IEEE 802.16b), C-band WLAN (5.0 GHz – IEEE 802.11j, 5.8 GHz – IEEE 802.11a), 5G NR bands (n40: 2.3–2.4 GHz, n46: 5.15–5.925 GHz, n47: 5.855–5.925 GHz, n96: 5.925–7.125 GHz, n102: 5.925–6.425 GHz, n104: 6.425–7.125 GHz), X-band (8–12 GHz for radar, space communication, and broadband), lower Ku-band (13.64–15.72 GHz for satellite communication), and upper Ku-band (16.32–17.24 GHz for molecular rotational spectroscopy) wireless communication applications. Proposed structure features an octagonal slotted radiating patch with double duplications and a trapezoidal partial ground part, designed on an FR-4 substrate material. Simulated results confirm its performance, showcasing favourable return loss, radiation patterns, gain, and efficiency across the targeted bands, with stable operation across the antenna’s resonating modes.

articleTitle: Video Trailer Generation using Multimodal Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Trailers have been a vital part of the entertainment industry to pique audience interest. The process of trailer generation has been evolving to provide effective trailers to the public. In this paper we propose a novel approach by utilizing the audio and video modalities to extract key trailer segments that are compiled to create an effective trailer which highlights the impactful scenes of the short film. In contrast to previous work in this domain, the novel approach gives greater emphasis to the auditory features, since auditory features have a significant impact on the film in the horror genre. The dataset is a compilation of 311 short films and their respective trailers from various reputable public sources. Our approach introduces an audio guided visual model that compliments the acoustic features ensuring that the extracted segments are key moments both in terms of audio and video. The results obtained indicate that a significant proportion of predicted segments are deemed highly trailer-worthy.

articleTitle: Benchmarking SDN Controllers: Performance Analysis of POX and Floodlight in DCell Data Centre Topology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This study presents a comparative performance analysis of two SDN (Software Defined Networking) controllers, POX and Floodlight in a DCell data centre architecture. Using a simulated Mininet environment, the investigation measures critical network performance indicators namely round-trip time (RTT), latency, jitter and throughput. The scalability and resource utilization of both the controllers under varying traffic condition has also been examined. The findings shows that POX achieves lower latency, reduced RTT and better throughput making it preferable for time-sensitive applications. Whereas, Floodlight delivers more stability in jitter. The outcomes provide insights for optimizing controller selection in data centre deployments.

articleTitle: Deep Learning with Self-Attention Mechanisms for Parkinson’s Disease Classification Through MRI images
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder affecting millions globally, characterized by the progressive loss of dopamine-producing neurons in the brain. Advanced machine learning and deep learning approaches, combined with medical imaging, have become instrumental in diagnosing PD. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), particularly T1-weighted scans, has proven effective in detecting structural brain changes linked to dopamine deficiency, making it a critical tool for PD diagnosis. This study focuses on developing and evaluating robust convolutional neural networks (CNNs) integrated with a self-attention mechanism for enhanced feature extraction and accurate PD classification. A Random Forest (RF) classifier differentiates PD patients and healthy controls (HC). The proposed approach achieves superior performance, with an accuracy of 95.78%, a sensitivity of 96%, and a specificity of 96%. This model outperforms other advanced techniques, making it a reliable tool for accurate diagnosis of PD and a helpful aid for neurologists in making clinical decisions.

articleTitle: A Domain-Aware Data Fusion Scheme for Cold Start Problem in Early-Stage IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In recent years, edge computing has become increasingly popular, and edge intelligence is one of the key components of this paradigm. However, in the early phases of deployment, edge-based models frequently face an issue called the “cold start problem” caused by insufficient data. To address this problem, this work presents a data fusion model based on the ideas of domain adaptation. The model first evaluates the degree of similarity between the learning methodology’s source and target domains. Then, it appropriately combines data from both sources to train the model efficiently and reduce the possibility of overfitting. A lot of testing has been done to evaluate the effectiveness of this suggested learning model using the Ganga River and Sangam datasets. Compared to the Target and Source-only models, the findings show a notable improvement, especially in accuracy, during the initial training period.

articleTitle: Sustainable Agriculture with Advanced Plant Disease Detection using YOLOv11 and XAI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: India has agriculture high on its list, but as plant diseases do not get noticed early enough, agricultural waste increases. This study proposes using XAI and leading computer vision algorithms to spot plant diseases in the right fashion. The work employs a YOLOv11 model especially trained using a Roboflow dataset that has used images from both PlantVillage and PlantDoc for the purpose of an agricultural context. Anchor-free detection as well as instance segmentation are catered to by its architecture. With the assistance of YOLOv11, it is applied to accurately classify 20 distinct disease types on several crops. For this application, each XAI-enhanced disease condition is described in simple terms, encompassing symptoms, possible causes, and treatments, especially for farmers with non-technical backgrounds. Since the mean Average Precision (mAP) for detecting diseases reaches as high as 97.5%, it proves that the studies showed robustness in the YOLOv11 model. This has further demonstrated the exceptional combination of high adaptability and high reliability, under a variety of environmental conditions, through graphical studies like Precision-Recall and Confidence Curve, with the model. It particularly indicates how this particular combination of YOLOv11 and XAI offers superb precision for scalable yet straightforward methods to address plant disease control.

articleTitle: Humanizing NPCs-AI Driven Realistic Conversations and Reactions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for developing advanced non-playable characters (NPCs) that utilize artificial intelligence (AI) to achieve realistic interactions in virtual environments made using Unreal Engine. NPCs often rely on defined behaviors and scripted responses, which limit immersion and also give the same experience for every user, but this approach integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) features and machine learning techniques to create NPCs capable of dynamic, conscious conversations that mimic human interaction to respond with emotional depth and adaptability making the experience unique for every user. By crafting a custom dataset that encapsulates distinct personality traits. Incorporating memory recall allows Non Playable Characters to learn from past interactions, enhancing their ability to provide personalized experiences over time. AI-driven NPCs significantly enhance user immersion by offering unique, evolving interactions tailored to individual players. This research not only advances the field of game development but also lays the framework for creating lifelike digital characters capable of enriching virtual narratives for game plots.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Time Series Models for Rainfall Prediction: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Rainfall variability plays a critical role in agriculture, water resources, and disaster management in India. This study focuses on the usage of a SARIMAX model to analyze and predict rainfall patterns while accounting for both non-seasonal and seasonal components. The model adequately captures seasonal variations, illustrating the relevance of incorporating seasonal factors into forecasting. However, the non-seasonal components did not considerably improve the model’s performance. Diagnostic tests demonstrate that the model handles autocorrelation satisfactorily; however, the residuals exhibit irregularities, as evidenced by skewness and large tails. While the model has fair prediction accuracy, the findings show areas for development, particularly in fine-tuning non-seasonal dynamics and eliminating residual abnormalities. This research emphasizes the importance of seasonality in rainfall forecasting and lays the framework for future model improvements. The study provides valuable information on rainfall patterns, supporting better planning and management

articleTitle: CropAI: Crop disease prediction and growth tracking using AI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Recognizing plant diseases is essential to maintaining a nation with a high level of agricultural development. A successful agricultural industry and the reduction of financial and other resource waste depend on the timely and productive discovery of plant diseases. Many illnesses can affect crops, causing farmers to lose more money every year. By detecting diseases in plant foliage early on, deep learning systems can greatly help farmers prevent crop failures. To identify crop illnesses, we tested the effectiveness of Convolutional Neural Network(CNN), VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 models using the 10,101 images of the Plant Village from the huge data records. The 98.60%, 92.99%, 97.85%, and 99.29% accuracy percentages attained for Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), ResNet50, VGG16, and VGG19, in that order. With a fidelity of 98.17%, the solution shows that the ResNet50 execute great results when compared to other models. The goal is to enable early diagnosis of plant diseases and provide prompt treatment to abet the farmers in preserving resources and minimal financial losses.

articleTitle: GMatchBERT: BERT-Enhanced Relation Learning for Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Learning the relations between two items is an important step in completing the knowledge graph. Knowledge graph completion typically requires numerous training examples for each relation to increase their coverage. In KGs, long-tail relations are more prevalent, and freshly inserted links generally don’t have enough training triplets. One-shot relation learning is a transformational approach in the field of knowledge graphs, tackling the issues given by data scarcity and the necessity for fast reasoning mechanisms. Existing one-shot relation learning approaches rely on embedding-based methods based on the continuous vector-space. This study proposes GMatchBERT, a one-shot relation learning method with BERT embedding. The approach uses information from BERT embeddings and integrates the embeddings with one-hop graph topologies to create a matching metric. Experiments on two sets of data show that our suggested framework surpasses the existing approach for one-shot relation learning.

articleTitle: Decentralised Cloud Architecture: Blockchain Driven Integrity and Raptor Codes for Enhanced Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Ensuring data integrity and security has become integral in the digital era. Blockchain, an immutable ledger can be leveraged to provide data integrity to the cloud system. Centralised cloud systems present challenges in data integrity, reliability and security due to single point of failure and control. The alternative decentralised approach distributes data across multiple nodes thus reducing reliance on one server. However, this can lead to issues like network congestion, difficulty verifying file integrity and origin of tampering. The proposed system uses a combination of decentralised cloud nodes, blockchain, and fountain codes to provide a robust, scalable and secure cloud solution. Blockchain is used to store hashes of the files and validate every operation ensuring transparency and integrity. To provide a robust data recovery and enhance reliability of communication amongst the nodes, fountain codes are utilised for data transmission.

articleTitle: Fair Price Prediction for Farmers: Leveraging Freshness of Perishable Goods Through Machine Learning and Sustainable Practices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Fresh produce enhances sales and promotes better health, whereas stale stock leads to financial losses and significant food wastage. Additionally, inefficiencies in the perishable food supply chain contribute to sustainability challenges. This study proposes a system that integrates freshness classification and fair pricing mechanisms to support farmers and mitigate waste. The approach employs the VGG16 model to classify produce as fresh or rotten, achieving 96.88% accuracy. Further freshness analysis is conducted using image processing techniques such as edge analysis with the Laplacian of Gaussian (LoG), texture analysis with Local Binary Patterns (LBP), and color analysis using the HSV model, yielding accuracies of 82%, 86%, and 87%, respectively. A computed freshness index enables shelf-life estimation, helping optimize inventory management and reduce waste. Additionally, a fair pricing model based on the freshness index ensures that farmers receive equitable compensation for their produce. The SARIMAX model, used for price prediction, achieves a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 28.18%. By linking freshness assessment with pricing, this framework incentivizes better agricultural practices, enhances efficiency, promotes sustainability, and minimizes environmental impact. The proposed system contributes to a resilient and eco-friendly perishable food supply chain, benefiting both farmers and consumers.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Metamaterial Microwave devices for High efficiency Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In this research work, a novel approach in the design and modeling of metamaterial-based microwave devices for improved bandwidth and efficiency for the next generation wireless technology; 5G and all subsequent generations is presented. The design combines SRRs and CSRRs to realize a prototype that resonates at 5.85 GHz with -22.9 dB of return loss and 93% efficiency of transmission. The simulation results presented in this work demonstrated an operation bandwidth of 780 MHz, which was three times higher than conventional designs. Microwave design was performed using CST Microwave Studio and HFSS, while the experimental characteristics were obtained using a vector network analyzer. This paper describes the methodology, instruments, and control factors for obtaining this level of performance and indicates possible areas of using high-speed data transfers and signal quality in 5G and subsequent networks.

articleTitle: Modelling Clinical and Radiographic Data for Early Detection and Prediction of Osteoarthritis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative disease in joint area that impacts the quality of life of people who face it. This chronic disease causes lifelong pain and affects mobility, thus causing lifelong suffering. The early detection and prediction of this disease can aid in timely treatment thus saving quality of life and reducing healthcare costs. Despite numerous researches, accurate early detection of this disease has always been a challenge in the medical field due to the complex and multifactorial nature of the disease. This research provides a comprehensive approach to the detection and prediction of OA by two different types of data: symptoms, clinical data embedded with radiological data and patient’s X-ray images of knee joints. By integrating diverse data, the model uses EfficientNetB3, a powerful Convolution Neural Network (CNN)-based algorithm for the X-ray image analysis and XGBoost and a Deep Learning approach for analyzing clinical data which is diverse and has a wide spectrum of clinical fields for analysis. The EfficientNetB3 achieves an accuracy of 95.2% for detecting the presence of OA and accuracy of 84% for grading the severity of OA. The XGBoost model achieves an accuracy of 85.35% for detecting the presence of OA and accuracy of 72.46% for grading the severity of OA. The proposed deep learning achieves validation accuracy of 84.26% for detecting OA and 70-72% for grading the severity of OA. The independent analysis of the data with various models has given us promising results and the research has shown us the advantage of using several types of data thus enabling further early prediction and improving clinical outputs for patients with OA.

articleTitle: The Evolution of Cloud Computing: A Study of Aspirational Technologies and Practical Achievements
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Cloud computing has transformed the digital landscape, providing scalability, cost efficiency, and seamless access to computing resources. Yet, there is a gap between its theoretical aspirations and real-world achievements because of data privacy concerns, regulatory compliance, vendor lock-in, and performance bottlenecks. This paper critically examines these disparities through case studies, technological breakthroughs, and industry trends as a guide to understanding these impediments to cloud adoption. The study reviews the theoretical background of cloud computing, which include models related to deployment and service, and illustrates its successes in performance, reliability, and security. Persistent barriers, however, mean security and compliance are insecure while cost unpredictability remains a concern for organizations in using the maximum potential of a cloud. The study proposes strategic solutions that can serve to bridge the gap in terms of hybrid and multi-cloud adoption, AI-driven security frameworks, regulatory compliance automation, and various cost optimization techniques. Emerging trends like quantum computing, edge computing, and green cloud initiatives are shaping the future of cloud computing. By implementing these solutions, more is made out of the potential of cloud computing in securing a more efficient and sustainable digital infrastructure.

articleTitle: Optimized Scheduling Model of Integrated Energy System in Industrial Park Based on Improved MPA
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In the context of the global energy shortage and the increasing emphasis on sustainable development goals, optimizing the scheduling of integrated energy systems in industrial parks has become a critical issue. This paper presents an optimal scheduling model and an improved solution method to enhance energy efficiency in industrial parks. Firstly, we develop an energy efficiency optimization model for the integrated energy system in an industrial park. The model aims to maximize system energy efficiency and minimize operational costs while considering load balance constraints, equipment capacity, operational limits, and renewable energy generation constraints. Secondly, we introduce an enhanced Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) incorporating an adaptive step-size strategy and a multi-subgroup approach. These improvements enable adaptive adjustment of the iteration step size, accelerating convergence and improving solution accuracy, thus facilitating the efficient solving of the model. Then, The effectiveness of the proposed solution method is validated through standard test functions. Finally, we test the model through simulations. The results show that, when considering both energy efficiency and economic factors, our proposed scheduling model effectively improves energy efficiency. It can theoretically reduce energy costs by 3.13% and save 23.683 tons of standard coal annually, all while maintaining the same output level.

articleTitle: Coding Agents: A Comprehensive Survey of Automated Bug Fixing Systems and Benchmarks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: One of the trickiest problems in software engineering is automating software issue fixes, which calls for a thorough comprehension of contextual relationships, code semantics, and dynamic debugging techniques. The development of automatic program repair (APR) is examined in this survey, which traces a path from early template and constraint-based approaches to more recent developments powered by large language models (LLMs). Three main paradigms are compared here: retrieval-augmented approaches that integrate external knowledge sources, agent-based systems that use multi-agent frameworks, and agentless systems that use simplified repair pipelines. Real-world benchmarks that mimic actual engineering workflows and repository-level difficulties, such as SWE-bench, CODEAGENT-BENCH, and CodeRAG-Bench, are used to assess these cutting-edge technologies. This study demonstrates how agentic, agentless, and retrieval-augmented systems use LLMs to achieve previously unheard-of precision and scalability by following the shift from localized, single-file solutions to solving complicated, multi-file, and repository-wide difficulties. According to our findings, while complex agent architectures have potential, straightforward test-time scaling frequently produces better outcomes, especially when paired with containerized environments that allow for parallel exploration. Additionally, the survey looks at industrial applications, emphasizing effective connections with quality assurance and DevOps procedures. In order to further the development of more resilient and flexible APR frameworks that blend in perfectly with contemporary software engineering practices, we conclude by highlighting important issues in context handling and validation and suggesting future research directions in improved contextual models, human-AI collaboration, and multi-modal debugging systems.

articleTitle: Coupling Clearing Model for Coordinated Operation of Inter provincial and Intra provincial Integration Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This article proposes a coupled clearing model to address the market coupling and clearing mechanism issues in the coordinated operation of inter provincial and intra provincial electricity markets in China, in order to achieve effective integration and coordination of inter provincial and intra provincial electricity markets. Firstly, this study establishes a dual layer optimization model that considers the coupling characteristics between electricity markets in different provinces. The upper layer model is used to coordinate market transactions between different provinces, while the lower layer model is used for clearing calculations within the provincial market, ensuring optimal resource allocation and market fairness. Next, this study uses the Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) algorithm to solve the model, in order to improve computational efficiency and stability. At the same time, a penalty factor is introduced to regulate market behavior, ensuring the convergence of the model and the rationality of the results. The experimental results show that the coupled clearing model reduced the average total electricity cost by about 5.4% within 10 days, from 11.45 million yuan to 10.6 million yuan, and increased the inter provincial electricity dispatch by about 4.2%, significantly improving the inter provincial utilization efficiency of electricity resources. It also increased the consumption of renewable energy in the intra provincial market by about 10%, verifying its advantages in improving resource allocation and market fairness.

Author Keywords: Inter Provincial and Intra Provincial Coordination

articleTitle: Intelli-Helmet for Motorcycles Using Internet Of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Transport may be an essential requirement for the society. It makes human life simple and comfortable. It causes the passing of people and damages any part of the body. To avoid the particular action, we attempt to actualize a framework that is a Mishap discovery and informing framework utilizing Bluetooth-based Portable Application. In this framework, the vibration sensor is utilized as an input to the framework and the microcontroller analyzes the reaction by comparing it. In the event that mishap happens, sensors perusing exceed the limit, and it takes the suitable activity. The system sends an SMS alert to specialists, ensuring quick assistance for accident victims. It also monitors driver activity, detecting signs of intoxication before starting the vehicle or while driving. The proposed embedded approach delivers promising results in enhancing road safety.

articleTitle: Energy Performance, Carbon Footprint and Hardware Efficiency of Blockchain Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: High Performance Computing (HPC) plays a critical role in supporting the computationally intensive tasks of blockchain technologies, such as consensus algorithms, data processing, and validation. However, the growing adoption of blockchain has raised concerns regarding the substantial energy consumption and carbon footprint associated with HPC systems. This paper investigates the energy efficiency and environmental impact of HPC in blockchain applications, with a focus on hardware and associated hashing algorithms for mining. We analyze power consumption and carbon emissions from computational devices such as Central Processing Units (CPUs), Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), and Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs), particularly in cryptocurrency mining and decentralized applications. Additionally, we assess the environmental implications of different consensus algorithms, providing a comprehensive understanding of their energy demands and carbon emissions. Our findings offer valuable insights into blockchain sustainability, encouraging the adoption of more energy-efficient and environmentally conscious practices in the industry.

articleTitle: Javascript Code Simplification And Optimization Based On Hybrid Static and Dynamic Analysis Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of Web application functions, JavaScript libraries are widely used to improve development efficiency and user experience. However, many applications do not make full use of all JavaScript code during loading, resulting in redundant code being packaged into deployment files, which increases the page loading burden and affects performance. Existing optimization methods often rely on static analysis or dynamic analysis, but these methods alone are difficult to fully identify redundant code, static analysis cannot capture the dynamic behavior of the run time, and dynamic analysis is limited by test coverage and prone to false positives. Therefore, a hybrid analysis method combining static analysis and dynamic monitoring is proposed in this paper. Through static analysis, function call diagram is constructed and redundant functions are identified. Meanwhile, dynamic piling technology is combined to track code execution and supplement the shortcomings of static analysis, and accurate function call diagram is generated to identify and optimize redundant code.
