Based on this method, this paper develops a JavaScript code optimization tool that can automatically identify redundant code and reduce the size of the deployment package. Experimental results show that this tool can reduce about 59% of redundant code and improve the loading performance and stability of Web applications.

articleTitle: Security Implications of Augmented Reality in Healthcare: Integrating Human-Computer Interaction for Modern Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The current study presents a risk assessment and mitigation framework based on augmented reality (AR) used in healthcare systems to improve human-computer interaction and assistive technology. The proposed approach is proactive, identifying hardware and software vulnerabilities, assessing risk exposure, and prioritizing mitigation strategies. The framework adapts dynamically to emerging flaws from stakeholder feedback, ensuring continuous improvement and technological relevance. With a performance in key areas such as data safety, user authentication, access control, privacy protection, and threat detection, the technique far outperforms existing systems like Secure AR Framework, AR Guard System, Health Secure AR, MedTech Shield, and Safe AR in data security, system stability, legal compliance, and user training. By applying this proactive approach, cognitive health takes precedence over enabling informed decision-making based on precise mathematical risk quantification. According to the findings, this strategy significantly improves the safety of AR healthcare applications and protects patient data and system integrity. Ultimately, it guarantees the creation of safer and more consistent healthcare AR systems, thus bringing safety and contentment to patients and specialists.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fake Account Detection on Digital Platforms Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This research addresses the growing challenge of detecting fake accounts on digital platforms, such as social media and professional networks, which pose significant threats to user trust, platform security, and public discourse. The proposed framework integrates several powerful architectures, including Attention-Based LSTM, Bidirectional GRU, Bidirectional LSTM, LSTM with Flatten Layer, and Bidirectional LSTM with Flatten Layer, each designed to capture complex patterns and dependencies in the user profile data. These models are evaluated based on key performance metrics, such as F1-score, precision, recall, accuracy, and loss value, to assess their effectiveness in fake account detection. The results show that the LSTM with Flatten Layer model achieved the highest accuracy (95.83%), precision (94%), and recall (98%), making it the most effective model in distinguishing fake profiles. The Bidirectional LSTM with Flatten Layer (AdamW) also exhibited strong results, with an accuracy of 94.91%. The results of this study contribute to the development of more robust and accurate systems for detecting fraudulent profiles, offering valuable guidance for addressing the challenges posed by fake accounts in digital environments.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Enabled Smart Hand Gesture Virtual Mouse System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This research is aim to focus on IoT based hand gesture model. Mouse is one of the most important input devices of a computer. It works as a pointing device and allows the user to move the pointer as needed by the user. In the early days, a wired mechanical mouse was used for this purpose. In mechanical mouse a ball is fixed underneath the mouse, which rotates as the user moves the mouse. This movement of the ball is used to move the mouse pointer on the screen. Now mostly we use optical mouse which can be wired or wireless. An optical mouse has a high-power laser below it, which takes more than thousand pictures of the surface below the mouse. An image comparator compares the images and sends the signal to move the mouse pointer as the texture of the image changes. Both the types of mouse works based on old technology. As technology leaps to greater heights, the need for simplicity also increases. With the invention of different kind of sensors, microcontrollers and other electronics, we can eliminate the mouse as an input device and instead use our hands to do the work of a mouse. This prototype is an embedded system which runs with the help of an arduino microcontroller. Flex sensors are used to capture the hand gestures. The proposed IoT based hand gesture model is providing high accuracy rate compare to the regular model. The proposed model is analyzed with accuracy level, the average accuracy level of proposed model is more than 90%.

articleTitle: Hybrid Anomaly Detection Framework for Matter-Enabled IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Communications reliability and security of Matter-enabled IoT networks are now gaining even more prominence with their widespread acceptance and deployment. Nonetheless, such advancements indeed introduce further challenges, most notably in the detection of the diverse set of anomalies caused by device faults and DDoS attacks that may destabilize the network. This paper presents a hybrid anomaly detection system specifically designed for Matter-enabled IoT environments where rule-based filtering is incorporated with an ML-based detection approach leveraging Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). The rule-based module detects potential anomalies by applying predefined threshold conditions, and the XGBoost aims to curtail this detection into high detection capability and reduced false positives. The system is experimented with making the prediction on IoT telemetry data, achieving 97% precision, recall, and accuracy-greatly exceeding the lone detection strategies. The results prove how our approach can help mitigate the occurrence of false alarms, alongside imbalanced datasets being major obstacles in IoT networks' anomaly detection. Future research will further include the real-time detection application of sophisticated temporal models, scalable improvements, and security optimization within the confines of resource-constrained Matter-enabled IoT deployment.

articleTitle: Overcoming Dataset Imbalances and Computational Challenges in IoT Intrusion Detection: A SMOTE-Enhanced Transformer-Based Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)

authors.preferredName: S. K. B. Pradeep Kumar Ch

abstract: Due to security holes in IoT-enabled networks, the massive adoption of IoT has unleashed a new wave of threats into computer networks. Due to their limited resources, these devices are ill-equipped to handle security measures, making them the most vulnerable part of our computer networks and putting our data and systems at risk. Some have suggested Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) as a means to lessen the impact of intrusions connected to the IoT in an effort to solve this problem. Although IDS are essential for detecting threats, they are not widely used because of their high computing costs and reliance on labelled data. Finding a happy medium between fast detection and excellent accuracy is the objective of this model development effort. In order to accomplish this, to present a feature selection method based on the black-winged kite algorithm (BKA), a groundbreaking swarm intelligence technique that combines the Leader tactic and the Cauchy variation procedure to find the expansive appropriate convergence solution. BKA is based on the migratory and predatory instincts of black-winged kites. The study used few-shot learning techniques by leveraging transfer learning models and specifically using pre-trained architectures for categorisation. It also fine-tuned four pre-trained transformers. To take into account the imbalance in these datasets as a significant component and use the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to address it. The research team used BoT-IoT, TON-IoT, and CIC-DDoS2019 as benchmark datasets to assess the impact of the chosen features on the suggested model's performance. Metrics for evaluation include F1-score, recall, precision, and accuracy of detection. Evidence from experiments shows that the suggested ensemble model outperforms state-of-the-art AIDS topologies for IoT networks in terms of detection accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Exploring Deep Learning Paradigms for Handwritten Digit Recognition: Insights and Advances
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In the application area of postal automation to signature verification, the Handwritten digit recognition (HRD) is major challenging field in the era of pattern recognition and machine learning. The convolutional neural networks (CNNs) becoming most emerging technology in the field of deep learning. The CNN made significant advancement in landscape of digit recognition, surpassing traditional methods in accuracy and performance. Motivated by the significance of accurate digit classification, this research presents a comprehensive review and synthesis of seminal works in the field. Through a meticulous examination of pioneering studies, we identify trends, challenges, and emerging paradigms characterizing contemporary research in handwritten digit recognition. Five deep learning methods, including a Baseline MLP, Simple CNN Model, Larger CNN Model, Basic ResNet Architecture, and Inception V3, are evaluated for their performance in digit recognition tasks. Results demonstrate that the Inception V3 model achieves the highest accuracy of 0.99, with a precision of 0.9929 and a recall of 0.9995. The review encompasses foundational works laying the groundwork for digit recognition algorithms, as well as cutting-edge research leveraging transfer learning, hybrid models, and advanced deep learning architectures. By synthesizing insights from these studies, our aim is to provide researchers and practitioners with a comprehensive understanding of state-of-art techniques, enabling informed decision-making and inspiring future advancements in HRD.

articleTitle: Underpinning of Resource-Constrained IoT Networks: Analysis and Countermeasures for Attacks and Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The Internet of Things integrate various electronics devices on common platform as objects over the Internet. IoT devices have limited capabilities, such as low power, less memory, and low computational processing. Besides these constraints, IoT deals with a large amount of sensitive and personal data, making the IoT networks highly prone to attacks and various vulnerabilities. This paper summarizes the different possible attacks and vulnerabilities on resource-constrained IoT networks and the security requirements compromised. It also presents available countermeasures for these possible attacks. Furthermore, the paper discusses the simulation-based parameters for results on detection of such vulnerabilities and attacks in IoT networks. The paper presents protocols for resource-constrained IoT networks and maps different attacks with existing protocols. Finally, the paper summarizes the vulnerabilities in the IoT specially designed for resource-constrained environments and, discusses the potential impact of these vulnerabilities, and outlines countermeasures to address the same.

articleTitle: Cost-balanced Adaptive Replica Server Cache Management under Time-Varying User Request Density in CCDNs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In today’s growing Internet, cost-effective on-demand provisioning of caching resources in Cloud-based Content Delivery Networks (CCDNs) is essential to preserve the cache hit ratio while reducing storage requirements. However, during the high and fluctuating request rates at different locations, the sudden increase in cache to mitigate the miss rate requires a balance between storage cost (from dynamic cache provisioning) and miss cost (from latency in retrieving content from the Origin Server (OS) or other Replica Servers (RSs)). In such an environment, some RS instances remain underutilized while others are overburdened across different locations and time intervals, which requires effective RS management to activate only sufficient RSs by adapting to the user demands. To overcome these challenges, a cost-balanced adaptive cache management approach is proposed for dynamic cache provisioning in CCDN. This method aims to dynamically manage the activation of RS to optimize resource utilization, and cache instance provisioning and content caching operations in these RSs are managed by introducing an Adaptive Cache Manager that retrieves content from the OS or other RSs by effectively balancing costs in different time intervals. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method reduces the number of active replica servers in CCDN across different time intervals while decreasing the average total cost by about 56% relative to the LRU caching policy on fixed cache and about 10% compared to the dynamic selective caching policy on RCW cache.

articleTitle: Employee Attrition Prediction: a Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: At present organizations are leveraging superior technology to reap their desires more efficiently. Artificial Intelligence (AI), which includes Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning, performs a pivotal position in improving organizational development. Machine Learning, transforms employee attrition datasets into actionable insights, permitting a employee overall performance and behaviour. This study uses Machine Learning for organizational by using distinctive classifiers to assess employee attrition. ML classifiers have been analyzed on this dataset that includes features such as Age, Daily Rate, Distance From Home, Environment Satisfaction, Job Involvement, Job Level, Job Satisfaction, Num Companies Worked, Percent Salary Hike, Relationship Satisfaction, Stock Option Level, Total Working Years, Training Times Last Year, Work Life Balance, Years In Current Role, Years Since Last Promotion, Years With Current Manager. Each classifier is evaluated primarily based totally on its accuracy rating in predicting ordinary employee attrition. By evaluating accuracy rankings with the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve, this study identifies the best classifier for organizational use. This study provides valuable insights from ML classifiers and their potential to predict employee attrition.

articleTitle: A Custom Features-Based Face Recognition using a Bag of Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Recognizing faces in unconstrained environments remains a significant challenge in face recognition research. In this paper, we present a bag of classifiers for unconstrained face recognition, to enhance recognition accuracy by leveraging the strengths of unique custom feature extraction techniques. The proposed method combines well-established facial features, including distance ratios, skin tone, texture, and a newly designed area-intensity-density feature. To ensure robust evaluation, we test the approach on three widely-used benchmark datasets—Yale, AR, and LFW, and assess performance using key metrics such as accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, F1-score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), and Area Under the Curve (AUC). Extensive experiments demonstrate that the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) performs best on the Yale dataset, while the Random Forest (RF) classifier achieves the highest accuracy on Labeled Faces in the Wild (LFW), with results of 86.67% and 79.19%, respectively. These findings underscore the potential of the bag of classifiers approach as an effective and efficient solution for face recognition in practical applications, highlighting the importance of selecting an optimal feature extraction-classifier pair.

articleTitle: Prediction of Customer Satisfaction using Machine Learning Algorithms: Perspectives of Service and Operational Factors in Airline Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Customer satisfaction in the airline industry is influenced by demographic, service-related, and operational factors. As competition grows and passenger expectations evolve, understanding these determinants is crucial for improving service quality and loyalty. This study uses machine learning algorithms to analyze key drivers of customer satisfaction and derive actionable insights. It employs techniques such as Logistic Regression, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Gradient Boosting, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Random Forest classifiers. Among these, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with AUC scores of 0.99 and 0.9937. A strong correlation (0.97) between departure and arrival delays highlights the importance of punctuality. Inflight services like entertainment and legroom, especially on long-haul flights, significantly enhance satisfaction. Demographic analysis shows passengers aged 40+ report higher satisfaction, emphasizing the need for tailored service strategies, while younger passengers (20-40) show lower satisfaction, indicating a need for personalized engagement. These findings provide a data-driven foundation for improving airline operations and service delivery. Future research should integrate real-time data for more adaptive service improvements.

articleTitle: The Missing Data Imputation Method for Medical Data Classification Using Most Probable Value
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In medical data classification, improving the performance of classification is essential when the dataset's size is small, and some attributes' values need to be included. Classification performance can suffer if the training dataset starts with insufficient data samples. The challenges like overfitting, high variance, inability to find real performance of model, biased models, sensitivity to noise, improper evaluation occurs with small dataset. The proposed algorithm uses domain-based multiple imputations to create additional data tuples and appends these tuples to the originally available training data. This improves the classification power of the classifier. This proposed technique uses a set of domain values to impute missing attribute values. The accuracy of imputed tuples is verified using classifier filters. The proposed technique significantly improves the classification performance of the classifier. This technique is suitable for small to medium-sized data sets. Data imputation helps develop improved and more accurate classifiers. The proposed approach offers improved classification performance. The proposed method achieves a 4.01% improvement in the classification accuracy of fuzzy neural network FBNFC. We performed two hypothesis tests, the t-test, and the Wilcoxon rank sum test. It is observed that the alternative hypothesis is true.

articleTitle: Optimizing Crop Selection Through Hyperparameter Tuning of Neural Networks: Development and Evaluation of Deep Learning Models for Enhancing Crop Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Applications of Precision Agriculture are becoming more popular throughout the world due to the possibilities that this technology offers to enhance crop yields as a result of decision-making based on effective data. By leveraging data such as pH, temperature, and rainfall, the models provide precise predictions, enabling farmers to make informed crop selection decisions. In this study, we propose and test two neural network models for crop recommendation based on the soil and or environmental data. The first architecture has 5 parameters, in fact, it consists of two hidden layers; the second one has 300 parameters it consists of five hidden layers so we can observe the difference between the model complexity and performance. Thus, we employed grid search and 5-fold cross-validation to optimize the use of hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and activation function. Using the two-hidden-layer model, we obtained an accuracy of 98.7% percent, thereby closely performing better compared to the five-hidden-layer model that achieved 98.4% accuracy. Analyzing experimental results confirmed that larger learning rate and the Adam optimizer provided the highest average scores in both networks architecture. For example, the architecture with five hidden layers was almost five times slower, pointing to the time-space trade-off in neural network models. The results are useful in the current endeavor of deploying AI for agriculture and recommending crops by implementing this file-based approach. Further studies on the same work will involve accumulating a larger database with the soil characteristics of the Bangladesh region, with the hope of establishing a more refined and specific recommendation for the right crops to be grown.

articleTitle: Integrated Framework for Equitable Healthcare AI: Bias Mitigation, Community Participation, and Regulatory Governance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionized healthcare by enhancing diagnostic precision, personalizing treatments, and optimizing clinical workflows. However, algorithmic biases arising from imbalanced training data dis-proportionately affect marginalized populations, perpetuating health disparities. For instance, a widely-used predictive model underprioritized Black patients by equating healthcare costs with illness severity, restricting access to essential care. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an integrated framework combining adversarial debiasing, reinforcement learning (RL)-driven threshold optimization, synthetic data augmentation, and community engagement strategies. Empirical evaluations using the MIMIC-III dataset demonstrate near-perfect Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC = 0.994) alongside significant reductions in demographic parity (DP = 0.000) and error rate differences across subgroups. While the RL-optimized threshold ensures no missed diagnoses, it increases false positives, highlighting the trade-offs between fairness and precision. This work underscores the importance of synthesizing technical, regulatory, and community-driven approaches to promote equitable AI deployments. By embedding participatory design principles and aligning with emerging governance frameworks like the European Union’s AI Act, the proposed methodology offers a scalable pathway toward transparent, accountable, and high-impact healthcare AI solutions.

articleTitle: SYNCVISION: High-Resolution Speech-Synchronized Portrait Animation Using Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: SYNCVISION is a deep learning-based system designed to generate high-resolution speech-synced portrait animations. By utilizing the pretrained Wav2Lip model, it aligns lip movements in portrait images with corresponding audio input, ensuring high-quality animations with computational efficiency. The system is optimized to handle various accents, languages, and visual contexts, making it versatile across different scenarios. SYNCVISION is evaluated using metrics like Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Lip Synchronization Error (LSE), as well as subjective quality assessments. This project aims to provide a scalable solution for creating realistic speech-driven animations in applications like entertainment, education, and virtual communication.

articleTitle: Real-time Posture Correction System in sitting using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In today's workplace, desk employees often spend long hours sitting in front of computers, leading to issues such as poor posture, back pain, neck strain, and other musculoskeletal problems. This research presents a solution using wearable devices and computer vision technology to tackle these health concerns. The system monitors the user's body position in real-time by analyzing images captured by the wearable device. It calculates body angles and relevant data to evaluate posture and offers corrective feedback when poor posture is detected. Maintaining good posture is important not only for physical well-being but also for enhancing productivity. Recognizing this, researchers and developers are creating technological solutions to help desk workers develop healthier posture habits throughout the workday. This paper introduces a system designed to promote better posture using computer vision. The camera capture real-time images of the user, and the system uses algorithms to identify key body points and calculate posture angles. If improper posture is identified, the system provides the user with guidance to make adjustments, helping prevent posture-related health issues. This technology offers a practical approach to reducing the physical strain associated with prolonged sitting, benefiting both individual health and workplace efficiency.

articleTitle: Advanced Fault Sleuth System Architectures for Prognostic Anomaly Detection and Autonomous Irregularity Mitigation in Intelligent Power Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Revenue losses, inconsistent service, delayed problem detection, and electricity theft are just a few of the major issues that power distribution networks deal with. The suggested Fault Sleuth System makes use of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to facilitate remote system control, automatic anomaly detection, and real-time electrical parameter monitoring. The technology guarantees accurate fault localization and proactive theft prevention by combining sophisticated data analytics and feature extraction techniques. The technology greatly lowers maintenance costs and security threats while improving operating efficiency through thorough data collecting, preprocessing, and intelligent analysis. In addition to improving problem detection and theft mitigation, this strategy also raises customer happiness, power quality, and service reliability. The study's conclusions show how the Fault Sleuth System can revolutionize the way that important power distribution issues are handled. This technology opens the door for a more robust, safe, and effective energy infrastructure that can satisfy needs in the future by leveraging real-time analytics and state-of-the-art IoT technologies.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Usage of AI in Prevention of Social Engineering Attack
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: AI has become a tool for social engineering attackers, enhancing the likelihood of successful attacks. However, as the saying goes, "Diamonds cut diamonds." In this research, we have enlisted the usage of AI to initiate, launch, counter and prevent social engineering attacks. We have explored not only traditional forms of social engineering attacks with AI, such as phishing, eavesdropping, shoulder surfing, dumpster diving, piggybacking, and tailgating but also the latest forms of AI-enabled social engineering attacks, known as vishing, baiting, Smishing, Whaling, Quishing and Quid Pro Quo. This research paper also conducted a systematic literature review of AI-based defending techniques like AI Sentry,

articleTitle: Power Internet of Things Access System Based on Low Power Communication Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In response to the issues of data transmission energy efficiency and network coverage in the power Internet of Things system, this study introduces an access scheme based on low-power communication technology. By optimizing the network architecture and communication protocol, the aim is to improve the energy efficiency of sensor nodes in the power Internet of Things and reduce communication latency. Firstly, an access scheme based on low power wide area network (LPWAN) technology is designed. LoRa (Long Range Radio) or NB-IoT (Narrow Band Internet of Thing) is selected as the communication protocol. By optimizing the working mode of sensor nodes, periodic transmission and event-driven mechanism are adopted. Secondly, an adaptive data transmission mechanism is designed to dynamically adjust the transmission frequency and rate according to environmental changes to ensure reliability under different network conditions. Furthermore, deep sleep mode and power consumption scheduling algorithm are adopted, and the network architecture adopts star topology to ensure the efficiency of signal coverage and data forwarding, and the secure transmission of data information is guaranteed by encryption and authentication mechanism. Finally, through simulation and actual deployment, the performance of the scheme in the actual environment is verified, and its stability and data transmission efficiency under different network scales are evaluated. The battery life of periodic wake-up mode is significantly lower than that of deep sleep mode. Under low-frequency transmission (once an hour), the battery life is 320 days. In periodic wake-up mode, the average power consumption of sensor nodes is significantly higher than that of deep sleep mode. At low frequency transmission, average power consumption is 3.5 mW and battery life drops to 75 days. The power Internet of Things access system based on low-power communication technology proposed in this work effectively solves the bottleneck problems of the current power Internet of Things system in terms of energy efficiency and communication delay, and has good application prospects.

Author Keywords: Power Internet of Things Access System

articleTitle: Evaluating GNSS Spoofing and Jamming Attacks on UAV Navigation: Implementation and Impact
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The rapid increase in the use of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAV) across various critical sectors, such as defense, underscores the urgent need to address their vulnerability to GPS-based interference. This project examines the dual threats of GPS spoofing and jamming, both of which can significantly undermine the integrity and reliability of drone operations. Spoofing misleads the flight controller by manipulating location data causing the drone to believe it is operating in a different location than its actual position, while Jamming disrupts communication with satellite signals, making navigation systems ineffective. Utilizing a Cube Orange with Pixhawk, HackRF One, Here3+ GPS, and a custom- built VCO-based RF jammer, this study examines the serious implications of these threats on drone stability and functionality. The project follows a systematic approach, starting with the careful assembly and calibration of a custom quadcopter. By employing gps-sdr-sim software and HackRF One, realistic spoofing signals were created to manipulate GPS telemetry, while a custom-designed jammer circuit, developed in Altium Designer, showcased the ability to disable navigation systems completely. Testing and validation were carried out using Mission Planner and QGroundControl, revealing that spoofing could convincingly change the drone’s perceived location, resulting in incorrect behavior, while jamming led to immediate operational failure.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Framework for Optimizing Node Deployment in WSNs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Efficient node deployment in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is critical for maximizing network coverage, enhancing energy efficiency, and prolonging network lifetime. However, achieving optimal node placement is challenging due to the limited energy resources and dynamic environmental conditions in WSNs. This paper presents a novel hybrid approach that combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) with the Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm to optimize node deployment in WSNs. In this method, RL dynamically adapts node positions based on local network states, while DE performs global optimization to refine these placements and improve coverage. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RL-DE hybrid approach significantly outperforms traditional deployment methods, standalone RL, and DE in terms of coverage, energy conservation, and network longevity. The results suggest that the RL-DE approach provides an adaptive and robust solution for node deployment in WSNs, with potential applications in real-world sensor network deployments.

articleTitle: Novel Deep Learning Approach for Tooth Segmentation in Orthodontic Treatment Using STU-RestNet
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In this paper we introduce the novel approach in dentistry deep learning method for image segmentation which is helpful for orthodontics treatment. In oral diagnosis treatment the image segmentation plays an important role to determine caries for accurate diagnosis in dental treatment. The previous traditional method failed in the clinical segment in labeling the process of tooth i.e. both label and unlabel data. We address these types of issues using the Swin Transformer UNet and Rest Net method. It is a self-learning-based algorithm named as STU-RestNet–Swin Transformer U-Net RestNet method demonstrated the performance on the dataset which proving its performance and effectiveness, robustness, accuracy in tooth segmentation. Our architecture is based on the segmentation approach with novel mechanisms to decode the various regions and deep supervision technique using STU-RestNet.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Cyber Attack Detection in the Presence of Highly Imbalanced Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Due to the rapid growth in the number of Internet of Things (IoT) networks, the cyber risk has increased exponentially, and therefore, we have to develop effective IDS that can work well with highly imbalanced datasets. High rate of missed threats can be the result as traditional machine learning models tend to struggle in identifying attacks as normal data volume is so much higher than the volume of attacks. For example, the data set used in this study reveals a strong class imbalance with 94,659 instances of the majority class and only 28 instances of the minority class, in which determining rare attacks accurately is quite challenging. The challenges presented in this research are addressed by hybrid sampling techniques designed to drive data imbalance detection accuracy in IoT domains. After doing so, we then evaluate the performance of several machine learning models such as Random Forest, Soft Voting, Support Vector Classifier (SVC), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Logistic Regression with respect to the classification of cyber-attacks accurately. The obtained results indicate that the Random Forest model achieved the best performance value of 0.9903 of Kappa score, 0.9961 of test accuracy and 0.9994 of AUC. It also shows strong performance in the Soft Voting model, with an accuracy of 0.9952 and AUC of 0.9997, while the latter is an indication of the benefits of combining models’ prediction. Overall, this work has shown the great benefit of hybrid sampling combined with robust model selection and feature selection to deliver a dramatic increase in of IoT security against cyber-attack, an important factor for implementing security in environments with strongly imbalanced data.

articleTitle: Algorithms for Machine Learning to Predict Childbirth Modes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Health and well-being of women and bonding created with the newborn are heavily de- pendent on the birth process. What delivery method to choose is a critical decision that often needs to be applied in a timely manner to ensure the well-being of the baby and mother. Errors in this regard may cause serious health consequences for the mother and fetus, making it hard for healthcare professionals to make timely and correct decisions. In this paper, a decision support system based on machine learning for predicting the safest delivery method is presented. Various supervised learning algorithms are tested, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree, and a stochastic classifier. The outcomes of this paper indicate that the Random Forest algorithm has better accuracy in predicting the delivery method and thereby aids healthcare professionals in reducing judgmental errors and improving the safety of neonates and mothers.

articleTitle: Implementation and Analysis of Energy Efficient LEACH-C Algorithm for Network of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The proliferation of bandwidth-hungry apps and the growing number of connected devices have resulted in an unprecedented demand for wireless communication networks. The introduction of fifth generation (5G) networks has created new opportunities to improve connectivity, especially in difficult situations such as distant locations or places affected by disasters. In this regard, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) have been shown to be a flexible tool. As the 5G network did, the 6G network is anticipated to offer millions of interconnected devices massive connectivity with a wide range of quality of service (QoS) requirements, ubiquitous coverage, a high level of embedded artificial intelligence (AI), energy efficiency, and adaptive network security. UAVs are expected to play an important role in 6G networks. In this paper, LEACH-C algorithm is implemented and analyzed for improving the network throughput and energy efficiency. The experiment is performed in MATLAB. The proposed algorithm results are compared with optimal UAV placement algorithm, resulting in better performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic Forensic Analysis of CryptBot Malware
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: CryptBot, an infostealer malware first identified in 2019, poses a serious threat by stealing sensitive data, including login credentials and cryptocurrency wallet details, and transmitting them to command-and-control servers. It spreads through phishing emails, malicious ads, and pirated software, using advanced evasion techniques to remain undetected. This study employs dynamic malware analysis to observe CryptBot’s real-time behavior, including its data exfiltration methods, persistence mechanisms, and evasion strategies. Key findings reveal tactics such as subprocess creation, process renaming, and temporary file usage to facilitate data theft. To mitigate such threats, a multi-layered security approach is essential, combining dynamic, static, and hybrid analysis methods with security measures like intrusion detection, encryption, and multi-factor authentication. Additionally, user education on phishing and software piracy is crucial in preventing infections. This research enhances understanding of CryptBot’s operations and proposes detection and mitigation strategies. Future work includes developing advanced sandbox environments and integrating machine learning to improve threat detection and response.

articleTitle: An Approach for Detecting and classification of Lung Cancer Using Deep Learning and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the top causes of cancer-related fatalities worldwide, demanding early and accurate detection for better patient outcomes. This work addresses the merging of neural network (ML) along with deep learning (DL) approaches to increase lung cancer diagnosis and classification. Using sophisticated convolution neural networks (CNNs) for image analysis and standard machine learning (ML) models like random forest algorithms and supported vector machines (SVMs) for structured data, the suggested technique achieves excellent diagnostic accuracy, avoiding false positives and negatives. Enhanced CNNs give higher efficiency with precision of 93%, recall of 98.5%, and an accuracy of 97%. Key indicators include cumulative risk, age, and weariness, whereas demographic characteristics have a modest influence. Visualization methods such as feature significance charts and confusion matrices verify model dependability. This hybrid AI-driven approach indicates great promise in transforming lung cancer diagnoses, however problems including data privacy, computing needs, and validation in clinical trials remain and This work utilizes artificial intelligence (AI) (ML) in conjunction with deep learning (DL) technology to produce a more precise and automated approach for lung cancer diagnosis and categorization.

articleTitle: Advance Collaborative AI-Driven Bots Using RPA to Enhance Workplace Inclusivity for Employees with Disabilities in India
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: AI-powered bots are designed to assist workers with disabilities in various work environments. It explores adaptive interfaces and supportive features that enable these bots to meet the diverse needs of individuals facing visual, auditory, motor, and cognitive challenges. By synthesizing existing research, this review emphasizes the possibility of AI to explore workplace inclusivity, assesses the effectiveness of different assistive technologies, and identifies critical gaps in current studies. Furthermore, the paper highlights emerging trends in AI-driven accessibility tools and provides recommendations for future research and development initiatives.

articleTitle: Building Secure and Decentralized Survey Methodology: A Comprehensive Solution with FIDO2 Authentication and Fluree
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Traditional survey systems struggle with data immutability, privacy protection, and reliable storage. These limitations compromise transparency, security, and data integrity. This paper proposes a decentralized and secure survey platform to address these challenges. Fast Identity Online 2 (FIDO2) passwordless authentication strengthens user verification, backed by public key cryptography. Fluree, a permissioned blockchain based graph database, ensures decentralized storage and minimizes data tampering. Smart codes are designed based on user requirements, while integrated statistical analyses enhance data insights. This approach of integrating these technologies prioritizes transparency, security, and integrity in the data collection process while maintaining a seamless user experience. By fostering trust among stakeholders, it enables reliable, data driven decision-making.

articleTitle: Mitigating Security Vulnerabilities in Cloud-Based Home Automation through Advanced Edge Computing: A Comprehensive Framework for Privacy Enhancement and Data Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: With the soaring adoption of cloud-constructed home automation systems with CAGR of 8.5% from 2023 to 2030, security and privacy concerns have become critical considerations. This paper examines the security risks in cloud-based home automation systems and proposes leveraging edge computing to improve data security and privacy. We examine weaknesses including unapproved access, data leaks and highlight limitations of cloud-centric architectures. By integrating edge computing, we reduce data exposure, enable local processing, and improve control within the home environment. We explore how edge computing addresses specific attacks and offline operation during network disruptions. Challenges of incorporating edge computing into cloud-based home automation are discussed. This research contributes insights for achieving a more secure and privacy-enhanced home automation system.

articleTitle: Smart Monitoring of High-Performance KY Converter in IoT-Enabled Electric Vehicle Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The smart Electric Vehicle (EV)-Improved KY Converter monitoring system, which is Internet of Things (IoT)-based, provides an advanced method for improving the dependability and efficiency of EV power systems. By utilizing IoT technology, this system keeps a close eye on the enhanced KY converter's efficiency, which is essential for controlling power conversion in electric vehicles. The Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) effectively operates the system at maximum power level with fast response and low oscillations. It effectively optimizes energy conversion from Photo Voltaic (PV) by dynamically modifying to the operating point under varying environmental conditions. The deployment of this intelligent monitoring system is expected to yield notable progress in the administration and functioning of electric vehicle power systems, hence augmenting the general sustainability of electric-powered transportation. The proposed system is implemented in MATLAB, employing its sophisticated simulation capabilities to analyse the PV system. This simulation framework enables for the testing and validation of key performance metrics of 98% efficiency exhibiting in boosting power extraction and grid stability.

articleTitle: Perceptual Learning Technology Based on Computer Vision and Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: To address the issue of low accuracy and poor robustness of perceptual learning in complex scenarios, a new method integrating computer vision and machine learning is adopted, that is, by applying deep neural networks, transfer learning and self-supervised learning, combined with multimodal data fusion strategy, to improve target recognition efficiency and learning ability. First, based on the preprocessing algorithm of improved Gaussian filtering and image segmentation, the quality of image features is improved. Data enhancement methods such as random rotation, flipping, and blurring are used to expand data distribution and improve model adaptability. Secondly, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is utilized in combination with an attention mechanism to extract multi-scale target features, and transfer learning is applied to transfer common features from pre-trained models to reduce dependence on large-scale labeled data. Finally, a contrastive learning framework is constructed to mine the correlation of unlabeled data. Transformer is used to realize the fusion of multimodal data of images and texts, and the model performance is optimized through multi-task learning. The mAP (Mean Average Precision) of the traditional method in dynamic occlusion scenarios is 60.5%, which is relatively weak. This may be because the traditional method cannot fully extract the effective features of the target under the occlusion of complex moving targets. The mAP of the method in this paper is 72.8%, which is higher than that of the traditional method. The perceptual learning method adopted in this paper effectively improves the accuracy and robustness in complex scenarios, and provides reliable technical support for intelligent applications. In the future, it can be combined with edge computing to further optimize the real-time processing capability and promote its application in the fields of unmanned driving and intelligent security.

articleTitle: Generative AI SSH Honeypot With Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In today's rapidly evolving cyber landscape, traditional honeypots face significant limitations in their ability to adapt to sophisticated attack patterns and maintain convincing interactions with attackers. We propose Generative AI SSH Honeypot (GASH): an innovative approach to this problem combining Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Large Language Models (LLMs) to create a dynamic, engaging honeypot system. GASH employs a Deep Q-Network (DQN) architecture for strategic decision-making and leverages OpenAI’s GPT-4o for generating contextually appropriate responses while maintaining robust security measures. Our experimental results demonstrate improvements in attacker engagement duration compared to traditional honeypot systems like Kippo and Cowrie.

articleTitle: The Overfitting Dilemma: Exploring Solutions for Robust Classification Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: A major problem in machine learning is still overfitting, which produces models that do well on training data but poorly on unknown data. The overfitting challenge is examined in this study along with its sources, effects, and practical solutions. In order to improve classification performance, we go over regularization strategies, data augmentation, ensemble learning, and model pruning. We also look at the trade-off between generalization and model complexity, highlighting the significance of reliable assessment techniques. We offer insights into maximizing model performance while avoiding overfitting by contrasting different strategies. Our research helps create more dependable machine learning models that can maintain accuracy in practical settings.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Model for Cyber Threat Intelligence, Sharing Across Multi-Organizational Platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The research presents a privacy-preserving structure for secure Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) exchanging, using cutting-edge AI techniques to increase cooperative IT delicacy while keeping secret information safe. We propose a system based on Federated Learning, Differential Privacy and Homomorphic Encryption to model training in multiple organizations without exchanging the raw data. Using these privacy-preserving techniques together, organizations can collaborate to enhance their overall threat detection and response capabilities while maintaining the confidentiality of sensitive data. The implemented results indicate significant advancements with a 50%-55% detection accuracy overall for role intention measurement, model accuracy increase to 82% (predicting the next role intention), 30% computational overhead improvement, and a 10% improvement in novel threat detection. It provides 85% compliance against regulatory standards including GDPR and NIST. The applicability of the proposed solution on real-world data in the financial and healthcare domains demonstrates the proposed solution achieves a balance between privacy protection and CTI sharing still providing a powerful method for distributed, scalable and efficient collaboration in secure cybersecurity .

articleTitle: Development of a Flood Dynamic Monitoring and Forecasting System Based on Remote Sensing Big Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: To minimize the economic losses and casualties caused by flooding, early warning of flood disasters is crucial. This paper develops a flood dynamic monitoring and forecasting system based on remote sensing big data. By using remote sensing image processing techniques, the system extracts temporal changes in water body and surface information, identifies the extent and variations of water bodies, and determines the flooded areas. Based on flood disaster level assessments, the system forecasts flood dynamics and visualizes the results through GIS technology. The results show that the maximum flood inundation area in Fengzhan City increased from 196 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 3320 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and then decreased to 2219 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The flood-affected areas in Fengzhan City, Wahe City, Yunxiang City, and Guannan City account for 30%–70% of the total sowing area, which classifies them as moderately affected. Guikou City and Changyu City, with flood-affected areas accounting for less than 30% of the total sowing area, are classified as lightly affected. The relative error between the fitted inundation area in the system and the area extracted from remote sensing images does not exceed 4.00%, indicating that the system has high accuracy and reliability in monitoring water body inundation areas and assessing disaster severity.

articleTitle: Design Of Stepper Motor Based Dosing System to Enhanced Accuracy & Efficiency For Chemical Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This research paper presents the design and implementation of a stepper motor based dosing system aimed at improving accuracy and efficiency in the chemical industry. Because liquid dosing precision is becoming more and more important, especially in the manufacturing of pharmaceuticals, chemicals, and packaging, this system uses a hybrid NEMA 17 stepper motor that offers accurate control with a 0.9 degree step angle. To ensure precise fluid distribution and preserve operational integrity, the dosing mechanism makes use of sophisticated control algorithms in conjunction with a dependable auger system and non-return valves. Thorough testing was done at different volume settings (5, 10, 15, and 20 mL) to assess the accuracy and repeatability of the system, showing that it can greatly reduce errors. By reducing manual intervention, the system's automated architecture improves both operational efficiency and product quality. The study also highlights how crucial real time monitoring and user friendly interfaces are for simple supervision and adjustment. This study addresses important issues in liquid dosing processes across a range of industries by demonstrating its adaptability for various industrial applications, advancing precision engineering and industrial automation.

articleTitle: Improvement and Performance of Data Transmission Algorithms in Computer Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In response to the current problems of low data transmission efficiency, high latency, and insufficient stability in computer communications, this paper studies a comprehensive optimized data transmission algorithm, which aims to improve network resource utilization efficiency and transmission performance and reduce the frequency of congestion by dynamically adjusting the transmission rate, adaptive congestion control and queue management optimization. Firstly, a dynamic rate adjustment mechanism based on real-time network status detection is designed to monitor the network bandwidth, latency, and packet loss rate in real time to dynamically adjust the data packet transmission rate. Secondly, an adaptive congestion control strategy is applied to reduce the impact of congestion on data transmission by monitoring the network congestion status in real time and adjusting it according to the changing trend. Finally, queue management and priority scheduling algorithms are used to reasonably arrange the transmission order of data packets, reduce queuing delays, and improve the transmission efficiency of high-priority data packets. In terms of latency and throughput, as latency increases, throughput gradually decreases. Taking the bandwidth of 100Mbps as an example, when the network latency is 20ms, the throughput is 92.15Mbps, and when the latency is 100ms, the throughput drops to 74.11Mbps. The optimized data transmission algorithm proposed in this paper significantly improves the efficiency and stability of network transmission by dynamically adapting to network conditions. In future research, the application of this algorithm can be further expanded, and its adaptability and robustness in more complex network environments and high-load applications can be enhanced to improve the reliability of data transmission.

articleTitle: Effective Node Deployment in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are vital for applications like environmental monitoring and smart cities, but effective node deployment remains challenging. Traditional methods often fail in dynamic scenarios. This paper proposes a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based framework to optimize WSN node deployment, maximizing coverage while minimizing energy use and extending network lifetime. The RL model adapts to environmental changes and varying network conditions, ensuring robust performance in static, dynamic, and high-density environments. Experimental results show the RL approach outperforms conventional methods, achieving better coverage, lower energy consumption, and improved network longevity. The study demonstrates RL’s adaptability and effectiveness in addressing WSN deployment challenges, enabling intelligent, self-optimizing networks for dynamic real-world applications.

articleTitle: Optimized Approaches to Malware Detection: A Study of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Digital systems find it challenging to keep up with cybersecurity threats. The daily emergence of more than 560,000 new malware strains poses significant hazards to the digital ecosystem. The traditional malware detection methods fail to operate properly and yield high false positive rates with low accuracy of the protection system. This study explores the ways in which malware can be detected using these machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches to address those shortcomings. This study also includes a systematic comparison of the performance of some of the widely used ML models, such as random forest, multi-layer perceptron (MLP), and deep neural network (DNN), for determining the effectiveness of the domain of modern malware threat systems. We use a considerable-sized database from Kaggle, which has undergone optimized feature selection and preprocessing to improve model performance. Our finding suggests that the DNN model outperformed the other traditional models with the highest training accuracy of 99.92% and an almost perfect AUC score. Furthermore, the feature selection and preprocessing can help improve the capabilities of detection. This research makes an important contribution by analyzing the performance of the model on the performance metrics and providing insight into the effectiveness of the advanced detection techniques to build more robust and more reliable cybersecurity solutions against the growing malware threats.

articleTitle: Efficient Pathfinding in a Maze to overcome Challenges in Robotics and AI Using Breadth-First Search
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Efficient pathfinding in a maze is a key obstacle in robotics, computer science, and artificial intelligence. The article is proposing a strategy using the Breadth-First Search (BFS) algorithm to establish the shortest path for a robot navigating from the top-left to the bottom-right corner of a maze depicted as a two-dimensional grid. The maze comprises open pathways and obstructions, signified by 0 and 1, respectively. The robot's permissible actions include up, down, left, and right, restricted by the boundaries of the grid and the position of obstacles. BFS, an approach well-suited for unweighted graphs, sequentially examines all available routes, ensuring that the first observed path to the goal is the shortest. A visited set removes redundant cell visits, reducing infinite loops and inefficient processing. The algorithm's efficiency is dramatically upgraded by harnessing a queue structure to maintain live routes and their associated steps. This approach assures effectiveness and extensiveness for grid-based navigation problems, making it especially appropriate for real-world robotic applications where minimizing traversal cost is critical. Additionally, the paper discusses the algorithm's execution, complexities, and potential upgrades for larger grids or dynamic environments. Experimental results demonstrate BFS's resilience and efficacy in solving pathfinding challenges in various maze configurations. This work contributes to developing stable navigation techniques, integral to advancing autonomous robotic navigation and related fields.

articleTitle: Application and Research of Intelligent Speech Recognition Technology in Barrier-Free Human-Computer Interaction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low efficiency and insufficient recognition accuracy of disabled users in the existing barrier-free human-computer interaction system, intelligent speech recognition technology is introduced as an improvement tool to improve the interactive response speed and operation convenience of the system. First, based on the deep learning model combining Convolutional Neural Network ( CNN ) and Long Short-Term Memory Network ( LSTM), audio samples suited to barrier-free interaction scenarios are curated, and speech data with real scene interference such as environmental noise and background music are collected to construct a barrier-free dataset specific to speech recognition. Then, in the low layer, the convolutional neural network is used to capture low-level audio features such as spectrum images and time domain. In the high layer, the model inputs the feature vector output by the convolution layer into the long short-term memory network (LSTM) to capture the temporal dependency of speech and adapt to long instructions and complex sentences. The attention mechanism is introduced through the hidden layer to enhance the focus on key features. The features are classified and output through the fully connected layer to achieve efficient speech feature extraction and dynamic learning in complex environments. Finally, its applicability and stability are verified in actual barrier-free interaction devices in quiet, noisy and background music environments. After the introduction of intelligent speech recognition technology, in the background music environment, the recognition accuracy fluctuated slightly around the expected value of 94.8%, with the maximum value close to 95.5% and the minimum value about 93.9%. The application of intelligent speech recognition technology in barrier-free human-computer interaction has effectively improved the quality of interaction and ease of use, offering a novel pathway for advancing barrier-free technologies in the future.

articleTitle: Leveraging Next-Generation Business Intelligence for Proactive Cybersecurity Defense
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This paper explores how Business Intelligence operates better for protecting cybersecurity through its capability to merge predictive analytics methods with real-time data detection. A qualitative research design enables us to study how BI systems fit into present-day cybersecurity practices, specifically through predictive threat prevention alongside real-time database data. The evaluation process of BI tools leads organizations to select the most valuable system for detecting threats and minimizing risks. We introduce a data-oriented defense system that uses BI tools to implement proactive cybersecurity protection methods. The assessment focuses on implementing obstacles by understanding the main obstacles that stem from data privacy regulations, data overload, and worker skill gaps. The research establishes an orga- nized method which helps organizations use data analytics and automated threat identification to boost their security position through BI-based security tactics. The research shows that BI tools should be incorporated into cybersecurity approaches since they build robust security protocols and decrease vulnerability risks while fostering better resistance against modern security threats.

articleTitle: Improving Chronic Kidney Disease Detection Efficiency: Fine Tuned CatBoost and Nature-Inspired Algorithms with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a major global health issue which is affecting million people around the world and with increasing rate of mortality. Mitigation of progression of CKD and better patient outcomes requires early detection. Nevertheless, limitations lie in traditional diagnostic methods, especially in resource constrained settings. This study proposes an advanced machine learning approach to enhance CKD detection by evaluating four models: Random Forest (RF), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Logistic Regression (LR), and a fine-tuned CatBoost algorithm. Specifically, among these, the fine-tuned CatBoost model demonstrated the best overall performance having an accuracy of 98.75%, an AUC of 0.9993 and a Kappa score of 97.35% of the studies. The proposed CatBoost model has used a nature inspired algorithm such as Simulated Annealing to select the most important features, Cuckoo Search to adjust outliers and grid search to fine tune its settings in such a way to achieve improved prediction accuracy. Features significance is explained by SHAP-a well-known XAI technique-for gaining transparency in the decision-making process of proposed model and bring up trust in diagnostic systems. Using SHAP, the significant clinical features were identified as specific gravity, serum creatinine, albumin, hemoglobin, and diabetes mellitus. The potential of advanced machine learning techniques in CKD detection is shown in this research, particularly for low income and middle-income healthcare settings where prompt and correct diagnoses are vital. This study seeks to provide a highly accurate, interpretable, and efficient diagnostic tool to add to efforts for early intervention and improved healthcare outcomes for all CKD patients.

articleTitle: Predicting and Classifying Energy Usage Patterns Using Advanced Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of energy consumption trends is vital for effective energy management and achieving sustainability goals. In this research work explores the application of advanced machine learning models to predict and classify energy usage patterns, using a comprehensive dataset of energy-related variables. The preprocessing pipeline included the imputation of missing values, normalization, and advanced feature engineering through polynomial transformations. Models such as Linear Regression, Polynomial Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR), and an enhanced Random Forest model, (IRF) were trained and evaluated using key performance metrics: root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score. The results demonstrate that hyperparameter optimization significantly improved the performance of non-linear models. Among the tested algorithms, the Improved Random Forest (IRF) emerged as the most accurate and robust, outperforming other models in all evaluation metrics. The IRF's ability to capture complex feature interactions and handle non-linear dependencies in the data contributed to its superior predictive accuracy and reliability. Residual analysis and visualizations confirmed the robustness of the IRF, highlighting minimal prediction bias. This research work emphasizes the critical role of model selection and feature engineering in accurately modeling diverse energy consumption behaviors. The numerical findings provide actionable insights for energy optimization, resource allocation, and policy formulation, paving the way for a more sustainable and efficient energy future.

articleTitle: Advanced IoT and Machine Learning System for Real-Time Crop and Fertilizer Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML) technology has the capacity to transform agriculture via the improvement of precision agricultural methods. The proposed research work explores integration of IoT and ML in field of crop and fertilizer recommendation. Proposed system's primary goal is to develop predictive models for determining the appropriate crop and fertilizer types based on various environmental and soil features. Using ML techniques, this research work aims to recommend the best crop and fertilizer combinations to optimize agricultural yield and sustainability. The collected data of IoT sensors give immediate soil health information, while ML algorithms analyze this data to recommends the most suitable crops and suggests the appropriate fertilizers. This integration promises to enhance agricultural productivity and sustainability through data-oriented decision taking and resource efficient utilization. The proposed system has used four ML models as Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, CatBoost, and XGBoost for predictions by using precision, recall, accuracy and F1 score. The obtained results shows that best accuracy value among the models for recommending crop is 0.9909 and for recommending fertilizer is 0.9886.

articleTitle: A Novel Deep Learning Approach Utilizing HSV Color Space for Real-Time Early Fire
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: This study proposes a novel fire detection system aimed at improving fire prevention and control efforts, particularly addressing the growing threat posed by fires in urban settings and the alarming frequency of wildfires. Early detection of fire plays a critical role in safeguarding lives and property in places such as shopping malls, offices, factories, and educational institutions. Existing systems for detecting fires, which rely mainly on alarm-based mechanisms, have limitations in their responsiveness. In this project, we developed a machine learning-based fire detection system using computer vision techniques. The proposed model integrates a webcam as part of the surveillance setup to continuously monitor indoor environments. By leveraging video feeds, the system processes the input using machine learning algorithms and the Hue, Saturation, Value (HSV) color space to detect fire at an early stage. OpenCV is employed to handle real-time video processing, ensuring prompt fire detection and timely alerts. This approach demonstrates a significant advancement over traditional systems, offering real-time detection capabilities through the combination of deep learning and advanced color space techniques.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Sentiment Analysis for Enhancing Customer Experience in Phygital Retail Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: In today’s world customer shopping experience seamlessly blend physical and digital spaces. In understanding customer attitudes in this blended environment, sentiment analysis acts as a crucial tool. The advanced deep learning techniques are necessary to capture the complexity of customer’s emotion in Phygital retail since the traditional methods fail to do. This study aims to analyse the effectiveness of CNN, LSTM, GRU and BiLSTM in sentiment analysis within Phygital retail environments. The findings reveal that CNN achieves the highest accuracy score at 96.03%. Business can enhance customer satisfaction, streamline operations and maintain competitive edge by leveraging these deep learning techniques in Phygital Retail.

articleTitle: A Hardware Trojan Detection using Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Hardware Trojan is a major vulnerability in the security of the system. Various researchers have worked on the hardware Trojan detection and prevention techniques as solutions that are based on traditional methods such as side-channel analysis, logic testing, and IC fingerprinting. These methods focus on detecting anomalies in the system's behavior or physical characteristics. In this paper, we are giving insights of hardware trojan detection and prevention along with experimental study using several machine learning techniques. We used an open-source circuit dataset for the design phase known as Gate Level Netlist (GLN) that is available on the trust-hub data repository. In experiments we found that Hierarchical Machine learning Methods such as decision tree and random forest classified the hardware trojan infected and non-infected chips with 98-99% accuracy

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques for Intrusion Detection Systems in Healthcare Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Nowadays, healthcare systems face ever-increasing cyber security threats due to the sensitive nature of patient data and the proliferation of IoT-enabled medical devices. Traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) struggle to adapt to healthcare environments' dynamic and heterogeneous data. Deep learning techniques, with their ability to analyze complex and high-dimensional data, have emerged as a promising approach to enhancing IDS performance. This paper explores the application of deep learning methods for intrusion detection in healthcare, focusing on their advantages, challenges, and practical implementations. Topics include neural network architectures, feature engineering for medical and network data, and real-time intrusion detection in resource-constrained environments. The goal is to provide a roadmap for leveraging deep learning to ensure robust and scalable security for healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Classification of Cardiovascular Diseases through Retinal Fundus Images using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is one of the most significant global health concerns, necessitating early detection for effective treatment. Traditional diagnostic tools such as electrocardiograms (ECG), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), blood tests, and coronary angiography are commonly used but are often invasive, costly, and inaccessible in resource-constrained settings. To overcome these challenges, this study employs a unique dataset of retinal fundus images to propose a novel, non-invasive, and economical approach for classifying CVD risk using deep learning techniques. Convolutional Neural Networks have demonstrated exceptional promise in recognizing disease abnormalities in the optic nerve and retinal vasculature. This study explores the advancements in CVD risk prediction and demonstrates the efficacy of retinal fundus imaging as a diagnostic tool. By automatically identifying detailed retinal features such as vasculature, microaneurysms, hemorrhages, exudates, and the optic disc, deep learning models offer superior efficiency when compared to traditional approaches, supporting early risk prediction and timely intervention.

articleTitle: Real Time Analysis of Twin Image Style Transfer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Research in image styling has focused on developing techniques that allow the transfer of artistic styles to a content image, enhancing the flexibility and richness of visual representation. This research proposes a novel method that combines two distinct styles onto a single content image, in contrast to traditional strategies that usually employ a single style image. To combine two different styles, the VGG-19 model is used to extract features and create Gram Matrices. The final outcome may be fine-tuned using this method’s wide control over the blending ratio. According to the experimental data, the loss of style and content decreases significantly as the number of epochs increases. Additionally, the suggested method is quantitatively validated with a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 28.6 dB, which suggests minimal distortion in the generated images, a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 0.92, which indicates strong structural preservation, and a Frechet Inception Distance (FID) of 45.3, which indicates high visual similarity.

articleTitle: Analysis of Global Trends in Communication Encryption Development Based on Bibliometrics
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 14th International Conference on Communication Systems and Network Technologies (CSNT)
abstract: Communication encryption provides significant assurance for information transmission.
